Google Chrome
Honey
Honey has now lost 4 million Chrome users after shady tactics were revealed
Ben Schoon
| Mar 31 2025 - 7:20 am PT
1 Comment
Late last year the popular Chrome extension Honey (owned by PayPal) was revealed for employing a few shady tactics, and the extension has since lost around 4 million users on Google’s browser alone.
To recap the situation thus far, Honey has amassed millions of users over the past several years on the promise of finding coupon codes for various online stores. The free extension saw wide advertisements and was eventually
purchased by PayPal in 2020
for $4 billion.
In December 2024,
a video on YouTube
by the channel
MegaLag
exposed Honey for two shady practices. The first was how the extension took advantage of affiliate codes. Honey has always used affiliate programs to subsidize its service, but the video revealed that the extension would hijack these programs – removing affiliate codes from other refferers such as online creators and website – even if it didn’t have coupon codes or cash back to offer in return. The practice was working behind the scenes with businesses to control which codes would appear to Honey users, effectively directly lying about its promise of finding the “best” coupon codes on the web.
That video amassed over 17 million views, and Honey has now lost over 4 million users on Chrome.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
As
we reported in early January,
Honey had lost around 3 million users immediately after the video went viral, but ended up
gaining back
around 1 million later on. Now, as of March 2025, Honey is down to 16 million users
on Chrome
, down from its peak of 20 million.
This drop comes
after new Chrome policy has taken effect which prevents
Honey, and extensions like it, from practices including taking over affiliate codes without disclosure or without benefit to the extension’s users. Honey has since
updated its extension listing with disclosure
, and
we found that the behavior shown in the December video no longer occurs
.
Are you still using Honey?

data.title: JEP draft: Prepare to make final mean final
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在未来Java版本中对通过深度反射修改`final`字段的行为发出警告，并准备在默认情况下限制这种修改，以增强Java程序的安全性和性能。主要目标包括：为Java生态系统做好准备，在默认情况下禁止通过深度反射修改`final`字段，使其与记录类组件保持一致；同时允许序列化库在必要时继续对`final`字段进行修改。文章还解释了当前Java平台通过深度反射允许修改`final`字段所带来的问题，包括对正确性和性能优化的影响。最终目标是通过实施“默认完整性”策略，确保代码和JVM能够信任`final`字段的不可变性。非目标包括不弃用或移除任何Java平台API，也不阻止序列化库在反序列化过程中修改`final`字段。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java中关于`final`字段的可变性及相关优化的讨论

不同观点：
• cogman10：支持为类添加注解（如`@FinalMutatableByReflection`），以便在需要时允许通过反射改变`final`字段，同时在其他地方保持`final`的不可变性。这样可以在序列化等场景中灵活处理，而不影响其他代码的不可变性。
• elric：虽然经常使用反射操作私有字段，但从未改变过`final`字段，认为这种演变是有益的。
• exabrial：支持这种变化，并认为主流框架（如JsonB、JAXB）早已建议避免愚蠢的操作。对这种变化可能破坏一些序列化库表示关注，但相信开发者能适应。
• theanonymousone：对能够在Java 17后仍能改变`final`字段感到惊讶，原以为这种能力已被限制。
• nightpool：质疑是否需要如此复杂的机制来支持未来计划中的优化，特别是涉及跨应用运行的不可变性。对这种优化的实际需求和形式表示困惑。
• bironran：担心这种变化会导致许多应用需要添加额外的命令行参数（如`--add-opens`）以支持常用库，最终可能无法真正实现预期的优化效果。
• magicalhippo：非Java开发者，最初以为与标记为`final`的类有关，认为提案在精神上是合理的。
• GauntletWizard：分享了一个在Facebook工作时的案例，说明实际工程中对`final`的滥用情况，认为这种做法虽然有效，但工程上不妥。
• jjmarr：作为C++开发者，提到类似`const_cast`的问题，赞赏Java愿意打破常规以改进语言。
• TOGoS：质疑为什么需要标记为`final`却要允许改变，认为如果需要改变，就不应标记为`final`。批评一些框架滥用反射打破规则。
• aardvark179：对这一变化表示欢迎。
• mberning：担心这种变化会导致需要大量JVM参数来支持遗留应用，类似包可见性变化的情况。
• stickfigure：希望`final`成为所有字段、变量和参数的默认值，以减少可变性（虽然知道这会破坏现有语法）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应该允许通过反射改变`final`字段，以及这种变化对现有库和框架的影响。
• 一些开发者支持这种变化，认为可以提高性能和代码的明确性，而另一些开发者则担心这种变化带来的复杂性和对遗留系统的冲击。
• 对未来优化的实际需求和效果存在疑问，特别是涉及跨应用运行的不可变性优化。
• 工程实践中对`final`的滥用案例引发了对工程文化和框架设计的深入思考。

JEP draft: Prepare to Make Final Mean Final
Author
Ron Pressler & Alex Buckley
Owner
Ron Pressler
Type
Feature
Scope
JDK
Status
Draft
Component
core-libs
Discussion
jdk dash dev at openjdk dot org
Reviewed by
Alan Bateman
Created
2025/02/06 10:25
Updated
2025/03/31 17:35
Issue
8349536
Summary
Issue warnings about uses of
deep reflection
to mutate
final
fields. The warnings aim to prepare developers for a future release that ensures
integrity by default
by restricting
final
field mutation; this makes Java programs safer and potentially faster. Application developers can avoid both current warnings and future restrictions by selectively enabling the ability to mutate
final
fields where essential.
Goals
Prepare the Java ecosystem for a future release that, by default, disallows the mutation of
final
fields by deep reflection. As of that release, application developers will have to explicitly enable the capability to do so at startup.
Align
final
fields in normal classes with the components of record classes, which cannot be mutated by deep reflection.
Allow serialization libraries to continue working with
Serializable
classes, even those with
final
fields.
Non-Goals
It is not a goal to deprecate or remove any part of the Java Platform API.
It is not a goal to prevent the mutation of
final
fields by serialization libraries during deserialization.
Motivation
Java developers rely on
final
fields to represent immutable state. Once assigned in a constructor (for
final
instance fields) or in a class initializer (for
static final
fields), a
final
field cannot be reassigned; its value, whether a primitive value or a reference to an object, is immutable. The expectation that a
final
field cannot be reassigned in far-flung parts of the program, whether deliberately or accidentally, is often crucial when developers reason about correctness. Furthermore, many classes exist
only
to represent immutable state, so
records
were introduced in JDK 16 to provide a concise way to declare a class where all fields are
final
, making it easy to reason about correctness.
The expectation that a
final
field cannot be reassigned is also important for performance. The more the JVM knows about the behavior of a class, the more optimizations it can apply. For example, being able to trust that
final
fields are never reassigned makes it possible for the JVM to perform
constant folding
, an optimization that elides the need to load a value from memory since the value can instead be embedded in the machine code emitted by the JIT compiler. Constant folding is often the first step in a chain of optimizations that together provide a massive speed-up.
Unfortunately, the expectation that a
final
field cannot be reassigned is
false
. The Java Platform provides
a number of APIs
that allow
final
fields to be reassigned at any time by any code in the program, undermining all reasoning about correctness and invalidating important optimizations. The most prevalent of these APIs is
deep reflection
. Here is an example that uses deep reflection to mutate a
final
field at will:
class C {
final int x;
C() { x = 100; }
}
// Perform deep reflection over C's final field
java.lang.reflect.Field f = C.class.getDeclaredField("x");
f.setAccessible(true);
// Create an object of class C
C obj = new C();
System.out.println(obj.x);  // Prints 100
// Mutate the final field in the object
f.set(obj, 200);
System.out.println(obj.x);  // Prints 200
f.set(obj, 300);
System.out.println(obj.x);  // Prints 300
Accordingly, a
final
field is as mutable as a non-
final
field. Developers are unable to use
final
fields to construct the deeply immutable graphs of objects that would enable the JVM to deliver the best performance optimizations.
It might seem absurd for the Java Platform to provide an API that undermines the meaning of
final
. However, after JDK 5 introduced the
Java Memory Model
that led to widespread use of
final
fields
, such an API was deemed necessary to support serialization libraries. In retrospect, offering such unconstrained functionality was a poor choice because it sacrificed integrity. When we introduced
hidden classes
in JDK 15 and
record classes
in JDK 16, we constrained deep reflection to
disallow mutation of
final
fields in hidden and record classes
.
We constrained deep reflection further when we
strongly encapsulated JDK internals
in JDK 17. In JDK 24,
we started a process
to remove methods in
sun.misc.Unsafe
that, like deep reflection, allow mutation of
final
fields.
Relatively little code mutates
final
fields, but the mere existence of APIs for doing so makes it impossible for developers or the JVM to trust the value of
any
final
field. This compromises safety and performance in
all
programs. In line with the policy of
integrity by default
, we plan to enforce the immutability of
final
fields so that code cannot use deep reflection to reassign them at will. We will support one special case -- serialization libraries that need to mutate
final
fields d
43538919.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了在未来Java版本中对通过深度反射修改`final`字段的行为发出警告，并准备在默认情况下限制这种修改，以增强Java程序的安全性和性能。主要目标包括：为Java生态系统做好准备，在默认情况下禁止通过深度反射修改`final`字段，使其与记录类组件保持一致；同时允许序列化库在必要时继续对`final`字段进行修改。文章还解释了当前Java平台通过深度反射允许修改`final`字段所带来的问题，包括对正确性和性能优化的影响。最终目标是通过实施“默认完整性”策略，确保代码和JVM能够信任`final`字段的不可变性。非目标包括不弃用或移除任何Java平台API，也不阻止序列化库在反序列化过程中修改`final`字段。
43538919.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java中关于`final`字段的可变性及相关优化的讨论

不同观点：
• cogman10：支持为类添加注解（如`@FinalMutatableByReflection`），以便在需要时允许通过反射改变`final`字段，同时在其他地方保持`final`的不可变性。这样可以在序列化等场景中灵活处理，而不影响其他代码的不可变性。
• elric：虽然经常使用反射操作私有字段，但从未改变过`final`字段，认为这种演变是有益的。
• exabrial：支持这种变化，并认为主流框架（如JsonB、JAXB）早已建议避免愚蠢的操作。对这种变化可能破坏一些序列化库表示关注，但相信开发者能适应。
• theanonymousone：对能够在Java 17后仍能改变`final`字段感到惊讶，原以为这种能力已被限制。
• nightpool：质疑是否需要如此复杂的机制来支持未来计划中的优化，特别是涉及跨应用运行的不可变性。对这种优化的实际需求和形式表示困惑。
• bironran：担心这种变化会导致许多应用需要添加额外的命令行参数（如`--add-opens`）以支持常用库，最终可能无法真正实现预期的优化效果。
• magicalhippo：非Java开发者，最初以为与标记为`final`的类有关，认为提案在精神上是合理的。
• GauntletWizard：分享了一个在Facebook工作时的案例，说明实际工程中对`final`的滥用情况，认为这种做法虽然有效，但工程上不妥。
• jjmarr：作为C++开发者，提到类似`const_cast`的问题，赞赏Java愿意打破常规以改进语言。
• TOGoS：质疑为什么需要标记为`final`却要允许改变，认为如果需要改变，就不应标记为`final`。批评一些框架滥用反射打破规则。
• aardvark179：对这一变化表示欢迎。
• mberning：担心这种变化会导致需要大量JVM参数来支持遗留应用，类似包可见性变化的情况。
• stickfigure：希望`final`成为所有字段、变量和参数的默认值，以减少可变性（虽然知道这会破坏现有语法）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应该允许通过反射改变`final`字段，以及这种变化对现有库和框架的影响。
• 一些开发者支持这种变化，认为可以提高性能和代码的明确性，而另一些开发者则担心这种变化带来的复杂性和对遗留系统的冲击。
• 对未来优化的实际需求和效果存在疑问，特别是涉及跨应用运行的不可变性优化。
• 工程实践中对`final`的滥用案例引发了对工程文化和框架设计的深入思考。

data.title: Show HN: I made a little puzzle game about a rogue chess knight
data.author: freetonik
data.article_summary: 《Knight Ride》是一款棋类游戏，目标是到达终点获胜。玩家可以通过捕获棋子获得积分和额外移动机会。关卡得分计算方式为积分乘以剩余移动次数，还要小心敌方攻击。游戏显示最高得分、当前得分、剩余移动次数和总分。每关完成后，根据剩余移动和是否清空棋盘计算关卡得分。如果移动次数用完，游戏结束，显示最终得分和最高得分，并提供重新开始选项。游戏由Rakhim D.制作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款基于骑士移动的棋类游戏的玩法、规则解释、改进建议及技术问题

不同观点：
• BrenBarn认为游戏有趣，但提出了一些改进建议，如增加关卡选择功能、当前关卡重启功能以及更详细的得分说明。
• Dylan604分享了与游戏类似的个人经历，认为该游戏适合用于儿童国际象棋俱乐部的教学，无需实现人机对战。
• Gjm11指出游戏规则说明不够清晰，提供了详细的改进建议，包括得分和奖励机制的解释，以及如何优化规则说明的呈现方式。
• Parsimo2010欣赏游戏的多样化玩法，认为游戏对不同层次的玩家都有吸引力，无论是认真追求高分的玩家还是休闲玩家。
• Eric_WVGG提到这款游戏与Alexei Pajitnov的另一款游戏《Knight Move》有相似之处，将游戏置于历史背景中。

补充讨论：
• Nomilk建议在被攻击时失去更多，例如直接失败并重启关卡，而不是仅仅扣分，并认为增加惩罚机制会增加游戏难度。
• Lerc强调了在手机上的游戏体验，建议显示最佳可能得分，并提出对进入危险区域施加更严厉惩罚的建议。
• Sionisrecur认为如果无法移动到被攻击的位置会增加游戏的趣味和挑战性，并指出规则解释不足的问题。
• Yubiox询问关卡是手动设计还是自动生成，并对游戏的趣味性给予肯定。
• Freetonik提供了关于游戏制作的博客链接，为玩家提供了更多背景信息。
• Bobbiechen赞赏游戏的同时，报告了一个潜在的bug，即在Android的Firefox浏览器上可以无限刷分。
• Rco8786简单表示游戏有趣，但花了些时间才弄明白规则。
• Berbec希望游戏能保存进度，而不是每次都重新开始。
• Snarf21询问是否有帮助屏幕或规则触发方式，显示出对规则说明的需求。

争议焦点：
- 游戏规则的清晰度及说明方式是讨论的焦点，部分玩家如Gjm11和Sionisrecur认为需要更详细的解释和提示。
- 惩罚机制的严厉程度存在不同看法，Nomilk和Lerc建议增加更严厉的惩罚以提升游戏挑战性，而Parsimo2010则认为现有机制适合不同层次的玩家。

总的来说，玩家们普遍赞赏游戏的趣味性和设计，但对规则说明、惩罚机制及关卡选择等方面提出了改进建议。

data.title: Kagi for Kids
data.author: ryanjamurphy
data.article_summary: Kagi的Family Plan旨在为家庭和孩子提供更安全、无广告的搜索体验。该计划强调学习而非消费，尊重家庭隐私，并提供多种功能如家长控制、快速答案和个性化搜索结果。家长可以通过“Lenses”功能限制孩子访问的网站，并可屏蔽或推荐多达1000个网站。此外，Kagi提供简单易用的界面和新的插图，甚至包括一个有趣的“便便头像”，以帮助孩子学习身份、隐私和在线安全。家长可以通过邮件邀请家庭成员，孩子只需用户名即可登录，确保浏览安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对儿童网络内容过滤和安全浏览的解决方案

不同观点：
• Roritharr：对YouTube Kids当前的过滤效果不满意，由于孩子通过Minecraft Influencer接触到宗教内容，他使用Pi-Hole屏蔽了YouTube。他希望有一种工具可以根据自然语言规则筛选出有价值的视频，但目前没有这样的解决方案。
• viraptor：对过滤有害内容的难度表示理解，认为目前的搜索过滤可能是当前最好的解决方案，但对其实际效果持保留态度。
• kylehotchkiss：建议不仅要屏蔽YouTube，还可以考虑屏蔽CNN、Fox、Facebook和TikTok等内容，以避免有害信息。
• jmathai：虽然尚未使用Kagi的服务，但对类似技术公司表示期待。同时，对NextDNS的效果表示满意，但承认孩子并不喜欢。
• facile3232：认为内容过滤需要围绕父母的价值体系进行策划，对完全依赖软件过滤的效果持悲观态度。
• dcchambers：作为Kagi的付费用户，对Kagi在儿童内容过滤方面的努力表示赞赏，并认为当前的YouTube Kids等平台效果不佳。
• yzydserd：质疑Kagi关于家庭计划的描述，指出其提供的计划信息不够清晰。
• philips：支持Kagi的基本理念，但希望过滤过程更加社交化，可以与朋友和学校共享和协作，并提出多种实际的儿童内容管理工具和方法。
• an_aparallel：认为互联网的多样性和未知性曾是其魅力所在，对过度过滤和控制表示不满。
• ilrwbwrkhv：非常期待Kagi能为儿童提供安全可靠的搜索服务，但对搜索结果中是否会包含不良网站表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体工具和方法包括Pi-Hole、NextDNS、Jellyfin、Calibre等，展示了当前父母在管理儿童网络内容方面的多样化需求和实践。
• 对Kagi家庭计划的具体内容和描述存在疑问，用户对计划的清晰度和实用性有不同看法。
• 对完全依赖软件过滤的有效性存在争议，部分用户认为父母和教育者的直接参与和管理不可或缺。
• 对互联网的自由和控制之间的平衡有不同看法，部分用户怀念过去互联网的“野性”，对过度控制表示担忧。

Family Plan
â
Since the inception, Kagi has been driven by the idea of humanizing the web, especially for families and kids. Our commitment to this cause was the inspiration behind the creation of Kagi. Many of our staff are parents working together to build a better search and web future for our children. We strive to provide a search engine that prioritizes the well-being of your loved ones, particularly the most vulnerable ones like children, by offering an ad-free and safe browsing experience. We offer two different group plans based on your specific needs.
The Kagi Family Plan is perfect for families wanting to search smarter, emphasizing learning over consumption while respecting your family's privacy. With a simple, affordable pricing model and powerful features, the Kagi Family Plan makes it easy to get the most out of Kagi Search as a family.
Table of Contents
How to Use the Kagi Family Plan

Unique Features
Kid-Friendly Search Experience

Story behind the Poop Avatar
How to Use the Kagi Family Plan
â
To sign up for the Family Plan, select the plan that fits your family's size and needs at Kagi
account creation
.
If you have an existing Kagi account and want to upgrade to the Family plan, everything you need to do is cancel your existing plan, and then resubscribe to the Family plan (any credit left over will be pro-rated).
Adding family members is easy, you can
invite them via email
through Kagi. For kids, you can use a username, and an adult will help them log in by getting a verification email.
The
Family Plan dashboard
gives you a complete picture of your family's members
The
Billing screen
has the overview of the plan and allows you to update payment info or cancel the subscription.
Logging in for Kids
â
To log-in kid accounts, just proceed to normal login on their device. Kids enter just their username and password is not needed.
A verification email will be sent to the account owner. They can just click the link in the email to automatically log in the kid account, or enter the provided numerical code.
Unique Features
â
The Kagi Family Plan has unique features that make it perfect for families.
Kid-Friendly Search Experience
â
The Kagi Family Plan also includes a kid-friendly search experience that uses strict content filters to ensure children are not exposed to harmful content. Kidâs profile simplifies the search experience with larger text, icons, and content adjusted for kids.
Parental Controls
â
The Kagi Family Plan comes with parental controls that let parents manage their children's search experience.
Kagi allows parents to toggle whether kids will have access to the search results on the entire web or a restricted set of sites (whitelist) only through âlenses.â
Safe search filters exclude adult material from the search results.
Quick Answers
â
We are featuring state of the art AI tools that can improve the quality of consumed information for kids. AI tools can be beneficial for getting quick answers to common questions, but it's important to remember that they're not always accurate. We encourage you to talk with kids about the potential risks and benefits of AI question-answering tools. It's important for kids to understand how these tools work and how to use them safely and responsibly in a way to nurture curiosity.
We added appropriate warnings for AI tools around the interface and a particular content-moderation filter to ensure AI output does not contain harmful content.
Lenses
â
Lenses are a subset of search results that are restricted to a subset of whitelisted sites (up to 10 per lens). You can create and share multiple lenses, such as having a lens for Education, School work, or Entertainment and assign the default one to be used for searches. We allow you to export and import lenses to share with other community parents.
Parents can create lenses for children to ensure they have access to the resources they need while keeping them safe from inappropriate content.
Personalized Results
â
In addition to lenses, we include the ability for parents to completely block (ban) websites from showing in the results, or to promote useful sites. Up to 1,000 websites can be curated in this way.
New Illustrations
â
Our mascot Doggo now has a lady friend, and we introduced several new and delightful illustrations throughout the interface.
Story behind the Poop Avatar
â
Our selection of avatars for kids includes a poop avatar (which most kids find really funny), and there's a reason why we made this choice that goes deeper than what meets the eye.

data.title: LLM Workflows then Agents: Getting Started with Apache Airflow
data.author: alittletooraph2
data.article_summary: `airflow-ai-sdk` 是一个用于在 Apache Airflow 中操作大型语言模型（LLM）和 AI 代理的 SDK，基于 Pydantic AI。它允许用户直接在 Airflow 管道中调用 LLM 并编排代理任务，使用基于装饰器的任务语法，如 `@task.llm`、`@task.llm_branch` 和 `@task.agent`。SDK 提供自动输出解析、分支控制等功能，支持多种 LLM 模型（如 OpenAI、Anthropic 等）。通过该 SDK，用户可以轻松将 LLM 工作流集成到 Airflow 管道中，从简单的 LLM 调用到复杂的代理工作流均可实现。示例代码和安装说明详见 GitHub 仓库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于工作流引擎和AI代理的讨论，包括对不同工具和设计模式的看法。

不同观点：
• [jumski] 认为 pgflow 是一个简单、以 Postgres 为主的引擎，使用任务队列来执行实际工作，具有明确的DAG方法、强类型安全、良好的TypeScript DSL，并能够在 Supabase 上运行而不需要任何外部工具。他对即将发布的 alpha 版本感到兴奋，并邀请其他人关注其项目。

• [mushufasa] 认为 Airflow 对于新项目来说已经过时，但目前没有一个明确的替代者。他提到了多个框架（如 Prefect、Dagster、Temporal 等），并表示选择过多让人感到不知所措。他建议一篇技术博客对不同设计模式和如何整合LLM特性进行分析会很有帮助。

• [greatgib] 对使用装饰器的示例提出质疑，认为装饰器在实际应用中并没有太大作用，反而会使参数化和从配置中获取值变得困难，认为这是不好的实践。

• [drdaeman] 对 `@task.agent` 装饰器的必要性提出疑问，认为与直接使用 `return my_agent.run_sync(...)` 相比，装饰器显得更具限制性和可能不够直观。

• [itsallrelative] 对“代理”在工作流中的必要性持怀疑态度，认为在许多情况下，仅通过少量LLM增强的确定性工作流已经足够。

• [datadrivenangel] 正在探索在SQL触发器中使用LLM调用以实现代理/代理工作流，认为LLM驱动的工作流可以带来强大的结果。

• [falcor84] 提出反向思考，询问是否有人尝试过由AI代理定义和迭代长期运行的工作流。

• [nikolayasdf123] 简单地表示 Airflow 是一个合适的选择。

• [ldjkfkdsjnv] 对现有工具解决代理工作流的能力持悲观态度，认为只有 Temporal 有可能成功，因为 Airflow 等工具并非为高度动态执行设计。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到 Airflow 的局限性和替代工具的选择问题，尤其是针对代理和工作流自动化的需求。
• 有人对装饰器的实用性提出质疑，认为在某些情况下，装饰器可能不是最佳设计选择。
• 对LLM在工作流中的应用和潜力存在不同看法，有人认为增强的确定性工作流已经足够，而有人则在探索更复杂的代理工作流。

争议焦点：
• 现有工具（如 Airflow）是否适合用于新的代理工作流项目，以及是否需要新的设计模式和技术博客来指导选择。
• 装饰器的实际效用和其在代码中的合理性。
• LLM 在工作流中应扮演的角色和其应用潜力。

airflow-ai-sdk
This repository contains an SDK for working with LLMs from Apache Airflow, based on
Pydantic AI
. It allows users to call LLMs and orchestrate agent calls directly within their Airflow pipelines using decorator-based tasks. The SDK leverages the familiar Airflow
@task
syntax with extensions like
@task.llm
,
@task.llm_branch
, and
@task.agent
.
To get started, check out the
examples repository here
, which offers a full local Airflow instance with the AI SDK installed and 5 example pipelines. If you already have Airflow running, you can also install the package with any optional dependencies you need:
pip install airflow-ai-sdk[openai,duckduckgo]
Note that installing the package with no optional dependencies will install the slim version of the package, which does not include any LLM models or tools. The available optional packages are listed
here
. While this SDK offers the optional dependencies for convenience sake, you can also install the optional dependencies from
Pydantic AI
directly.
Table of Contents:
Features
Motivation
Examples
LLM calls from a DAG (summarize Airflow's commits)
LLM calls with structured outputs using
@task.llm
(user feedback -> sentiment and feature requests)
Agent calls with
@task.agent
(deep research agent)
Changing dag control flow with
@task.llm_branch
(support ticket routing)
Future Work
Features
LLM tasks with
@task.llm
:
Define tasks that call language models (e.g. GPT-3.5-turbo) to process text.
Agent tasks with
@task.agent
:
Orchestrate multi-step AI reasoning by leveraging custom tools.
Automatic output parsing:
Use function type hints (including Pydantic models) to automatically parse and validate LLM outputs.
Branching with
@task.llm_branch
:
Change the control flow of a DAG based on the output of an LLM.
Model support:
Support for
all models in the Pydantic AI library
(OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, Groq, Mistral, Cohere, Bedrock)
Design Principles
We follow the taskflow pattern of Airflow with three decorators:
@task.llm
: Define a task that calls an LLM. Under the hood, this creates a Pydantic AI
Agent
with no tools.
@task.agent
: Define a task that calls an agent. You can pass in a Pydantic AI
Agent
directly.
@task.llm_branch
: Define a task that branches the control flow of a DAG based on the output of an LLM. Enforces that the LLM output is one of the downstream task_ids.
The function supplied to each decorator is a translation function that converts the Airflow task's input into the LLM's input. If you don't want to do any translation, you
can just return the input unchanged.
Motivation
AI workflows are becoming increasingly common as organizations look for pragmatic ways to get value out of LLMs. As with
any workflow, it's important to have a flexible and scalable way to orchestrate them.
Airflow is a popular choice for orchestrating data pipelines. It's a powerful tool for managing the dependencies
between tasks and for scheduling and monitoring them, and has been trusted by data teams everywhere for 10+ years. It comes "batteries included" with a rich set of capabilities:
Flexible scheduling:
run tasks on a fixed schedule, on-demand, or based on external events
Dynamic task mapping:
easily process multiple inputs in parallel with full error handling and observability
Branching and conditional logic:
change the control flow of a DAG based on the output of certain tasks
Error handling:
built-in support for retries, exponential backoff, and timeouts
Resource management:
limit the concurrency of tasks with Airflow Pools
Monitoring:
detailed logs and monitoring capabilities
Scalability:
designed for production workflows
This SDK is designed to make it easy to integrate LLM workflows into your Airflow pipelines. It allows you to do anything from simple LLM calls to complex agentic workflows.
Examples
See the full set of examples in the
examples/dags
directory.
LLM calls from a DAG (summarize Airflow's commits)
This example shows how to use the
@task.llm
decorator as part of an Airflow DAG. In the
@task.llm
decorator, we can
specify a model and system prompt. The decorator allows you to transform the Airflow task's input into the LLM's input.
See full example:

data.title: The Surprising History of Scientific Ballooning in 11 Missions
data.author: dnetesn
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了科学气球在人类探索宇宙和大气层过程中的重要作用，以及历史上一些关键的气球任务。NASA去年在南极放飞了一个携带5000磅望远镜的大型气球（GUSTO），旨在帮助天文学家了解宇宙中的恒星形成。文章回顾了自1783年以来的一些重要气球任务，如1783年法国蒙戈尔菲耶兄弟的首次动物气球实验，1804年盖-吕萨克的高空气体研究，1898年泰塞朗·德·博尔对平流层的发现，1912年维克多·赫斯对宇宙射线的发现等。此外，文章还介绍了1931年皮卡尔德设计的加压舱气球，1947年后的塑料气球时代，以及1960年NASA的“卫星气球”项目。这些任务展示了气球在科学探索中的独特价值和贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Joseph Kittinger在科学气球和极限跳伞历史中的地位和贡献的讨论。

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：MrMcCall认为文章遗漏了Joseph Kittinger是一个失误。他强调Kittinger在科学气球历史中的重要性，尤其是其在102,000英尺高空跳伞、成为第一个完全目睹地球曲率的人，并认为这是极具历史意义的成就。
• 第二种观点：有人可能认为Kittinger的记录已经被Red Bull赞助的跳伞者打破，因此其历史地位不再那么重要。然而，MrMcCall似乎认为Kittinger的成就依然具有特殊价值，尤其是他在飞行服破损情况下仍坚持跳伞的勇气和专业精神。

补充讨论：
• Kittinger的跳伞视频和纪录片具有很高的观赏价值，展示了其个性和冒险精神，比如他在降落后做出手势和吸烟的场景。
• Kittinger跳伞过程中的物理体验，尤其是其在太空中无法感知速度的描述，增加了这一历史事件的技术和科学讨论维度。
• 争议的焦点可能在于Kittinger成就的现代意义，尤其是在他的记录被打破后，其历史贡献应如何被评价。

ast year, NASA lofted a massive balloon over Antarctica, carrying beneath it a 5,000-pound telescope. Known as GUSTO, it will help astronomers understand the story of star formation in the universe.

A
lofted balloon
might seem rather a low-tech approach to enable front-line cosmological discoveries in an era when rockets are now ripping into space with such regularity. But scientists have been working for nearly 250 years to perfect the art of scientific ballooning. From the first samples of the Earth’s high troposphere—gathered in a glass bottle—to new hints about the shape of the universe, balloons have played a surprisingly
important role
in our understanding of our own planet and the universe beyond. Here are 11 of the most fascinating balloon missions across history.
1783:
In late 1700s France, the Montgolfier brothers sent the first passengers into the skies in a balloon: At the court of King Louis XVI at Versailles, they loaded a sheep, duck, and chicken into a round wicker basket tied to a hydrogen-filled balloon by a rope. As onlookers applauded in awe, the balloon lifted off the ground and soared into the air—only to descend into nearby woods 10 minutes later. (The animals survived the flight.)
Just two months later, human passengers boarded a basket attached to a spherical balloon, which toured the heavens for 25 minutes. A
new era
of science had commenced: Human aeronauts began using balloons to study the atmosphere.

During a crash landing, he and his assistant wore helmets fashioned from wicker chicken baskets.
1804:
French chemist Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac flew a balloon up to 23,000 feet to
study
how gases react to different environments. He
carried
a thermometer, a barometer, and a hygrometer with him. High in the atmosphere, he filled an evacuated glass bottle—the air had been removed from inside to create a vacuum—with an air sample and found that it had the same chemical composition as air on the ground.
1898:
French meteorologist Léon Teisserenc de Bort wanted to know how air temperatures vary at different elevations from the Earth, so he loaded an unpiloted balloon made of paper and silk with temperature-reading devices and
dispatched
it into the atmosphere. He found that temperatures dropped as the balloon rose, but above 26,000 feet, the temperature held steady. In 1902, he proposed a name for this upper layer of the atmosphere: the stratosphere. (We now know that temperature changes are inverted in the stratosphere and actually
increase
with height to a certain altitude.)
1912:
In a single year, Austrian physicist
Victor F. Hess made seven
different
voyages in a hydrogen balloon. On his seventh, he
ascended
above the Bohemian town of Aussig to more than 15,000 feet, where he was surprised to find that, according to his carefully calibrated electroscope, ionization of the atmosphere did not fall as he rose. Instead, it was nearly three times higher up there than it was on the ground. These observations led to the
discovery
of cosmic rays, for which he received a Nobel Prize in 1936.

IT’S A BIRD!:
This communication satellite-balloon combo, nicknamed a satelloon, first launched in 1960. Here, it’s seen fully inflated, with workers nearby for scale. The satelloon was so large it could be seen with the naked eye from the ground as it passed 120,000 feet overhead.
Photo by NASA / Goddard Space Flight Center.
1931:
Swiss physicist
Auguste Piccard wanted to make his own observations of cosmic radiation in the atmosphere via hydrogen balloon. To protect himself and his assistant, though, Piccard
designed
a spherical airtight pressurized aluminum cabin. During a crash
landing
into the Bavarian Alps, he and his assistant wore helmets fashioned from wicker chicken baskets and pillows on their heads. He would go on to create special hatch doors to improve safety on crewed flights. He later predicted that a closed-capsule system would one day take humans to the moon.
1947:
After World War II, the era of plastic balloons, known as “skyhooks,”
Stratoscope I
, a 12-inch reflecting telescope operated by remote control and suspended from a polyethylene balloon. The Stratoscope I flew seven times between 1957 and 1959 with the aim of capturing high resolution imaging of solar activity. It was followed by Stratoscope II in the early ’60s, which shares some
similarities
with early prototypes for today’s Hubble Space Telescope.
1960:
Deep in the Space Race, NASA launched an ambitious project: a
satelloon
—half satellite, half balloon. It took seven tries before the balloon successfully

data.title: Show HN: GuMCP – Open-source MCP servers, hosted for free
data.author: murb
data.article_summary: Gumloop Unified Model Context Protocol (guMCP) 是一个开源项目，提供可在本地和远程运行的模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器集合。该项目旨在通过统一的后端架构，创建最大的MCP服务器集合，支持社区在人工智能（AI）集成和通用人工智能（AGI）领域的发展。guMCP支持stdio和SSE两种传输方式，包含文件系统、数据库、开发工具、AI等各类服务器。项目使用Python 3.11和Git进行安装和配置，并提供了详细的贡献指南和安全漏洞报告奖励机制。该项目遵循GPL-3.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（Model Context Protocol）的实现、工具易用性、认证机制、部署方式以及未来发展方向

不同观点：
• [johnjungles] 强调了MCP在实际工程中设置的困难，尤其是SSE设置、API密钥和作用域问题，并介绍了他们开发的https://skeet.build/mcp，旨在简化MCP的设置和使用，专注于实用性和高质量的MCP服务器。他们还提到正在开发桌面应用以增强用户体验。

• [rbehal1729] 进一步阐述了他们方案（GuMCP）的独特性，包括通过stdio和SSE统一运行服务器的方式、灵活的认证机制（如GumloopAuthClient和LocalAuthClient），以及一键部署SSE的简便性。他们特别指出现有其他选项的不足，比如Zapier's MCP是闭源的，而他们的方案提供了更多的自主性和灵活性。

• [tuananh] 选择了不同的技术路径，使用WASM作为包格式，并选择OCI注册表或DockerHub/GHCR作为包发布方式，以支持多种编程语言，尽管目前Rust对WASM的支持最好。

• [billllll] 提出了关于MCP服务器普遍可用性的问题，指出大多数现有选项都需要本地运行或自行托管，呼应了对简化部署的需求。

• [canadaduane] 关注TypeScript MCP服务器的开发，询问是否有可能推出TypeScript相关的服务器集合，以与其现有的Web基础设施更好地集成。

• [vessenes] 对MCP作为新范式的潜力表示兴奋，并提出未来是否有可能出现MCP服务器的“应用商店”，以方便用户选择和使用。

• [yahoozoo] 询问了在本地文件系统上编辑文件是否需要本地运行的MCP服务器，涉及到MCP服务器在本地开发环境中的必要性。

补充讨论：
• [compootr] 引用了一个XKCD漫画链接，暗示市场上已经有很多标准化项目，提出对“一个标准化MCP服务器项目”的幽默质疑，可能暗示对市场饱和的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 不同方案在易用性、灵活性和自主性方面的权衡。例如，[johnjungles]和[rbehal1729]强调的简化设置和自主托管，与[tuananh]选择的WASM和OCI路径的技术差异。
• 未来MCP服务器生态的构建，尤其是[vessenes]提出的“应用商店”模式的可行性和潜在价值。

Gumloop Unified Model Context Protocol (guMCP)
guMCP is an open-source collection of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that can be run both remotely and locally. The project aims to create the largest collection of MCP servers with a unified backend, fostering a community around AI integrations and the future of AGI.
Overview
While many MCP server providers are closed source, and open-source alternatives typically only support local hosting through stdio, guMCP provides:
A comprehensive collection of MCP servers that work both locally and remotely
Support for both stdio and SSE (Server-Sent Events) transports
A unified backend architecture for consistent implementation
Full open-source access to encourage community contributions
Features
Dual Transport Support
: All servers support both:
Local hosting through stdio
Remote hosting through SSE
Unified Backend
: Consistent implementation patterns across all servers
Extensive Server Collection
: Including servers for:
File systems and databases
Development tools
Web and browser automation
Productivity and communication
AI and specialized tools
Getting Started
Prerequisites
Python 3.11
Git
Installation
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/gumloop/guMCP.git
cd
guMCP
Create and activate virtual environment:
python -m venv venv
source
venv/bin/activate
#
On Unix/macOS
venv
\S
cripts
\a
ctivate
#
On Windows
Install dependencies:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
Set up environment variables:
cp .env.example .env
#
Then edit with your configuration
Usage
Running Stdio Servers
python src/servers/local.py --server=simple-tools-server
For convenience, we also provide a lightweight MCP Client to start and connect to stdio servers. Usage:
python tests/clients/LocalMCPTestClient.py --server=simple-tools-server
Running SSE Servers
An SSE server can be run locally. This will provide a single URL and host every server available.
To start the SSE development server, run:
./start_remote_dev_server.sh
For convenience, we also provide a lightweight MCP Client to connect to SSE servers. Usage:
python tests/clients/RemoteMCPTestClient.py --endpoint=http://localhost:8000/simple-tools-server/local
Contributing
We welcome contributions! Please see our
CONTRIBUTING.md
for guidelines.
Key areas for contribution:
New server implementations
Transport improvements
Documentation
Test coverage
Bug fixes
License
This project is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL-3.0) - see the
LICENSE
file for details.
Security
Security is the single highest priority for us.
That's why
Gumloop is SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and HIPAA compliant
, and why for this OSS repo, we're actively rewarding those who responsibly disclose serious vulnerabilities and exploits to
security@gumloop.com
.
Community
GitHub Issues: Bug reports and feature requests
GitHub Discussions: General questions and discussions
Forum
: Community discussions and support
Acknowledgments
This project builds on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification and is inspired by the work of various MCP implementations in the community, especially those at Anthropic.
Thank you to all the contributors that have provided feedback, advice, and early servers for the repository.

data.title: 'Water Is the New Oil' as Texas Cities Square Off over Aquifers
data.author: littlexsparkee
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了德克萨斯州中部的乔治敦市与附近城市之间因一项10亿美元引水项目而产生的激烈争端。乔治敦与一家投资者资助的企业签订合同，计划从80英里外的卡里佐-威尔考克斯含水层大量进口水源，以满足其快速增长的需求。然而，依赖同一水源的布莱恩和大学城等城市则提起诉讼，试图阻止该项目，担心其生存与发展受到威胁。该项目是多个类似引水项目中最大的一个，反映了德州城市因过度增长而面临的水资源紧缺问题。尽管立法者试图通过各种方案缓解水危机，但短期内仍依赖从农村含水层引水。而此类项目的监管机构——地下水保护区——权力有限，无法有效应对区域水资源竞争。尽管项目引发广泛反对，但其开发者声称遵循法律，并认为反对源于对未来变化的不适。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：德州水资源回收的局限性及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• malshe认为德州的水回收非常有限，建议在城市开发时强制要求水回收，但觉得由于市政府受制于开发商，这种措施难以实现。
• potato3732842对此持 cynical 态度，怀疑推动水资源讨论的动机是否真正关心水资源，还是只是为了土地估值。
• toomuchtodo引用了关于德州地下水私有产权的问题，担心如果个人拥有足够土地接触含水层，可能会无限制抽水，直至枯竭。
• kragen认为讨论的焦点应是城市用水而非农业用水，指出目前的水使用量可以通过海水淡化等技术解决。他详细分析了海水淡化的成本，并认为能源成本下降使得这种技术更加可行。同时，他指出远离海洋的地区面临更大的挑战，但通过提高设备能效和使用热泵技术，也可以降低成本。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了水资源管理的技术解决方案，如海水淡化和空气除湿技术，并通过数据分析了这些技术的成本效益。
• 争议的焦点包括水资源私有产权的问题以及不同地区如何因地制宜地解决水资源短缺，特别是在能源成本和地理位置不同的情况下。
• kragen还对比了不同地区和情境下的用水量，如洛杉矶和燃烧人节，以此说明节水的潜力和技术应用的可能性。

43539808.article_content:
In Central Texas, a bitter fight over a $1 billion water project offers a preview of the future for much of the state as decades of rapid growth push past the local limits of its most vital natural resource.
On one side: Georgetown, the fastest growing city in America for three years straight, which in 2023 signed a contract with an investor-funded enterprise to quickly begin importing vast volumes of water from the Simsboro Formation of the Carrizo Wilcox Aquifer, 80 miles to the east.
On the other side: the cities atop the Simsboro that rely on its water. Bryan, College Station and the Texas A&M University System, a metro area with almost 300,000 people, have sued the developer to stop the project. A trial is set for the first week of May.
“We’re going to fight this thing until the end,” said Bobby Gutierrez, the mayor of Bryan. “It effectively drains the water source of the cities.”
The pump and pipeline project to Georgetown, developed by California-based Upwell Water, is the largest of at least a half dozen similar projects recently completed, under construction or proposed to bring rural Carrizo Wilcox aquifer water into the booming urban corridor that follows Interstate 35 through Central Texas.
We’re hiring!
Please take a look at the new openings in our newsroom.
See jobs
It would eventually pump up to 89 million gallons per day, three times the usage of the city of Bryan, to Georgetown and its neighboring cities.
“That basically stops all the economic development we have,” Gutierrez said. “We’re talking about our survival.”
The fight over the Upwell project could well be a prelude for the broader battles to come as cities across Texas outgrow their water supplies. Lawmakers in the state Capitol are pushing to avert a broad scarcity crisis with funding to desalinate seawater, purify salty groundwater and treat
oilfield wastewater
to add to the supply. But all of these solutions remain years from realization. In the near term, only import projects from freshwater aquifers will continue to meet the growing water demands of thirsty Texas cities.
Regulation of such projects falls to a patchwork of small, rural agencies called groundwater conservation districts, which might not be fully equipped or empowered to manage plans for competing regional water needs that can affect entire cities for generations to come.
Texas law offers limited clarity, generally preferring a landowner’s right to pump their own groundwater over regulations on private property. Despite fierce denunciations of the Upwell project from nearby city leaders, no one has alleged that its developers have broken any laws.
“We’re following the rules. Why are we being vilified?” said David Lynch, a managing partner at Core Capital investment firm in Houston and a partner in the Upwell project. “I think they feel uncomfortable about what’s coming and their reaction is to make us go away.”
After all, he’s not the only one doing this. Five years ago, San Antonio started pumping up to 49 million gallons per day through a 140-mile pipeline from the Carrizo Wilcox Aquifer. Another pipeline was completed last year and will soon begin pumping to the city of Taylor and the new Samsung microchip manufacturing complex there. Another, scheduled for completion this year, will take water into the cities of Buda and Kyle.
After the lawsuit delayed the Upwell project’s tight timeline, Georgetown commissioned two other pipeline projects from the same aquifer.
“People are starting to pay enough for water to make these sorts of projects work,” Lynch said, driving his black Ford Super Duty Platinum truck down the dirt roads of Upwell’s 9,000-acre farm property and well field in Robertson County. “There’s no cheap water left in Texas.”
In the middle of all this is the little Brazos Valley Groundwater Conservation District, based in the small town of Hearne and also a defendant, alongside Upwell, in the lawsuit.
District manager Alan Day feels for the cities of Bryan and College Station. To an extent, he said, they are right. The more pumping from the aquifer, the sooner everyone will reach conditions of scarcity, though he doesn’t think it will happen as quickly as city leaders say.
At the same time, he said, “Bryan can’t claim the water.” Groundwater is a private property right in Texas as sacred as any other. Everyone is allowed to pump whatever their land produces.
“Water is the new oil,” said Day, a former ranch manager of 27 years. “They have a commodity that can be sold and they have every right to sell it.”
At this time, he said, he has no authority to stop landowners from pumping as long as they fulfill the requirements of the permitting process, which Upwell did. Even if he could do it, Day chuckled at the notion that state leaders would let his tiny office put the brakes on development along the I-35 corridor, home to manufacturing campuses of Tesla, Samsung and Apple, and offices of Amazon, Meta and Google, as well as one of the nation’s largest clus

data.title: Why I run FreeBSD for my home servers (2024)
data.author: psxuaw
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了2024年GNU/Linux作为桌面操作系统的出色表现，尤其在游戏方面取得巨大进步，归功于Valve/Steam。作者日常使用EndeavourOS，体验良好，满足安装软件、使用网络和远程工具等需求。然而，Linux作为服务器操作系统则被认为是混乱的，主要问题在于SystemD和不必要的抽象层（如Docker/Kubernetes），导致系统复杂且难以排查故障。作者强调简单和稳定性在生产环境中的重要性，并对比了Debian和FreeBSD，赞赏FreeBSD的简单、稳定和易于维护，尤其是在灾难恢复中表现优异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FreeBSD与Linux的比较，以及对systemd、容器技术（如Docker和Jails）的看法

不同观点：
• nine_k：认为systemd、Kubernetes等不是必须的，容器技术并不复杂，类似于BSD的jails。指出FreeBSD的优势在于ZFS、稳定的内核和网络栈等，而列举的Linux问题只是转移注意力的说法。
• solid_fuel：支持FreeBSD，主要因为其管理工具的稳定性，更新时不必担心工具变化或被移除，如`ifconfig`长期稳定。
• aeblyve：引用文章讨论复杂性与技术进步的关系，认为systemd解决了问题，但带来了复杂性和资源消耗，这是技术发展的自然过程。
• asveikau：选择FreeBSD的主要原因是ZFS，并从哲学角度更偏好*BSD系统。
• exiguus：认为Docker在隔离性、资源限制和可重现性方面优于jails和chroot，尤其是在CI/CD环境中。
• tracker1：强调使用Docker和容器技术可以快速搭建服务器和应用，适合个人使用，但在工作环境中可能需要更复杂的部署如Kubernetes。
• okanat：认为对systemd的不满是出于对复杂系统管理的不适应，systemd对大多数人是有益的。
• npodbielski：指出普通用户不想花费时间管理服务器，需要更简单的解决方案，如一键部署和自动更新工具。
• rollcat：对FreeBSD有褒有贬，认为其在某些方面优于Linux，但也有配置复杂、桌面体验不佳等问题，相比OpenBSD仍有不足。

补充讨论：
• lunarlull：认为Alpine、Void、Devuan或Artix等Linux发行版可以满足对无systemd的需求，BSD的优势不再明显。
• steeleduncan：驳斥复杂技术高概率失败的观点，指出复杂技术如现代飞机的安全性，认为不必使用Kubernetes或Docker，因为它们不是强制性的。

争议焦点：
• systemd的价值与复杂性：一部分人认为systemd带来了不必要的复杂性，而另一部分人认为它解决了问题并推动了技术进步。
• 容器技术与传统隔离技术的优劣：关于Docker和jails的讨论中，有人认为容器技术更具优势，尤其是在可重现性和管理方面。
• FreeBSD与Linux的实用性：讨论FreeBSD和Linux在个人服务器设置中的优缺点，特别是在管理工具的稳定性和系统更新方面。

Linux is pretty nice as Desktop :
#
In 2024 GNU/Linux is now a pretty nice OS as Desktop environnement you can absolutely runs everything without any issue.
Event if you're a gamer, huge progress has been made, thanks in particular to Valve/Steam.
On daily basic I use
EndeavourOS
on my laptop and it is great distro.
Everything works fine.
And much like a Windows user, I don't care how a particular service is launched, how the Ram is managed, etc. I just want to install/remove programs. Use Wifi, bluetooth devices, web applications, various remote control tools and some markdown / txt editors and have access to a shell.
As laptop user, the rest doesn't matter to me.
So yeah Linux is definitively a great OS Desktop.
And a big mess as Server OS :
#
Like every other sys/{ops,admin,store}, my company/customers use RHEL or Centos when it is necessary to use a Linux
And to be honest after dozens of year of administration; troubleshooting, workarround. I still didnât understand HOW this factory works.
And I've read tons of RedHat documentation / KB.
warning
SystemD.
TLDR : the main problem is SYSTEMD, the secondary problem is the stacking of abstraction layers docker / kubersomething most of the time used of unknown reasons âjust because it's modernâ.
Donât keep it Simple letâs do something complicated :
#
Looks like this is the new mantra ! The new âMicroServiceâ way of life thatâs generated gigatons of logs impossible to debug when you have issue on production.
Another point : everything that systemD manages (i.e. the entire system) makes things complicated.
Simple things like device mounting, which you'd think would be handled entirely by
/etc/fstab
, can be bypassed by systemd options.
Complicated stuff = high probably of failure = Complicated issue to troubleshoot in production
If you 2024 backend/system Product/Owner/Developpeur ... what ever please mark theses words !
warning
Reminder :
In other words : Overall system reliability is therefore the product of the individual reliability of each component.
Thus, the more components there are in the system (excepted redundancy), the greater the probability that at least one component will fail, reducing overall system reliability.
Example with a simple system the GNU/Linux log management :
#
As you can see log management is pretty simple on SystemD/Linux.
When one of your service doesnât trace anymore more the easiest way is to restart everything (journalct , syslog, rsyslog, syslog.socket ... who knows)
Also itâs pretty common on overloaded systemd to see journalctl consumming 100% of one core.
Could luck for trying to mitigate this.
I can ask you the same question what is the righ tool to use for Debian when you want deal with packages ? apt , aptitude, apt-get ?
We can also talk about the network configuration which can be done with
nmcli
or by changing config file ...
It doesn't really matter in a desktop environment. But on a server configuration, it does matter when 3 years later you have to reinstall the machine.
Yeah Debian ... ð
#
Donât talk me about SystemD/Debian please ...
Long time ago like a lot of people I was an sysadmin home user of Debian. I was running my services with âalmostâ RIP OpenVZ a
paravirtualisation
solution. At that time, Docker was just beginning to appear.
It was perfectly supported in 2.8 Kernel (Debian 8 or something even older) but for some reasons the Debian project choosen to not include the OpenVZ into the next Debian release as upstream solution. The only way to continue using OpenVZ was to ... downgrade its kernel to continue taking advantage of portability ?!!
And if you want to keep using OpenVZ
you have to use Devian
What a joke.
So I have to redo all my âarchitectureâ redeploy all my service into a new container solution ?! Rewrite/test the backup Script and so on ... Ho thank you and good bye Debian !
Professional distributions with which you can't even do a rolling upgrade (Rhel / Rocky) :
#
Thatâs probably the biggest joke for a profesionnal distribution : if you want to jump from 1 main branch to another one you have to reinstall everything (or use tools like leap)
Yeah I know , you can do it with Debian/Fedora/Arch (which is rolling).
And with FreeBSD ð
#
Everything is simple , everything is documented, everything make sense.
Ok things are probably a bit âold-schoolâ and use the old Unix-way to do thing.
But this is what we like/needs in production :
simplicity and stability
!
I ran FreeBSD on my personnals server since 9.x released and so far upgrade after upgrade no breaking changes !
Everything works since the beginning.
Of course, I've changed physical servers several times and had to deal with disaster recovery situations. Each time, the operation of restarting the services proved to be simple and effective.
Restoring from disaster (macro plan) :
#

data.title: Oregon abandoned its drug law. Then came the mass arrests
data.author: c420
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了俄勒冈州在取消毒品犯罪化法律后，重新开始大规模逮捕持有毒品和违规露营者的现象。2021年通过的110号提案原旨在将小量毒品持有去罪化，并投资于戒毒和减少伤害服务，但由于芬太尼泛滥、疫情和社会服务关闭，该政策面临强烈反对。2022年，州政府重新将小量毒品持有定为犯罪，最高可判180天监禁。这一转变导致无家可归者和毒品使用者频繁入狱，而他们获得法律援助和治疗的机会有限。尽管新政策减少了公共场所的显性毒品使用，但却加剧了无家可归者的困境。警方在执法中逮捕多人，但许多人在缺乏律师帮助的情况下反复进出监狱，难以获得有效治疗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对毒品问题的政策选择及其困境

不同观点：
• [spicyusername] 认为当前在减少监禁和继续逮捕吸毒者之间面临两难选择。减少监禁成本较低且对吸毒者较为人道，但无法减少社区内的毒品使用；而继续逮捕吸毒者则会将吸毒者从社区中移除，但成本高且道德上存在问题。最终的解决方案可能需要几十年才能见效，且需要多方面的社会变革，但在当前的文化和政治环境下几乎不可能实现。

• [verteu] 指出法律并未取得明显成效，并提供了一些数据和链接，显示在新冠和芬太尼流行期间，过量吸毒现象增加。这表明现行政策并非成功的解决方案。

• [acidmath] 强调许多成瘾者已经不再是单纯为了“寻求快感”，而是为了避免痛苦的戒断症状。Ibogaine诊所可以帮助很多人恢复正常生活，尽管并非对所有人有效，但对那些愿意改变生活方式的人来说是有用的。

• [josefritzishere] 认为监禁成本高昂，提出了一种不进行指控但没收和销毁毒品的政策，认为允许毒贩利用脆弱人群是不公正的。

• [timewizard] 同意成瘾者除非自愿戒毒，否则不会成功，并主张对毒品进行没收和销毁，而不应对个人进行刑事指控，认为强迫治疗是不公正的。

• [givemeethekeys] 认为政府意识到无法对抗毒贩集团，因此试图通过恐吓民众来达到治理目的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡减少毒品使用与处理成瘾者的人道方式。一方认为需要社会多方面的长期变革，另一方则关注具体干预措施如Ibogaine诊所的效果。
• 政策的经济成本和道德问题也是讨论的核心，特别是在监禁成本高昂且效果不显著的情况下。
• 不同意见还涉及到是否应强制治疗或依赖成瘾者的自我意愿，以及如何处理毒品的供应和贩卖问题。

43537866.article_content:
Police officers carry out arrests in Medford, Oregon, on 25 February. Due to the state’s ‘war on drugs’, many of these people are rearrested for possession or camping violations.
Photograph: Amanda Lucier/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Police officers carry out arrests in Medford, Oregon, on 25 February. Due to the state’s ‘war on drugs’, many of these people are rearrested for possession or camping violations.
Photograph: Amanda Lucier/The Guardian
Oregon
Oregon abandoned its radical drug law. Then came the mass arrests
Last year, the state ended a trailblazing law decriminalizing possession. Drug users in some counties are now in and out of jail, without lawyers, struggling to get treatment
Sam Levin
in Medford, Oregon, with photographs by Amanda Lucier
Mon 31 Mar 2025 10.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 31 Mar 2025 15.54 EDT
Share
At 7.45am on a cool February morning in Medford,
Oregon
, six police officers pulled up to a desolate road lined with tarps and a shopping cart and began making arrests.
The officers directed four adults to sit on the sidewalk, handcuffing them behind their backs and rifling through their pockets. They were being detained for illegal camping, but the officers were also searching for evidence of drugs.
“Love you!” a husband and wife shouted at each other as they were separated to be taken to jail.
Oregon judge blocks city from enforcing homeless camping ban
Read more
Officer Paul Verling placed one 43-year-old woman in the back of his car while his team tested a confiscated glass pipe for drug residue. He told her she could potentially avoid jail if she entered drug treatment.
The woman said she had been using methamphetamine to cope with homelessness and would be grateful for treatment. But once Verling ran her name through the system, he discovered she had a warrant for a probation violation. That made her ineligible for “deflection”. She, too, would be going to jail, he said, possibly for a month.
“You wanna engage in some rehab when you get out?” he said.
“Yes sir,” she mumbled.
“I’m glad we had this talk today,” Verling said, as he took her out of the car to escort her into a jail enclosure.
View image in fullscreen
Medford police officers detain a number of people in Medford, Oregon, on 25 February.
Welcome to Oregon’s “war on drugs” 2.0.
In September, Oregon lawmakers enacted legislation turning low-level drug possession into a
more serious crime punishable by up to 180 days in jail. The resulting crackdown has led to thousands of arrests statewide in recent months. People targeted in cities such as Medford, and overworked public defenders tasked with representing them, say the drug enforcement has been chaotic and at times brutal.
While the new policy has appeared to reduce visible drug use in some public spaces, unhoused people, who have been most impacted by the police response, say it has exacerbated their struggles.
The new law also marks a stunning reversal of policy for the Pacific north-west state.
Just four years ago, Oregon voters passed
Measure 110
, a groundbreaking drug decriminalization measure that abandoned jail sentences for possessing small amounts of drugs and imposed an infraction citation instead. Passed on the heels of
Black Lives Matter
uprisings, the measure aimed to treat addiction as a disease instead of a crime, prioritize services and recovery over jail,
reduce
overcrowding behind bars and help address racial disparities in policing and prosecutions.
At the time, Oregon was grappling with rising overdoses. It
ranked
second nationally for drug addiction rates and worst in the US for access to treatment. The problem was systemic, rooted in decades of failure to invest in the level of
behavioral health services
needed for people with mental illnesses and addiction. Measure 110 called for an
infusion of $302m
for addiction recovery and harm reduction services, with a focus on underserved communities, including Black and Indigenous people impacted by criminalization.
Drug policy reform advocates hoped the first-in-the-nation decriminalization experiment would become a model.
But the timing could not have been worse. The law went into effect in 2021 as
fentanyl
was rapidly entering Oregon’s unregulated drug market, the pandemic was shuttering vital social services and
homelessness
was surging amid Covid and unprecedented
wildfires
.
View image in fullscreen
Crystal Bilyeu of Max’s Mission, a harm-reduction organization, connects people with supplies such as Narcan, fentanyl test strips and wound care kits.
As Measure 110-funded recovery programs were just getting off the ground, the decriminalization measure was widely blamed for crime, surging fentanyl overdoses and the increasing visibility of homelessness and drug use, even as research
suggested
a complex set of
factors
behind these
trends
. The
backlash was fierce
, and the state’s Democratic governor, Tina Kotek, signed the bill last year recriminalizing possession.

43537866.article_summary: 本文讲述了俄勒冈州在取消毒品犯罪化法律后，重新开始大规模逮捕持有毒品和违规露营者的现象。2021年通过的110号提案原旨在将小量毒品持有去罪化，并投资于戒毒和减少伤害服务，但由于芬太尼泛滥、疫情和社会服务关闭，该政策面临强烈反对。2022年，州政府重新将小量毒品持有定为犯罪，最高可判180天监禁。这一转变导致无家可归者和毒品使用者频繁入狱，而他们获得法律援助和治疗的机会有限。尽管新政策减少了公共场所的显性毒品使用，但却加剧了无家可归者的困境。警方在执法中逮捕多人，但许多人在缺乏律师帮助的情况下反复进出监狱，难以获得有效治疗。
43537866.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [verteu] 指出法律并未取得明显成效，并提供了一些数据和链接，显示在新冠和芬太尼流行期间，过量吸毒现象增加。这表明现行政策并非成功的解决方案。

data.article_summary: Captrice是一款专为吉他玩家设计的练习应用，通过智能节拍器捕捉数据并提供可操作的练习建议，专注于速度、耐力、准确性和适应性。它无需音乐理论知识，提供练习库或自定义练习功能，免费使用，无广告和注册。应用可在任何浏览器上运行，数据存储在用户设备上，支持离线模式。主要功能包括节拍器、练习构建器、 tablature/乐谱嵌入、练习库、进度洞察和分享功能。Captrice旨在帮助用户每天有效练习，提升速度，针对弱点进行训练，适合各水平玩家。该应用由软件工程师兼吉他爱好者Vineet Naik开发，未来计划推出高级功能，但基础版将始终免费。

43512470.article_content:
A
deliberate
practice app
for guitar players who want to level up
Practice using a smart metronome that captures metrics and
turns them into actionable insights; paired with an effective
practice method focusing on speed, endurance, accuracy, and
adaptability.
No knowledge of music theory required
A library of exercises to import from, or create your own
Free to use. No ads. No signup
Works in any browser on PC & smartphone. No app download needed
Data is stored on your device. Export/Delete anytime.
Works in "Offline mode" (if the browser supports it)
Though Captrice aims for sustained progress, a 30 minutes
practice session is enough to see the difference in your
playing.
Try it out now
What makes captrice
effective
?
Features
Metronome
An ergonomic metronome, easily operated using keyboard
shortcuts while playing guitar
Exercise builder
Build your repository of exercises. Organize them into
collections
Tablature/Notation
Embed guitar tablature and music notation in exercises for
quick reference
Library
Get access to a library of exercises covering speed-building
drills, finger independence exercises, warmup routines and
more.
Insights
Track your progress and get actionable insights through
beautiful, intuitive visualizations
Sharing
Export/Import functionality to share exercises with
your friends, students and audience
Use cases
Practice
daily
Create/Import exercises based on scales, arpeggios, triads
etc. Add some warm up exercises into the mix. Aim to practice
them daily. Let the practice streaks chart fuel your motivation.
Build
speed
Want to nail a fast guitar solo/riff?
Turn challenges phrases into exercises. Progressively increase
speed while keeping track of how long you can consistenly
maintain speed and accuracy.
Target
weak spots
Work on specific guitar techniques such as two hand tapping,
legato, sweep picking etc. Find an exercise from the library or
create your own based on a tutorial video that works for you.
Beginner or expert, Captrice helps you improve by facilitating a
game-changing practice framework
focusing on speed, endurance, accuracy, and adaptability.
Read more
No signup
required
Captrice is a
local-first
app that stores all data in your browser.
That means your data is truly
your
data!
Export any time. Delete any time.
Give it a try
Pricing
It's
free
!
Captrice is a "passion project".
While there are plans to offer premium features at a price,
the "no-signup, local-only" version of this app is free and I intend to keep it that way.
If you'd like to support,
buy me a coffee
or help spread the word.
It means a lot to me! ð
Why
I built captrice?
If you have 30 minutes of free time, would you pick up your
guitar or phone? The path of least resistence always wins!
Even if you picked the guitar, you'd probably noodle away
instead of practicing something that advances your skills.
The challenge isn't finding what to practice—today,
exercises are everywhere—it's choosing practice over the
endless distractions we have at our fingertips.
I built this app to solve my own struggle - curated exercises
eliminate indecision about what to pratice, the metronome keeps
me focused, and data visualizations helps with motivation.
It works for me and it might work for you too.
Are you a
guitar teacher
?
Do you think this app could benefit your students, specially
if their practice data is made available to you in the form of
intuitive and insightful visualizations?
If you think something like this should exist please complete
this short
survey
.
Are you a guitar
content creator
?
Do you create tutorial videos, shorts/reels on
Youtube/Instagram?
If you're interested in publishing your tutorials and lessons
in the Library, please get in touch via
email
Help & Feedback
Need help or got feedback? Drop me a line at
show email
.
Subscribe
to the newsletter
Captrice doesn't need you to signup, so it's the only way I can
reach out. You will get notified about feature releases and new exercise
bundles in the library.
No spam, I promise!
Powered by Buttondown.
Who is behind this?
I am Vineet Naik, a software engineer and hobbyist guitar player
from Bangalore, India.
I picked up the guitar in 2001 and somehow the hobby has
stuck. I played in a few amateur bands during college. Since
then, I have pretty much been a bedroom musician.
Nevertheless, I am always on the lookout for new ways to
practice and level up, which is what this project was born out
of.
Thanks for stopping by!

data.title: Go Optimization Guide
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary:
《Go应用性能优化系列》是一组技术文章，旨在帮助开发者编写更快速、高效的Go应用。该系列提供实用模式、真实案例及底层性能洞察，涵盖高吞吐量API、微服务和分布式系统的优化。虽然Go的性能调优选项不如C++或Rust多，但仍有许多方法能显著提升应用性能，包括内存重用、分配控制、高效网络及并发模式。

目前文章涵盖的性能模式包括：
1. 有效使用`sync.Pool`
2. 避免不必要的内存分配
3. 结构布局与内存对齐
4. 高效错误处理
5. 零成本抽象的接口
6. 就地排序与切片重用

后续将深入探讨高性能网络，包括`net/http`和`net.Conn`的高效使用、并发连接管理、性能调优及负载测试技术。该系列适合后端工程师、对延迟敏感系统的开发者及迁移到Go的团队。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的内存管理与性能优化

不同观点：
• nopurpose认为，减少GC时间的关键在于最小化长时间存活的分配，而非所有分配。短生命周期的分配对GC时间影响较小，而在实际应用中，完全避免GC是不现实的。
• stouset指出，Go的类型系统在某些API（如sync.Pool）中失去了强类型的优势，且缺乏重置值为默认状态的API，这可能导致类型安全问题。
• kevmo314强调，零拷贝技术在Go中非常有用，但需要精心设计才能实现，其带来的性能提升是显著的。
• donatj对sync.Pool持谨慎态度，认为其使用复杂且容易出错，建议在万不得已时才使用。
• roundup提供了关于Go优化的外部资源链接，并表达了对工具支持的需求，以便在不同项目间切换时更容易记住重要信息。
• jrockway分享了GOMEMLIMIT在容器化和CI环境中的实用经验，帮助控制内存使用和GC频率。
• parhamn关心sync包是否会引入泛型，以提高类型安全和使用便利性。
• dennis-tra和EdwardDiego对编译器为何不自动处理结构体字段对齐感到疑惑，认为这应是编译器的优化功能。
• jensneuse提醒，使用sync.Pool时要小心，尽管pprof显示无分配，但实际内存使用可能很高，需衡量实际效益而非仅依赖合成基准测试。
• nikolayasdf123建议优化指南开放社区编辑和评论功能，以促进知识共享和更新。
• kunley对文章中默认使用32位架构的假设表示质疑，认为64位架构更为常见。
• _345询问是否有类似Python 3的优化资源。

补充讨论：
• nikolayasdf123对文章的组织和基准测试支持表示赞赏，认为这是社区驱动性能优化的良好起点。
• 争议的焦点包括sync.Pool的复杂性和潜在风险，以及Go类型系统在某些API中的应用问题。
• 讨论还涉及结构体字段对齐的自动化需求和实际开发中对优化技术的需求。

43539585.article_content:
Patterns and Techniques for Writing High-Performance Applications with Go
¶
The
Go App Optimization Series
is a collection of technical articles aimed at helping developers write faster, more efficient Go applications. Whether you're building high-throughput APIs, microservices, or distributed systems, this series offers practical patterns, real-world use cases, and low-level performance insights to guide your optimization efforts.
While Go doesn’t expose as many knobs for performance tuning as languages like C++ or Rust, it still provides
plenty of opportunities
to make your applications significantly faster. From memory reuse and allocation control to efficient networking and concurrency patterns, Go offers a pragmatic set of tools for writing high-performance code.
We focus on
concrete techniques
with
mesurable impact
you can apply immediately—covering everything from core language features to advanced networking strategies.
What’s Covered So Far
¶
Common Go Patterns for Performance
¶
In this first article, we explore a curated set of high-impact performance patterns every Go developer should know:
Using
sync.Pool
effectively
Avoiding unnecessary allocations
Struct layout and memory alignment
Efficient error handling
Zero-cost abstractions with interfaces
In-place sorting and slices reuse
Each pattern is grounded in practical use cases, with benchmarks and examples you can copy into your own codebase.
What’s Coming Next
¶
High-Performance Networking in Go
¶
In our upcoming deep dive into networking, we'll focus on building high-throughput network services with Go’s standard library and beyond. This includes:
Efficient use of
net/http
and
net.Conn
Managing large volumes of concurrent connections
Performance tuning with epoll/kqueue and
GOMAXPROCS
Load testing techniques and bottleneck diagnostics
TBD...
We'll also explore when to drop down to lower-level libraries like
fasthttp
, and how to balance performance with maintainability.
Who This Is For
¶
This series is ideal for:
Backend engineers optimizing Go services in production
Developers working on latency-sensitive systems
Teams migrating to Go and building performance-critical paths
Anyone curious about Go’s performance model and trade-offs
Stay tuned—more articles, code samples, and tools are on the way. You can bookmark this page to follow the series as it evolves.

• nopurpose认为，减少GC时间的关键在于最小化长时间存活的分配，而非所有分配。短生命周期的分配对GC时间影响较小，而在实际应用中，完全避免GC是不现实的。
• stouset指出，Go的类型系统在某些API（如sync.Pool）中失去了强类型的优势，且缺乏重置值为默认状态的API，这可能导致类型安全问题。
• kevmo314强调，零拷贝技术在Go中非常有用，但需要精心设计才能实现，其带来的性能提升是显著的。
• donatj对sync.Pool持谨慎态度，认为其使用复杂且容易出错，建议在万不得已时才使用。
• roundup提供了关于Go优化的外部资源链接，并表达了对工具支持的需求，以便在不同项目间切换时更容易记住重要信息。
• jrockway分享了GOMEMLIMIT在容器化和CI环境中的实用经验，帮助控制内存使用和GC频率。
• parhamn关心sync包是否会引入泛型，以提高类型安全和使用便利性。
• dennis-tra和EdwardDiego对编译器为何不自动处理结构体字段对齐感到疑惑，认为这应是编译器的优化功能。
• jensneuse提醒，使用sync.Pool时要小心，尽管pprof显示无分配，但实际内存使用可能很高，需衡量实际效益而非仅依赖合成基准测试。
• nikolayasdf123建议优化指南开放社区编辑和评论功能，以促进知识共享和更新。
• kunley对文章中默认使用32位架构的假设表示质疑，认为64位架构更为常见。
• _345询问是否有类似Python 3的优化资源。

补充讨论：
• nikolayasdf123对文章的组织和基准测试支持表示赞赏，认为这是社区驱动性能优化的良好起点。
• 争议的焦点包括sync.Pool的复杂性和潜在风险，以及Go类型系统在某些API中的应用问题。
• 讨论还涉及结构体字段对齐的自动化需求和实际开发中对优化技术的需求。

data.title: The Guardian flourishes without a paywall
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 《卫报》美国分部通过读者捐款支持其无付费墙的新闻模式，近年来取得了显著成功。在许多媒体因亿万富翁所有者的影响而面临编辑独立性问题时，《卫报》强调其没有受富人或企业压力的优势，专注于公正和准确的报道。自特朗普时代以来，《卫报》的筹款呼吁变得更加紧迫，尤其在《华盛顿邮报》和《洛杉矶时报》对卡玛拉·哈里斯撤回预期背书后，其捐款大幅增加。2024年总统选举周成为其美国读者收入历史上的最高峰。目前，《卫报》美国分部的读者捐款占总收入的60%以上，预计今年将达4400万美元，比去年增长33%。尽管曾面临亏损和重组，但在疫情期间及之后，其读者群显著增长，月访问量达4000万至5000万，甚至超过了《华尔街日报》在美国的受众规模。这种无付费墙模式的成功引发了业界对新闻商业模式创新的新思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《The Guardian》的商业模式、读者捐赠、内容质量及数字阅读体验的多角度讨论。

不同观点：
• **对《The Guardian》所有权模式的兴趣与质疑**：
  - [yen223] 认为《The Guardian》的信托所有权模式很有趣，旨在避免商业利益干扰，但其实际效果值得商榷。
  
• **财务状况与捐赠模式的有效性**：
  - [ackbar03] 指出《The Guardian》频繁请求捐款，让人感觉其财务状况不稳定，但同时肯定其新闻质量的重要性。
  - [antasvara] 认为尽管读者捐款数额可观，但要达到盈利仍需大量读者支持，将其收入与《华尔街日报》对比，指出其商业模式的挑战。
  - [sitkack] 表示自己每月捐款3美元以绕过捐款提示，暗示这种模式对读者的影响。

• **内容质量与读者体验**：
  - [puttycat] 强调《The Guardian》的出色内容和优秀作家是其成功的关键。
  - [rozab] 提到在阅读时被迫接受所有广告cookies，对用户体验有所影响。
  - [neilv] 指出《The Guardian》使用Google的DoubleClick进行广告，但比许多美国新闻机构对第三方追踪器的依赖要少。
  - [mcswell] 质疑《The Guardian》是否进行深入调查报道，与《华盛顿邮报》和《纽约时报》进行比较。

• **订阅与付费墙的讨论**：
  - [zem] 表示订阅《The Guardian》是因为它不设付费墙，可以让更多人免费阅读，认为物有所值。
  - [mrbluecoat] 幽默地提到自己因付费墙而无法阅读文章，暗示对付费墙模式的不满。

补充讨论：
• **《The Guardian》与《纽约时报》的对比**：
  - [julianeon] 提到《纽约时报》通过付费墙实现盈利，暗示这种模式的成功，可能为《The Guardian》提供参考。

争议焦点：
• 《The Guardian》的所有权模式是否有效避免了商业干扰。
• 读者捐款模式的可持续性及对读者体验的影响。
• 付费墙与内容质量之间的平衡与取舍。

43511529.article_content:
Photo-Illustration: Intelligencer; Photos: Getty Images
There was a time in media when having a billionaire owner was an asset. For many outlets, this is still the case, particularly those publishing
super-secretive group chats
of powerful government officials who seem eager to trample on the rights of the press. But for others, like the Washington
Post
and the Los Angeles
Times
, both of which have seen their benefactors bend a knee to Donald Trump and sacrifice the integrity of their newspapers in the process, ownership has become a problem. A problem that the
Guardian
US, the American arm of the British newspaper, has exploited.
“All around us, media organizations have begun to capitulate,” editor Betsy Reed writes in the current fundraising appeal at the bottom of each
Guardian
article. “
The Guardian
has neither a self-interested billionaire owner nor profit-seeking corporate henchmen pressuring us to appease the rich and powerful. With the new administration boasting about its desire to punish journalists, and Trump and his allies already pursuing lawsuits against newspapers whose stories they don’t like, it has never been more urgent, or more perilous, to pursue fair, accurate reporting. Can you support
The Guardian
today?”
The asks themselves are not new.
The Guardian
for the past eight years has asked readers to donate in support of its journalism, a “reader revenue” program that helps the paper exist without a paywall. But the appeals have gotten more strident — and more Trump-focused — since the
Post
and the L.A.
Times
withdrew expected endorsements for Kamala Harris last fall, and to great effect. The last week in February was the second-biggest week in U.S. reader-revenue history for
The Guardian
; the biggest was the week of the 2024 presidential election.
The
Guardian
US expects to hit $44 million in voluntary reader donations in the U.S. and Canada this year, up 33 percent over last year, with some people supporting on a recurring basis and others giving one-time contributions. A
first-person account
by a Canadian citizen detained by ICE, for example, netted $105,000 in pledged donations. These contributions account for more than 60 percent of the American operation’s total revenue, which last year exceeded costs by $16 million (the rest of its revenue comes from advertising and philanthropic support from foundations). The amount that people are contributing on a pledged basis doubled in October — the month that Jeff Bezos pulled the
Post
’s endorsement for Harris — and has stayed at that level every month since, according to internal data provided by
The Guardian
, which just surpassed 350,000 recurring supporters in the U.S.
“Our messaging does appeal to people to support our work as a kind of cause, and I think that works for a number of reasons,” Reed said in a recent interview in her downtown office, “but one is that there is a real crisis of access to reliable information for people who don’t want or have the means to subscribe to the New York
Times
. That is a real problem that we have an answer to.”
Guardian
managing director Steve Sachs added that
The Guardian
’s global perspective — the internal catchphrase of the U.S. operation is that it covers America for the world and the world for America — is also a draw at such a volatile moment in geopolitics. “People are even more interested now than they were six months ago,” he said. The
Guardian
US’ audience is split 50-50 between American and global readers.
The Guardian
launched its U.S. operation more than a decade ago and seemed to have a promising start, hiring high-profile columnists like Michael Wolff and Glenn Greenwald and winning a Pulitzer for
reporting
on widespread secret surveillance by the National Security Agency. But as the Obama era gave way to the Trump era, the close association of the
Guardian
US with surveillance-state reporting made it less relevant to American readers. Annual losses led to
restructuring
that
hit
the U.S. operation, once
housed
in an airy Soho loft, particularly hard.
But during the pandemic, the
Guardian
US, like other news outlets, experienced a surge in reader interest, readying it for an expansion in 2022 that included
hiring Reed
, formerly of
The Nation
and the Intercept, and
Sachs
, who’d spent years on the business side of Time Inc. The audience has continued to grow, with Sachs noting that the site typically sees between 40 million to 50 million unique visitors a month. “We’re now at a place where our audience is actually bigger in the U.S. than
The Wall Street Journal
’s audience in the U.S.,” he said.
Leaders and organizations across the media industry have been trying to innovate in the way people can pay for news. Sachs says he’s been increasingly asked about the no-paywall model, with others in the industry wondering whether they should adopt the same. “If you’re creative enough, you can figure out some new things,” he tells people. “But the question is, does it scale?” If it’s “anot

data.title: KOReader: Open-Source eBook Reader
data.author: charleshan
data.article_summary: KOReader是一款支持多种文档格式的电子书阅读应用，适用于Cervantes、Kindle、Kobo、PocketBook和Android设备。它支持固定页面格式（如PDF、DjVu）和重排电子书格式（如EPUB、FB2），并集成了Calibre、Wallabag、Wikipedia等服务。KOReader专为电子墨水屏设备优化，具有无动画的自定义UI、分页菜单和可调对比度。该应用高度可扩展，通过插件实现额外功能，并且在一些旧设备上具有更快的翻页速度。KOReader由全球志愿者开发和维护，支持通过Liberapay捐赠。主要功能包括多语言界面、自定义排版选项、在线词典查询和OTA更新等。安装步骤和开发指南可在其官网和Wiki上找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KOReader软件的功能、使用体验、技术细节以及在不同设备上的应用

不同观点：
• **KOReader的优势**：
  ◦ [II2II] 认为KOReader在用户界面和功能上进步显著，特别是其对阅读进度的跟踪功能，对技术书籍的阅读非常实用。整体设计注重阅读体验，而非商业销售。
  ◦ [OuterVale] 非常喜欢KOReader，尤其是在Kindle设备上的表现，并提到其家人也在使用。同时分享了在旧Kindle设备上安装KOReader的指南。
  ◦ [BeetleB] 指出KOReader在Kobo设备上处理标准epub文件的表现优于原生阅读器，特别是在高亮文本时没有卡顿。

• **KOReader的可定制性和技术细节**：
  ◦ [deng] 强调KOReader的高可 hack性，其大部分代码使用Lua编写，用户可以轻松添加新功能。
  ◦ [throwaway2046] 提到构建KOReader模拟器需要使用CMake、Meson和autotools三种不同的构建系统，质疑其必要性。
  ◦ [mmooss] 提问关于E-ink屏幕的独特挑战，如刷新速度慢、对比度和色彩表现不足等技术问题。

• **KOReader的局限性和争议**：
  ◦ [E39M5S62] 提到在Kobo Libra 2上打开大文件时速度较慢，且调整字体大小会导致整个文档重新排版，表现不如原生软件。
  ◦ [locusofself] 想尝试KOReader，但担心会损坏其不再销售的Kindle Oasis第二版设备。

• **KOReader与其他软件和服务的兼容性**：
  ◦ [ZeWaren] 使用自托管的calibre-web管理电子书，并与KOReader同步，认为KOReader的翻页速度更快。
  ◦ [sodality2] 也使用calibre-web与KOReader配合，避免使用USB或Amazon的传输方式，非常方便。
  ◦ [jtmoulia] 询问KOReader是否能与图书馆的电子书（通过Overdrive等）集成，但发现KOReader不支持DRM书籍。

• **关于获取DRM免费书籍的讨论**：
  ◦ [fisian] 询问推荐的购买无DRM书籍的网站，以便在KOReader上使用。
  ◦ [ementally] 推荐了Book Story作为另一个支持多种格式的FOSS电子书阅读器。

补充讨论：
• KOReader的跨平台支持和用户社区活跃度被多次提到，特别是在旧设备上的应用（如Kindle和Kobo）。
• 对E-ink屏幕的技术挑战和KOReader的性能优化是技术用户关注的重点。
• 用户对KOReader的功能和定制性表示赞赏，但也提到其在处理大文件和DRM书籍方面的局限性。

KOReader is a document viewer primarily aimed at e-ink readers.
Download
•
User guide
•
Wiki
•
Developer docs
Main features
portable
: runs on embedded devices (Cervantes, Kindle, Kobo, PocketBook, reMarkable), Android and Linux computers. Developers can run a KOReader emulator in Linux and MacOS.
multi-format documents
: supports fixed page formats (PDF, DjVu, CBT, CBZ) and reflowable e-book formats (EPUB, FB2, Mobi, DOC, RTF, HTML, CHM, TXT). Scanned PDF/DjVu documents can also be reflowed with the built-in K2pdfopt library.
ZIP files
are also supported for some formats.
full-featured reading
: multi-lingual user interface with a highly customizable reader view and many typesetting options. You can set arbitrary page margins, override line spacing and choose external fonts and styles. It has multi-lingual hyphenation dictionaries bundled into the application.
integrated
with
calibre
(search metadata, receive ebooks wirelessly, browse library via OPDS),
Wallabag
,
Wikipedia
,
Google Translate
and other content providers.
optimized for e-ink devices
: custom UI without animation, with paginated menus, adjustable text contrast, and easy zoom to fit content or page in paged media.
extensible
: via plugins
fast
: on some older devices, it has been measured to have less than half the page-turn delay as the built in reading software.
and much more
: look up words with StarDict dictionaries / Wikipedia, add your own online OPDS catalogs and RSS feeds, over-the-air software updates, an FTP client, an SSH server, …

and the

43539103.article_summary: KOReader是一款支持多种文档格式的电子书阅读应用，适用于Cervantes、Kindle、Kobo、PocketBook和Android设备。它支持固定页面格式（如PDF、DjVu）和重排电子书格式（如EPUB、FB2），并集成了Calibre、Wallabag、Wikipedia等服务。KOReader专为电子墨水屏设备优化，具有无动画的自定义UI、分页菜单和可调对比度。该应用高度可扩展，通过插件实现额外功能，并且在一些旧设备上具有更快的翻页速度。KOReader由全球志愿者开发和维护，支持通过Liberapay捐赠。主要功能包括多语言界面、自定义排版选项、在线词典查询和OTA更新等。安装步骤和开发指南可在其官网和Wiki上找到。

主要讨论点：网络文件系统在macOS等系统上的实现和改进

不同观点：
• [schmidtleonard] 认为，经过20年时间，希望新的网络文件系统实现能够解决macOS在网络延迟时卡顿的问题。这暗示当前的实现存在明显缺陷，尤其是在处理网络不稳定的情况下。

• [mrpippy] 指出，macOS、iOS和iPadOS其实已经内部使用这项技术多年，主要用于实现一些辅助文件系统（如FAT）。但直到macOS 15.4，这项技术才首次作为支持的API对第三方开放。这表明系统本身早已具备一定的技术基础，只是之前未对外公开。

• [leohonexus] 对新技术开放表示欢迎，并提到希望减少对macFUSE的依赖。macFUSE目前无人维护，且安装和使用都比较麻烦，因此新的API可能带来更好的用户体验。

补充讨论：
• [schmidtleonard] 提出的网络延迟问题是一个重要的用户痛点，可能反映出当前网络文件系统在处理不稳定网络环境时的不足。

• [mrpippy] 的回应揭示了这项技术其实早已存在，只是未被广泛应用或公开，这可能缓解了一些对技术成熟度的担忧。

• [leohonexus] 提到了第三方工具macFUSE的维护问题，这表明在实际应用中，用户对现有解决方案并不满意，期待官方的替代方案。

争议焦点：当前的网络文件系统实现是否足够成熟和稳定，能否解决实际使用中的卡顿问题。用户对macFUSE的依赖和不满也反映出对更好解决方案的迫切需求。

data.title: UK's GCHQ Intern Transferred Top Secret Files to His Phone
data.author: m463
data.article_summary: 前GCHQ实习生哈桑·阿尔沙德（Hasaan Arshad）承认违反《计算机滥用法》，将绝密数据从安全电脑转移到手机并带回家，危害国家安全。2022年8月24日，他将手机带入GCHQ绝密区域，连接工作站并传输数据。9月22日，警方逮捕了他并搜查其住所。阿尔沙德还承认在2022年9月7日至23日期间制作儿童不雅照片。法官麦高恩（McGowan）将判决推迟至6月13日，并要求提交量刑前报告，同时保释阿尔沙德，但禁止他访问暗网。她警告称，不排除判处监禁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GCHQ实习生的背景审查及其潜在安全风险

不同观点：
• ctippett认为，文章中对于Arshad此前承认制作儿童不雅照片的指控仅在最后几段提及，令人感到意外，并质疑GCHQ对实习生的背景审查是否充分。这暗示了对高敏感度岗位背景调查的担忧。

• Havoc对此表示震惊，质疑一个曾有前科的实习生如何能够接触到绝密信息，并将此事与之前发生的"DOGE实习生"事件相比较，暗示对GCHQ在人员筛选和信息安全管理上的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 提到"DOGE实习生"事件，可能是指过去发生过的类似安全漏洞，增加了对当前事件的批评力度，并暗示相关机构在管理上可能存在一贯的疏忽。

• 讨论中的一个焦点是，高敏感度机构如GCHQ在招聘实习生时是否进行了足够的背景调查，以及这些实习生是否真的能够接触到敏感信息。

GCHQ worker admits taking top secret data home
13 hours ago
Share
Save
Ewan Gawne
BBC News, Manchester
Share
Save
GCHQ
GCHQ is based in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire
A former GCHQ intern has admitted risking national security by taking top secret data home with him on his mobile phone.
Hasaan Arshad, 25, pleaded guilty to an offence under the Computer Misuse Act on what would have been the first day of his trial at the Old Bailey in London.
The charge related to committing an unauthorised act which risked damaging national security.
Arshad, from Rochdale in Greater Manchester, is said to have transferred sensitive data from a secure computer to his phone, which he had taken into a top secret area of GCHQ on 24 August 2022.
Top secret is the classification for the government's most sensitive information.
The compromise of this data might cause widespread loss of life or threaten the security or economic wellbeing of the country or friendly nations, according to Ministry of Justice security guidance.
'Recklessness'
A senior judge previously ruled that some parts of Arshad's case would be heard behind closed doors, in the absence of the press and public.
The court heard that Arshad took his work mobile into a top secret GCHQ area and connected it to work station.
He then transferred sensitive data from a secure, top secret computer to the phone before taking it home, it was claimed.
Arshad then transferred the data from the phone to a hard drive connected to his personal home computer.
He was arrested and his home was searched on 22 September 2022.
Arshad's lawyer Nina Grahame KC told the court that he had admitted the offence on the "basis of recklessness".
The court was told Arshad had previously admitted two charges of making an indecent photograph of a child in relation to a number of images found between 7 and 23 September 2022.
Mrs Justice McGowan adjourned sentencing for all the charges to June 13.
The senior judge ordered a pre-sentence report and granted Arshad continued bail with various conditions, including not to access the dark web.
She told him: "I want you to understand because of your age I am making the request for the pre-sentence report in this case, but that does not mean there will not be a custodial sentence."
Arshad wore a dark grey suit, white shirt and dark brown tie and nodded that he understood before leaving the dock.

data.article_summary: Aim 是一个开源、自托管的机器学习实验追踪工具，能够处理上万次训练运行，提供高效美观的用户界面以比较和观察训练数据，并通过API进行编程访问。它支持与多种流行ML框架的集成，如Pytorch、TensorFlow、Hugging Face等，并允许通过SDK对元数据进行查询。Aim 还提供实时监控、日志记录、运行分组和详细调试信息，帮助用户有效组织和管理实验。此外，Aim 提供内置转换器，方便从其他实验追踪工具（如TensorBoard、MLflow）迁移日志数据。Aim 的目标是让AI开发工具更普及。

data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary: 作者正在撰写一本名为《Refactoring English: Effective Writing for Software Developers》的书，为避免写完后无人购买，他通过Kickstarter进行了一个月的预售，目标是5000美元，否则项目将取消。在预售的大部分时间里，销售停滞，离目标还有2000美元差距，作者几乎以为项目失败。然而，最后他幸运地在Hacker News上发布的一篇文章带来了转机，成功达到了6000美元的预售额，超出目标。尽管起初通过邮件列表和博客宣传效果不佳，但最终通过再次利用之前受欢迎的文章实现了目标。
