data.title: My way to remove "Linuxisms" from FreeBSD
data.author: jaypatelani
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“Linuxisms”及其对不同操作系统的影响和兼容性问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [josephcsible的观点] 作为Linux用户，他并不喜欢“Linuxisms”，并认为这些特性应被称为“freedesktop-isms”，因为不仅仅是BSD用户不喜欢这些特性，Linux用户也同样可能不喜欢。这表明他希望这些特性与Linux系统本身有所区分，并归类为更广泛的自由桌面环境（freedesktop）范畴中的问题。

• [ggm的观点] 他认为目前正在努力消除“Waylandisms”并重新制作不依赖于Linux兼容性的软件包。他还指出，FreeBSD为了与现代Linux内核兼容，已经走了很长一段路，包括在FreeBSD内核中加入Linux兼容的ABI钩子，以便从供应商处导入针对Linux编写的驱动程序。这表明他支持通过兼容性措施来增强FreeBSD的功能，并认为这种做法在当前技术环境下是合理且必要的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：对“Linuxisms”的定义和命名存在争议。josephcsible认为应更名为“freedesktop-isms”，而ggm则关注FreeBSD通过兼容Linux ABI来增强功能，似乎默认接受了“Linuxisms”这一术语，且更关心实际的技术兼容性问题。

• 技术背景：讨论中提到的“Linuxisms”和“Waylandisms”指的是与Linux系统或Wayland显示服务器相关的特定实现或特性。这些特性在跨平台（如FreeBSD和Linux）兼容性上引发了不同用户的关注和争议。

• 实际影响：ggm提到了FreeBSD中为兼容Linux驱动所做的工作，表明这些兼容性措施对FreeBSD等系统获取更多硬件支持具有实际意义，而josephcsible则从用户体验角度表达了对这些特性潜在的不满。

data.title: Why America now eats a crazy number of avocados
data.author: fortran77
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： avocado产业的生产、消费和贸易，及其在美国市场的影响和争议。

不同观点：
• **[Animats]** 认为该文章像是一则广告，并指出加州今年的牛油果产量不错，去年因农业问题导致产量不佳。目前不需要进口牛油果，暗示市场需求被操控。

• **[alanh]** 对文章中的因果关系提出质疑，认为文章中的论述自相矛盾。文章一方面说牛油果在美国爆发性增长，另一方面又说是因为美国国内产量不足，需要进口来满足需求。

• **[ibejoeb]** 认为文章讲述了墨西哥牛油果在美国市场扩张的故事，尤其是墨西哥牛油果协会的大力推广。他指出，墨西哥和加州都能生产牛油果，但墨西哥的资源更为丰富，且美国的消费市场庞大，双方的贸易安排是互利的。

• **[latchkey]** 提出牛油果革命不仅仅是成熟技术的问题，还与品种有关。他比较了墨西哥/加州的牛油果与越南的不同品种，指出口感和形状的差异，并提到Haas和Booth两种不同品种的竞争。

• **[jb1991]** 指出欧洲市场的牛油果主要来自南美洲，如智利和秘鲁，且质量很好，质疑美国和墨西哥的市场主导地位。

• **[feverzsj]** 通过类比芬兰用生三文鱼吸引日本人，暗示牛油果在美国市场的推广也是一种市场策略。

• **[pajko]** 提供了一篇文章链接，讨论牛油果生产对环境的影响，暗示产业背后的环境代价。

• **[nailer]** 提到澳大利亚的一家餐厅在1990年代开始将牛油果和辣椒片放在烤酸面包上，可能推动了牛油果的流行。

• **[exodust]** 分享了一种牛油果的食用方法，展示了牛油果在饮食文化中的实际应用。

• **[ars]** 对美国政府在2000年代初建立的Hass牛油果销售收费项目表示不满，认为这是政府不当干预市场的行为，即使收费很少。

• **[levocardia]** 提到NAFTA（北美自由贸易协定）对美国牛油果市场的影响，认为这是自由贸易的胜利，但新的关税政策可能会导致双方都受损。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：文章的真实性和背后可能的商业利益，以及美国国内和进口牛油果市场的竞争关系。
- **讨论的另一个重要方面**：牛油果生产对环境的影响和政府政策在市场推广中的作用。
- **文化差异**：不同地区牛油果品种的差异及其在各地饮食文化中的应用。

data.title: Canoeing on the Danube
data.author: karagenit
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在多瑙河上划独木舟的建议和常见问题。多瑙河是欧洲第二长河，夏季常有人从德国至匈牙利进行划舟活动，还有每年一度的"多瑙河国际巡回赛"（TID），提供详细的行程和地图。划舟者可使用BIKELINE出版的多瑙河自行车道地图，但最后300公里需额外地图。划舟无需许可，但各国规则不同，如塞尔维亚需挂国旗，奥地利在水闸处需穿救生衣。多瑙河上有超过100个水坝，大多在德奥境内，TID提供详细行程和港口信息。遇到水坝时，通常需搬运独木舟，有些地方有滑道可利用。在塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的Djerdap I和II水坝可能遇到阻碍，需耐心沟通以通过。

43516117.article_content:
Travel and Lifestyle Writer with a focus on camping and the outdoors
Canoeing on the Danube: Advice & FAQs
CANOEING ON THE DANUBE
The Danube is Europe's second longest river and undergoes dramatic changes throughout its course. Though big, it is paddled fairly regularly each summer, particularly from Germany through to Hungary. There is also the organised
Tour International Danube
each year, a huge regatta where a large group paddle the entire length of the river. Their itinerary is extremely useful, outlining distances per day, the locations of locks and more. The 2017 itinerary can be found
here
. Below are probably just a few of your questions, so if you want to know more just get in touch through our
contact page
.
What maps did you use to canoe the Danube?
For the Danube we used the BIKELINE maps for the DANUBE CYCLE PATH (donauradweg) which come in a range of languages and can be ordered online. These maps cover the entire river and are a fantastic scale providing great detail. The maps also act as a concise guide book giving tid-bits of historic information along route. You need nothing more than these maps with the exception of the final 300kms of the Danube where the cycle path leaves the river in Romania. If you plan to canoe this section it is important to get another, up to date, map since the river here is awash with islands and difficult to navigate. To find such maps we suggest you contact
Tour International Danube
(TID)
who apparently provide specific maps for this section.
Do you need a river permit to canoe on the Danube?
No. The Danube is an international waterway and permits are not required. There are certain rules for individual countries that should be adhered to however. In Serbia national flags
must be flown (or an equivalent sticker on the canoe). In Austria life jackets must be worn at locks or dams (we strongly suggest you wear lifejackets the entire time, however. We did). In Germany you should have a boat name and address clearly marked on the vessel and should be affiliated with a canoeing body (for us membership of the British Canoe Union (BCU)).
Where are there dams on the river?
The Danube has more than 100 Dams with most in Germany and Austria, quickly petering out thereafter.  All of these dams and locks are well signposted and some have buoys that lead you to the river bank. The
Tour International Danube
publishes its annual itinerary which features all there camp points, along with all obstacles and locks including what bank you should pull in for portage (L or R) and what distance marker the Portage should begin. This information is accurate and definitely worth using, it can be found
here
on their 2017 PDF file.
N.B. On
TID
s itinerary for 15.07.17 in location named 'Cunovo' the description is to portage on the right bank to the old Danube river bed. This complicated section of the itinerary is deceiving, since there are really two options on the right hand side: You can go 'far right' or to a large dam that is on the right hand side but does not go all the way to the river-bank. It is for this dam you want to head and, once closer, you will find sign posts to help you with the portage. In short: at 1852 go right but head for the dam not for the river-bank, here there are signs for canoes.
How do I get around the dams?
There are a two ways around the locks. At most you must carry or wheel your canoe. There will be a ramp, or a series of steps which you can use. Sometimes there will be a trolley waiting there for you and you can wheel your canoe around the dam, and down to a similar dock on the far side of the dam. If there is no trolley, there might be one on the far side, so it could be worth a walk around to see.
On some dams there are shoots that you can slide down in your canoe. Sometimes you will see a bell and rope on the bank near one of these banks or a lever to pull. By ringing the bell you alert the control tower who will open the gate for you. Once this has lowered and the green light shows you can plummet down the ramp. If, like us, you find you are not canoeing during tourist season there may be no one there to operate the ramp. For this you can either carry around or (be cheeky) and go down the slide anyway even though theres not much water on it. but be careful because you don't want to get stuck!
The two locks in Serbia/Romania marked as Djerdap I and II are the only places you may have problems. The lock keepers do not want to deal with canoes and there is no sign posted set up here. We got shooed away from the lock on either side of the dam but eventually convinced the Romanian side to let us in with a cruise ship and go down in the lock. At the second we chatted and were slowed by countless members of authority but were eventually allowed to walk around and place our canoe back in the river on the other side. With these locks prepare for a long wait and a lot of talking, ultimately you have a right to be allowed passed.

43516117.article_summary: 本文介绍了在多瑙河上划独木舟的建议和常见问题。多瑙河是欧洲第二长河，夏季常有人从德国至匈牙利进行划舟活动，还有每年一度的"多瑙河国际巡回赛"（TID），提供详细的行程和地图。划舟者可使用BIKELINE出版的多瑙河自行车道地图，但最后300公里需额外地图。划舟无需许可，但各国规则不同，如塞尔维亚需挂国旗，奥地利在水闸处需穿救生衣。多瑙河上有超过100个水坝，大多在德奥境内，TID提供详细行程和港口信息。遇到水坝时，通常需搬运独木舟，有些地方有滑道可利用。在塞尔维亚和罗马尼亚的Djerdap I和II水坝可能遇到阻碍，需耐心沟通以通过。

data.title: Sales Compensation Simulator
data.author: seanlinehan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Exec的销售补偿模拟器，帮助用户通过调整不同的销售补偿方案来预测收入变化。主要功能包括设置基础薪资、目标佣金、佣金率、加速器设置等，并提供多种业绩情景模拟（如稳步提升、缓慢起步、大单周期等）。模拟器还显示总收入、年 quota、每月收入明细以及投资回报分析，帮助用户优化销售人员的业绩和补偿结构，以更快达到盈利目标。同时，文章还简要介绍了Exec的其他服务和联系方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：销售佣金计算系统的设计及其实施的简繁程度

不同观点：
• [ghiculescu] 认为佣金计算系统可以非常简单并具有可扩展性。他分享了自己的案例：销售人员根据成交类型获得1倍或2倍的月度经常性收入（MRR），而销售开发代表（SDRs）则根据完成的演示获得固定金额，该金额相当于0.75倍的典型客户MRR。他强调，这种简单的系统已经从不到100万美元的年度经常性收入（ARR）扩展到了比最初大100倍的规模。

• [tiffanyh] 对佣金率的输入方式提出了一个小异议。她指出，通常她看到的做法是将目标收入（Sales Target）作为输入，通过目标收入和佣金目标（Target Commission）的比值来确定佣金率（Commission Rate），而不是直接输入佣金率百分比。

• [gadders] 以讽刺的语气提出了一种不同的观点，暗示系统应该能够动态调整销售目标，特别是在销售人员接近达成目标时，以防止他们轻易获得佣金。这是一种对销售目标管理的动态调整思路。

补充讨论：
• 不同观点之间存在对系统设计简繁的争议。Ghiculescu强调简单化和可扩展性，而Tiffanyh则关注佣金率计算中的细节输入方式。Gadders的评论则带出了一种更加复杂的、动态调整销售目标的潜在需求。

• 争议的焦点在于佣金系统的设计是否应该简单直接，还是需要更复杂的机制来应对不同情况，比如动态调整目标以控制佣金支出。

data.title: Furry hackers who leaked Heritage Foundation data feared raided by feds
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 文章报道了曾隶属于黑客组织SiegedSec的成员声称其领导人vio遭遇联邦调查局（FBI）突袭，目前无法联系。该组织由“同性恋毛绒装爱好者黑客”组成，曾泄露右翼智库数据，并在去年解散。独立记者和另一名黑客证实了这一消息，但FBI拒绝置评。SiegedSec曾针对北约、以色列公司及反对跨性别权利的宗教组织进行黑客活动，并在曝光美国禁飞名单后引起关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对泄露帝国寡头数据事件的看法

不同观点：
• 支持泄密行为：
   - 认为泄露寡头数据是揭露腐败和不公正的必要手段。
   - 强调公众有权利知道这些信息，以促使社会变革。
   - 例子：历史上的泄密事件（如巴拿马文件）曾引发重要的政治改革。

• 反对泄密行为：
   - 认为这种行为违法，可能导致法律和安全问题。
   - 担心泄密可能引发社会不稳定或危及个人隐私。
   - 强调信息应该通过合法渠道公开，而不是通过黑客行为。

• 中立或复杂观点：
   - 承认泄密可能带来一些积极变化，但同时也可能造成负面影响。
   - 关注泄密信息的真实性和准确性，担心被误用或曲解。
   - 建议加强信息透明机制，通过合法途径公开重要数据。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于泄密行为的合法性与道德性之间的平衡。
- 讨论中涉及到信息透明与国家安全、个人隐私之间的矛盾。
- 有人提出应建立更完善的举报人保护机制，以鼓励合法揭露不当行为。

43542333.article_content:
The Trump administration acknowledged in a court
filing
Monday that it had grabbed a Maryland father with protected legal status and mistakenly deported him to El Salvador, but said that U.S. courts lack jurisdiction to order his return from the megaprison where he’s now locked up.
The case appears to be the first time the Trump administration has admitted to errors when it sent three planeloads of Salvadoran and Venezuelan deportees to El Salvador’s grim “Terrorism Confinement Center” on March 15. Attorneys for several Venezuelan deportees have said that the Trump administration falsely labeled their clients as gang members because of their tattoos. Trump officials have disputed those claims.
But in Monday’s court filing, attorneys for the government admitted that the Salvadoran man, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, was deported accidentally. “Although ICE was aware of his protection from removal to El Salvador, Abrego Garcia was removed to El Salvador because of an administrative error,” the government told the court. Trump lawyers said the court has no ability to bring him back now that Abrego Garcia is in Salvadoran custody.
Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, Abrego Garcia’s attorney, said he’s never seen a case in which the government knowingly deported someone who had already received protected legal status from an immigration judge. He is asking the court to order the Trump administration to ask for Abrego Garcia’s return and, if necessary, to withhold payment to the Salvadoran government, which says it’s charging the United States $6 million a year to jail U.S. deportees.
Trump administration attorneys told the court to dismiss the request on multiple grounds, including that Trump’s “primacy in foreign affairs” outweighs the interests of Abrego Garcia and his family.
“They claim that the court is powerless to order any relief,’’ Sandoval-Moshenberg told me. “If that’s true, the immigration laws are meaningless—all of them—because the government can deport whoever they want, wherever they want, whenever they want, and no court can do anything about it once it’s done.”
Court
filings
show Abrego Garcia came to the United States at age 16 in 2011 after fleeing gang threats in his native El Salvador. In 2019 he received a form of protected legal status known as “withholding of removal” from a U.S. immigration judge who found he would likely be targeted by gangs if deported back.
Abrego Garcia, who is married to a U.S. citizen and has a 5-year-old disabled child who is also a U.S. citizen, has no criminal record in the United States, according to his attorney. The Trump administration does not claim he has a criminal record, but called him a “danger to the community” and an active member of MS-13, the Salvadoran gang that Trump has declared a Foreign Terrorist Organization.
Sandoval-Moshenberg said those charges are false, and the gang label stems from a 2019 incident when Abrego Garcia and three other men were detained in a Home Depot parking lot by a police detective in Prince George’s County, Maryland. During questioning, one of the men told officers Abrego Garcia was a gang member, but the man offered no proof and police said they didn’t believe him, filings show. Police did not identify him as a gang member.
Abrego Garcia was not charged with a crime, but he was handed over to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement after the arrest to face deportation. In those proceedings, the government claimed that a reliable informant had identified him as a ranking member of MS-13. Abrego Garcia and his family hired an attorney and fought the government’s attempt to deport him. He received “withholding of removal” six months later, a protected status.
It is not a path to permanent U.S. residency, but it means the government won’t deport him back to his home country because he’s more likely than not to face harm there.
Abrego Garcia has had no contact with any law enforcement agency since his release, according to his attorney. He works full time as a union sheetmetal apprentice, has complied with requirements to check in annually with ICE, and cares for his five-year-old son, who has autism and a hearing defect, and is unable to communicate verbally.
On March 12 Abrego Garcia had picked up his son after work from the boy’s grandmother’s house when ICE officers stopped the car, saying his protected status had changed. Officers waited for Abrego Garcia’s wife to come to the scene and take care of the boy, then drove him away in handcuffs. Within two days he had been transferred to an ICE staging facility in Texas, along with other detainees the government was preparing to send to El Salvador. Trump had invoked the Alien Enemies Act of 1798, and the government planned to deport two planeloads of Venezuelans along with a separate group of Salvadorans.

43526058.article_content:
Why Is This Site Built With C
Created at: 2024-08-26
I've been writing about
things
on a personal website since
2017
.
Most of what I have written features in the category of notes-to-self. Mostly
on how to do A or B.
Only recently I've started polishing notes together and forming posts on
specific topics.
One thing I realised was preventing me of writing more frequently wasn't
the lack of ideas (or motivation), but the trouble of having to deal with
the website builder and platform I was using at the time.
GitHub pages didn't exist at the time and the canonical way was to have an
Apache server running the website in some web provider. I didn't know anything
about Apache and the little I saw didn't interest me, so I looked for an
alternative.
I built my first website with Django (serviced by Nginx) in a server hosted on
Digital Ocean. This is before the Droplets-era, so I had to rent an Ubuntu
machine which costed $5.00 USD per month. That was a bit steep for a dev on a
Brazilian salary considering I had to pay for other services too (registrar,
email, etc).
I was highly motivated to post things as I was still fresh in the web
development world and wanted to know how everything worked. I also had no idea
what I was doing and wanted my own website to be a sandbox where I could try
new things out.
That was my first mistake. Building a "static" website with Django is too
cumbersome. You have to set up views, templates, run the server, get GitHub
hooks for resetting the remote server in Digital Ocean when new commits are
pushed, etc.
Once the romantic view of a newbie blog-poster faded away, handling the whole
apparatus to publish a note took more time than writing the note itself.
At some point I had to make a switch before the website grew too big.
My second take was to ditch the whole website and start from scratch using
a static website generator. I decided to use Nuxt because I was using Vue at
work and the whole set up looked simple to start with.
It was nice in the beginning. I set it up with GitHub Pages. I only had to
get the static site that Nuxt creates via a cli command pushed to my git repo
and GitHub handled the rest for me. That was a major improvement over the
previous infrastructure. On top of that, I could do cool dynamic things with
JavaScript being embedded and having the framework to interact with it.
But I only had one blog post where I needed fancy JavaScript tooling. Soon it
became painful to maintain the website again. Publishing posts involved writing
things in Vue and that was just not an ergonomic way to write regular prose.
Also the framework was a new technology, and maintainers were pushing updates
that broke backwards compatibility. Handling versioning of Vue and Nuxt along
with all their JavaScript dependencies was a big pain point and I had to give
up at some point.
Now
Learning from these two past mistakes, I came up with a set of requirements for
my next (and hopefully final) website:
Starting a post must be as easy as typing into a blank file.
The website must be statically generated. And Fast.
There should be little to none dependencies for generating the website.
It needs to last for at least the next 10 years.
The first requirement is satisfied by writing using markdown files. Writing
this blog post in Neovim looks like this:
The second requirement is a bit trickier, but it is directly related to the
third.
Writing posts in markdown means that there needs to be a parser to convert the
files to html. I could either code this parser myself and have a beautiful
static site generator with zero dependencies, or I can allow myself a single
dependency.
The problem is that the move from zero dependencies to one dependency is huge.
It feels way bigger than going from 10 dependencies to 100 dependencies.
The problem is that writing a markdown parser isn't the most trivial
enterprise. At the same time, the parser was the only dependency I needed to
have. I managed to convince myself that a dependency was okay and then I moved
on.
My first instinct was to reach out to
Pandoc
. I did so
and implemented a small shell script that could read my directory tree of
markdown files and transpose them to html.
That worked fine for about 20 to 30 markdown files. After that, the process of
converting files to html started to deteriorate in speed. Pandoc is written in
Haskell, and it is not known for being fast at parsing large volumes of files.
An alternative for saving time with recompilation was to update my script so
that only new markdown files or changed ones are marked for recompilation. That
would involve too much wizardry if I wanted to make the script nice and robust.
I didn't want to do that. I didn't want my script to grow so much that I would
need to start adding test cases and coverage.
I also knew that parsing hundreds or even thousands of small files should be
doable in single-digit seconds. The problem was that Pandoc slowed everything
down, so my second requirement was not met.

data.title: Xfinity XB3 hardware mod: Disable WiFi and save 2 watts
data.author: p1mrx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种通过硬件修改来关闭Xfinity XB3（Arris TG1682P）路由器WiFi功能的方法，以节省功耗。背景提到，使用Xfinity NOW服务时必须使用该设备，且无法使用自己的调制解调器。尽管可以在桥接模式下操作，WiFi仍会广播隐藏SSID且无法关闭。作者通过拆解设备，找到一个TPS54328调节器的EN引脚，将其接地以关闭WiFi。修改后，设备功耗从14.9瓦降至12.5瓦，WiFi指示灯熄灭，有线以太网仍正常工作。需注意，该操作可能涉及电路风险，且设备使用的Intel Puma 6芯片组曾有延迟问题，但作者未遇到明显异常。

Xfinity XB3 hardware mod: Disable WiFi and save 2 watts
Raw
xb3_disable_wifi.md
Xfinity XB3 hardware mod: Disable WiFi and save 2 watts
Background
Comcast has a prepaid "Xfinity NOW" service that's cheaper than normal Xfinity, with unlimited data instead of a 1.2TB/month cap. If you currently have Xfinity, the NOW online signup is hidden, but when I called to cancel my Xfinity service on a date a couple weeks in the future, the NOW signup started working immediately. (I initially queried a neighbor's address to confirm that NOW was available in my area.)
The catch is that you can't use your own modem. They provide a free Arris TG1682P (also known as the XB3), but it's huge and uses more power (14.9 watts) than my Arris SB8200 (9.8 watts). I suspect they retired millions of these things and treat NOW as a recycling service.
The XB3 lets you enable bridge mode via the admin page at
http://10.0.0.1/
, and IPv4/IPv6 works just like a plain modem, but even in bridge mode, the gateway broadcasts several hidden SSIDs with no option to disable the radios.  Curiously I did not see an
xfinitywifi
broadcast, but your modem may vary.
The Hack
I found reversible hardware mod to disable the WiFi radios.
Refer to this
disassembly video
. There are 6 screws (2 hidden), lots of plastic prying, and you will probably wrinkle the rear sticker.
My circuit board is labeled TG1682/TG2472:
Notice the two shielded WiFi modules.  The shields just pop off but you can leave them on.  In between is an 8-pin chip labeled "54328", a
TPS54328 buck regulator
.  The output pins connect to various pins on both Atheros WiFi chips. Pin 1 is EN/enable. It measures 3.3 volts, and when I connect it directly to ground, it sinks negligible current.
So that's the mod. Connect Pin 1 on the 54328 to anything grounded.  I used the far side of this nearby capacitor:
The XB3's idle power consumption dropped from 14.9 watts to 12.5 watts, the WiFi lights are off, and everything else seems to work via wired ethernet.  I notice that
http://10.0.0.1/
is inaccessible (connection refused or HTTP 503) for a few minutes after booting, but it wakes up eventually.
Caveats
I don't actually know what circuit pulls up the EN pin, so it's possible that I'm overloading a digital output somewhere. I just measured amps to ground and saw a small number.  My first idea was to desolder/lift the pin, but I found that too difficult.
The XB3 uses an Intel Puma 6 chipset, which has been in the news over the years due to latency/jitter problems.  So far I'm not seeing anything weird on
https://gfblip.appspot.com/
or
https://speed.cloudflare.com/
.

主要讨论点：用户对语言学习工具的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• **文化偏好与界面设计**：[dataengineer56] 提到英语图标使用英国国旗（Union Jack）而不是美国国旗，让他对该服务评价更高。这反映出用户对文化细节的关注。
• **内容难度与提示设计**：[hobofan] 认为视频中的字幕让练习变得过于简单，因为答案几乎是直接给出的，降低了挑战性。
• **语言细分与自定义功能**：[philipjoubert] 建议细分西班牙语（西班牙与拉丁美洲），增加难度等级，并允许用户选择视频主题（如科学、名人八卦等）。这反映了对个性化学习体验的需求。
• **初学者友好性**：[CWIZO] 提到某些视频语速过快，不适合初学者，建议增加初学者模式。
• **语言扩展与用户需求**：[Caduceus1] 和其他用户（如[facile3232]）关注其他语言（如希腊语、普通话、斯瓦西里语）的加入时间，显示出对更多语言支持的期待。

补充讨论：
• **技术与界面问题**：[kstenerud] 提到在Firefox上按钮无响应，[anotherpaul] 则指出手机端拖放操作不便，导致错误评分。这反映了技术实现和用户体验方面的问题。
• **奖励与用户体验**：[mattsouth] 对完成示例后丢失积分表示失望，但总体上对工具的实用性给予了积极评价。
• **手动步骤与扩展性**：[black_puppydog] 询问是否有任何真正的手动步骤，特别是关于是否能扩展到其他语言的问题。
• **用户通知与设置清晰度**：[JackYoustra] 建议增加通知功能，以便在添加用户所需语言时获得通知。[vincvinc] 则建议在初始选择语言时更清晰地说明是母语还是目标学习语言，以减少用户困惑。

争议焦点：
• **评分准确性**：[mcjiggerlog] 提到在西班牙语练习中，2/5的视频评分不准确，这显示出工具在自动评分方面仍有改进空间。

总体而言，用户反馈集中在语言细分、个性化功能、初学者友好性、技术实现及扩展性等方面，同时对工具的整体设计与实用性给予了积极评价。

data.title: Show HN: Nue – Apps lighter than a React button
data.author: tipiirai
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Nue框架，它通过充分利用现代web标准（HTML、CSS、JS）实现极致性能。Nue应用比一个React按钮还轻量，并通过Rust计算引擎和事件溯源技术，实现对15万条数据瞬时操作，超越了JS引擎的极限。Nue在工具链上也表现出色，提供毫秒级反馈，支持VSCode/Sublime的实时更新。它呼吁Rust、Go和JS开发者摆脱React模式，采用模型优先、模块化设计，简化系统构建。同时，对设计和UX工程师而言，Nue提供更简单的CSS系统和更直接的用户体验控制。Nue旨在揭示并解决现代web开发中的复杂性问题，重建工具和框架，恢复开发乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新框架 Nue 的优缺点及与现有技术（如 React、Vue 等）的比较

不同观点：
• **fcpk 的观点**：Nue 试图解决当前 web 应用因大型框架导致的性能问题。他认为现代 web 应用依赖庞大的框架，导致页面加载速度极慢，尤其是在首次加载时。他支持 Nue 尝试简化这一问题，但对其能否改变现状持怀疑态度。

• **edweis 的观点**：对 Nue 的性能和创新性持谨慎态度。他质疑 Nue 是否真的比 React 性能更好，并希望看到代码示例及性能对比指标，以证明其优越性。他还提到 Nue 的设计灵感可能来自 Svelte，并希望了解其技术细节，如是否支持虚拟 DOM 或服务器端渲染。

• **davedx 的观点**：指出 Nue 的视图层类似于早期 Angular 2.0，且没有类型支持，可能更适合 Vue.js 开发者。他提到 Nue 的模型文件是纯 JavaScript，这可能不符合当前 React 开发者使用 TypeScript 的趋势。

• **n2d4 的观点**：希望在博客文章中首先看到代码示例，以便更好地理解新框架。

• **tipiirai 的观点**：作为 Nue 的开发者，他解释了 Nue 的设计目标是解决现代 web 开发中的臃肿问题，强调基于 web 标准，追求更简单、更高效的工作流。

• **dzonga 的观点**：认为 Inertia.js 是更合适的解决方案，它将 React 和 Vue 降级为纯视图层，简化了前后端的交互。

• **leonhard 的观点**：在 iOS Safari 上的体验不佳，滚动和布局存在问题，认为 Nue 在兼容性上还有待改进。

• **greg0r 的观点**：认为 Nue 对 React 的批评不公平，指出 React 库在应用中是复用的，因此不能简单地用单个按钮的大小来比较。

• **imiric 的观点**：赞赏 Nue 的 MVC 分离和现代 web 标准的使用，但也提到理想的框架应支持不转换为 JS 的纯 HTML 文件，并分享了自己正在实验的类似项目。

• **progx 的观点**：质疑 Nue 使用点击诱饵式的宣传方式。

• **mary-ext 的观点**：认为动画和缺乏节流/去抖动机制导致用户输入体验缓慢。

• **supermatt 的观点**：比较了 Nue 与 Preact 的文件大小，指出 Nue 在某些情况下并没有显著优势，且认为 Nue 的宣传对比不公平。

• **Garlef 的观点**：希望文档中的代码示例能更一致，并展示模型和视图如何连接。

• **gr__or 的观点**：认为 React 能有效地将 UI 和状态保持紧密联系，是前端开发的重大改进，对 Nue 提出的痛点感到陌生。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Nue 是否真的比现有的 React、Vue 等框架更轻量和高效，特别是其对 React 的批评是否公正。
• **技术细节**：Nue 的架构设计，如是否支持虚拟 DOM、服务器端渲染，及其与 Svelte 的相似性。
• **用户体验**：在不同浏览器上的兼容性问题及动画效果对用户体验的影响。
• **文档和示例**：开发者对代码示例和性能指标的需求，以便更好地理解和评估 Nue 的优势。

43543241.article_content:
On this release we're showing what you can do by taking the modern web standards — HTML, CSS, and JS — to their absolute peak:
The entire app is significantly lighter than a React button:
See benchmark and details
here ›
Going large-scale
Here’s the same app, now with a
Rust
computation engine and
Event Sourcing
for instant search and other operations over
150,000
records — far past where
JS-version
of the engine crashed with a maxium call stack exception:
Instant operations across 150.000 records with Rust/WASM
See this demo
live ›
Tooling
Nue crushes HMR and build speed records and sets you up with a millisecond feedback loop for your day-to-day VSCode/Sublime file-save operations:
Immediate feedback for design and component updates, preserving app state
Here's what this means:
For Rust, Go, and JS engineers
This is a wake-up call for Rust, Go, and JS engineers stuck wrestling with React idioms instead of leaning on timeless software patterns. Nue emphasizes a model-first approach, delivering modular design with simple, testable functions, true static typing, and minimal dependencies. Nue is a liberating experience for system devs whose skills can finally shine in a separated model layer.
For Design Engineers
This is a wake-up call for design engineers bogged down by React patterns and
40,000+ line
design systems. Build radically simpler systems with modern CSS (@layers, variables, calc()) and take control of your typography and whitespace.
For UX Engineers
This is a wake-up call for UX engineers tangled in React hooks and utility class walls instead of owning the user experience. Build apps as light as a React button to push the web—and your skills—forward.
FAQ: WTH is Nue?
Nue is a web framework focused on web standards, currently in active development. We aim to reveal the hidden complexity that’s become normalized in modern web development. When a single button outweighs an entire application, something’s fundamentally broken.
Nue drives the inevitable shift. We’re rebuilding tools and frameworks from the ground up with a cleaner, more robust architecture. Our goal is to restore the joy of web development for all key skill sets: frontend architects, design engineers, and UX engineers.

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了aiOla推出的最新ASR模型——Jargonic，该模型专为解决行业术语和噪音环境下的语音识别问题设计。Jargonic通过先进的领域自适应、实时上下文关键词检测和零样本学习，无需重新训练即可识别和适应特定行业的术语。其独特的双阶段架构将关键词检测与ASR结合，提高了对专业词汇的识别精度。此外，Jargonic采用专有的噪声处理方法，能在多语言环境下保持高准确性，并在多个性能基准测试中优于其他模型，如OpenAI Whisper、DeepGram等。Jargonic旨在实现企业级应用的高 robustness 和 precision。

主要讨论点：针对语音识别模型在处理未训练词汇时的表现以及相关技术方法的讨论。

不同观点：
• suchire 对 WER（词错误率）图表表示质疑，认为其效果差到令人感到可笑，暗示可能存在数据造假或严重缺陷。
• gronky_ 分享了使用模型后的惊奇体验，尤其是在输入完全虚构的词汇后，模型仍能准确识别。他认为这种能力违反直觉，因为通常认为模型需要音频样本才能识别未训练的词汇。他推测这是模型的跨模态识别能力（语音和文本之间）的涌现属性。
• FloatArtifact 关注关键词识别与语法或意图识别的比较，特别是在处理复杂短语作为命令时的表现，质疑关键词识别方法在处理复杂命令方面的有效性。
• four_fifths 试图总结技术机制，即通过在测试时提供词汇列表而非通过微调模型来处理未训练词汇。他提到这种方法的实用性取决于具体实现，例如可以处理的词汇量大小，并将其与 Whisper 模型进行比较。

补充讨论：
• htrp 提出一种假设，认为模型可能使用了某种高级语音合成技术（如 OpenAI 的 TTS 或类似技术）来生成波形并进行比对，以实现对未训练词汇的识别。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于模型在处理未训练词汇时表现出的超常能力是否真实，以及这种能力的技术实现机制是什么。部分用户对其效果感到惊讶和怀疑，并提出不同的技术假设。

Introducing Jargonic: The World’s Most Accurate Industry-Tuned ASR Model
April 1, 2025
Assaf Asbag
Introducing Jargonic: The World’s Most Accurate Industry-Tuned ASR Model
Introduction
Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has made significant strides over the last decade, but most ASR models on the market offer general-purpose transcription. They perform well in clean, controlled environments but break down when handling:
Technical jargon & acronyms
– Standard ASR models fail to recognize niche terminology used in most industries (i.e., medical terms, manufacturing terms, etc.).
Noisy industrial settings
– Background noise, overlapping speech, and other real-world conditions that degrade transcription quality.
Lack of real-time adaptability
– Most ASR models require extensive retraining to work effectively in new domains.
Jargonic, aiOla’s new foundation model for ASR, solves these issues through advanced domain adaptation, real-time contextual keyword spotting, and zero-shot learning, allowing it to handle industry-specific language out-of-the-box and allow real-world enterprise deployment.
How Jargonic Works
Jargonic leverages a state-of-the-art ASR architecture, designed for enterprise-scale applications, ensuring superior robustness and precision, especially with specialized industry vocabulary.
Instead of relying on extensive fine-tuning, Jargonic employs a
context-aware adaptive learning mechanism
that allows it to recognize domain-specific terminology without retraining. The jargon terms are detected by a proprietary keyword spotting (KWS) mechanism that is deeply integrated into the ASR architecture. Unlike standard ASR models that require manually curated vocabulary lists, Jargonic learns and auto-adapts to industry-specific terminology through its inference pipeline. That is, the keyword does not need to be given acoustically, and no further training or fine-tuning is needed for introducing the system with new keywords (e.g., jargon terms).
Combining Keyword Spotting with ASR
Jargonic’s approach integrates a proprietary KWS mechanism with advanced speech recognition in a two-stage architecture. First, the proprietary KWS system identifies the presence of domain-specific terms within the audio stream. Then, this contextual information is fed into the core ASR engine through an adaptive layer, effectively steering the model’s generation towards the relevant domain context.
This architecture allows Jargonic to achieve superior accuracy for general speech while also handling specialized vocabulary recognition. The KWS system is zero-shot and can be instantly reconfigured for different industry vocabularies by simply providing a new list of keywords, enabling flexibility across any domain with heavily jargonized speech. Through this approach, Jargonic improves overall accuracy for audio samples containing industry-specific terms while eliminating the resource-intensive retraining typically required for domain adaptation.
Innovative Noise Robustness for Multilingual Speech Recognition
Jargonic was trained using a proprietary noise-handling approach that works independently across languages. Unlike conventional approaches, we developed a specialized data enrichment process that utilizes various types of industrial noise under different conditions – both with and without speech present. This method is language-independent, allowing our model to maintain consistent performance regardless of which language is being processed. Traditional noise robustness techniques often add basic white noise or reverberation patterns primarily optimized for English, which can negatively impact the model’s ability to generalize performance improvements when processing other languages like Japanese or German. Our approach avoids this limitation by using real-world noise profiles from industrial settings and a pipeline that generalizes effectively across our entire language suite, ensuring reliable transcription even in the challenging acoustic environments found in manufacturing floor settings, for example.
Performance Benchmarks
The graphs compare the performance of Jargonic V2 against OpenAI Whisper (v3), DeepGram, AssemblyAI, and ElevenLabs across multiple languages. One figure illustrates the Word Error Rate (WER), where lower values indicate better performance, while the other shows Recall on jargon terms, where higher values are preferred. Overall, Jargonic V2 achieves superior WER across most languages and datasets, and it consistently outperforms all other models in keyword detection and transcription.
Jargonic V2
achieves strong results even without the keyword spotting mechanisms. Figure 3 presents the results for the English language across various English datasets. It shows that, in most cases, Jargonic V2  outperforms competitors, demonstrating superior performance in the majority of test cases and maintaining the highest average performance across all benchmarks.

data.title: 'A hostile state': Why some travellers are avoiding the US
data.author: isaacfrond
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了由于美国实施更严格的边境政策和与其他国家的关系紧张，一些国际旅客，特别是加拿大人，正选择避免前往美国。美国对长期盟友加征关税及加强移民管控，导致加拿大、德国、英国、丹麦、芬兰和葡萄牙等国发布旅行警告。加拿大的访美人数显著下降，2月份过境人数减少超过20%。一些旅客表示因政策变化和对边境安全担忧而取消美国旅行计划。有加拿大人选择转向墨西哥、南美和欧洲等目的地。美国旅游业因此可能面临经济损失，而其他国家的旅游业则从中受益。文章还提到，这种趋势正值美国旅游业本应经历创纪录增长的时期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国人旅行限制及相关政策影响的讨论

不同观点：
• pcthrowaway：在加拿大的Burning Man讨论组中，共识是由于关税战争以及对非营利组织的不满，今年几乎没人会去参加。很多人在讨论中取消了旅行计划，表明人们在度假方式上发生了变化。

'A hostile state': Why some travellers are avoiding the US
20 hours ago
Share

Lindsey Galloway

Getty Images
(Credit: Getty Images)
As the list of nations issuing travel warnings to the US grows, some visitors are opting to boycott it entirely. Here's why many foreigners are changing their travel plans and what this could mean for Americans.
As President Donald Trump implements
sweeping new policies
, issues
tariffs on longtime allies
and leads an
immigration crackdown
, some international travellers are rethinking their travel plans to the US.
The nation's stricter border enforcement has recently led to the
detention of Canadian and European tourists
, prompting
Germany
,
the UK
,
Denmark, Finland
and
Portugal
to issue travel warnings and advisories for the country. Now, it appears that a growing number of voices are advocating for an all-out
boycott of travel to the US
.
The cold shoulder has been particularly noticeable from the US's northern neighbour, Canada, which sends more than
20 million visitors
to the country per year – more than any other nation. In response to Trump's proposed
tariffs
and repeated threats to
annex the nation
, former prime minister Justin Trudeau recently urged his fellow Canadians: "Now is the time to choose Canada," adding, "it might mean changing your summer vacation plans to stay here in Canada."
Alamy
Justin Trudeau recently urged Canadians to stay in Canada instead of travelling to the US (Credit: Alamy)
The appeal seems to have caught on, as many infuriated Canadians are now
boycotting US holidays
. In February, border crossings were down by more than 20%,
according to Statistics Canada
. The US Travel Association estimates that even a 10% reduction in Canadian visitors could result in $2.1bn in lost spending and 14,000 job losses.
While some Canadians are snubbing the US because of policy changes, others say they simply don't feel as safe as they once did.
"My partner and I decided not to go ahead with our planned vacations to the US this year," said Canadian travel journalist Kate Dingwall. "I worry about the border and getting stuck somehow, especially with how prickly Trump is to Canada. There's just a sense of uneasiness around visiting America at the moment."
Keith Serry, a writer and comedian based in Montreal, Quebec, cancelled five April appearances in New York City (including four shows at the upcoming
New York City Fringe
festival) due to the tense political situation.
"This decision will, of course, rob me of the opportunity to share my art with many of you in New York I've grown to know and love," he wrote on his
Facebook page
. "That said, the honest truth is that I just don't feel safe travelling to the States right now. In addition, I feel a powerful disinclination to spending my money in any way that might aid the economy of a hostile state."
Alamy
Some international travellers have been inexplicably detained by US officials (Credit: Alamy)
In recent months, some Canadians have faced tougher border security than ever before – even those with clean records and valid documents. One woman made international headlines as
she was detained by ICE for two weeks
in reportedly bleak conditions after her visa was revoked.
"We're a country that prides itself, imperfectly but intentionally, on values like inclusion, equity and human rights. When those values feel out of step with what's happening across the border, it becomes harder to justify participation," said Amar Charles Marouf, a Canadian citizen who works as a curator at the
World Economic Forum
. "The political climate raises broader questions. What kind of treatment are we normalising? What assumptions are being made about who is welcome and who isn’t?"
It's not that Canadians aren't traveling internationally; many are simply swapping their traditional destinations. Marouf says Mexico, South America and Europe all feel more welcoming at the moment. "California will be there when this is all over, but I just feel like there's less risk going to Portugal instead," added Dingwall.
Some international properties have seen a bump in traffic, directly attributable to Canadians now spurning the US. "In the last several weeks, we've received 10-plus leads from Canadians seeking to relocate events from the United States this summer," said Diarmaid O'Sullivan, director of sales & marketing at
Hamilton Princess Hotel & Beach Club Bermuda
. "This is a mix of leisure travellers, including those planning weddings, and companies relocating business events. This represents an approximately 20% increase in forecasted revenue from the Canadian market."
Alamy
Ironically, the US had recently been touted as the world's top tourism market (Credit: Alamy)

data.title: Interview with the Creator of Deluxe Ski Jump
data.author: Kolorabi
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了芬兰游戏开发者Jussi Koskela及其经典游戏《Deluxe Ski Jump》的开发故事。Koskela自幼开始制作游戏，第一款商用游戏《Fatal Fumes》并未取得商业成功，但为他积累了经验。随后，他利用三个月的时间在高中毕业后入伍前开发了《Deluxe Ski Jump》。该游戏通过创新的鼠标控制和逼真的跳跃感受，成功模拟了滑雪跳跃的飞行体验，成为经典。Koskela强调，游戏成功的关键在于让玩家感受到真实的飞行体验，控制方式让玩家仿佛身临其境。文章还回顾了其他早期滑雪跳跃游戏，如《Four Hills》和《The Games: Winter Challenge》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕经典跳台滑雪游戏（主要是DSJ，即Deluxe Ski Jump）的怀旧讨论，涉及游戏体验、技术问题、文化影响以及对健康的影响。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与文化影响] pawelduda提到DSJ在波兰非常流行，尤其是在Adam Małysz成名期间，游戏甚至与当时的文化现象（如"Małysz"恶意软件）相关联。p0w3n3d也认同波兰对该游戏的热情，指出Małysz是当时的英雄，游戏因此得名。
• [技术与游戏体验] pawelduda分享了在老旧硬件（100 MHz CPU）上运行游戏的经历，通过"turbo"按钮短暂加速，但最终系统崩溃。fear91则指出，较差的电脑配置反而提升了游戏表现，因为慢速帮助更好地把握跳跃时机。
• [现代平台体验] moritz提到DSJ2已经在手机上可用，但体验仍不及鼠标操作的原版。SteelByte则从开发角度赞赏了DSJ，强调了其技术成就和独立开发者的努力。

43505340.article_content:
Jussi Koskela tells us the secret behind the game’s unique feeling of flying.
This is a complicated time for ski jumping in Norway. Interest has been declining for years, with plenty of negative press, and it all peaked recently with the disappointing revelations of widespread suit cheating among Norwegian jumpers. But perhaps we can use this rough patch to reminisce about truly great ski jumping experiences — experiences that, of course, took place in front of a screen.
Deluxe Ski Jump developer Jussi Koskela’s ski-jumping toy that you can see at the Finnish Museum of Games (Photo: Jussi Koskela)
There have been several games that have given us varying degrees of that wonderful feeling of lift. Growing up, I mostly stared into a screen powered by MS-DOS, and I’m guessing that most of us DOS folks have at some point played The Games: Winter Challenge. It offered a variety of winter sports activities, but let’s be honest — ski jumping was the only fun one. It was incredibly frustrating, though, that it was impossible to land jumps where you actually timed the take-off perfectly.
Back when the New Year’s competition in Garmisch-Partenkirchen felt more important than New Year’s Eve, I was thrilled to discover a little game called Four Hills by Jukka Hakosalo. It let me take part in the whole Four Hills Tournament, competing against legends like Bredesen and Goldberger. The game was very simple, but sometimes it doesn’t take much to be entertained.
But everything changed the year we discovered Deluxe Ski Jump. It was the game we’d been waiting for all along. At last, the ultimate ski jumping game had arrived. We had a chat with the man who gave us this gift more than 25 years ago.
First of all—who are you?
I’m Jussi Koskela, a 45-year-old solo game developer from Finland, and I’ve been working on the Deluxe Ski Jump games since 1999.
Jussi Koskela at the Pixel Heaven 2024 in Warsaw together with DSJ2 players. (Photo: Jussi Koskela)
How did you get started with game development?
I started making little games already as a child. When I was 9, I wrote my first «game», where the goal was to kill a giant spider by swinging a sword at the right time. You just had to press F1 once to win the game.
Later, my games grew in complexity and size little by little. I sold my first game when I was 12, to a friend who was 7. I think he was mostly interested in the source code…
Can you tell us about your first commercial game, Fatal Fumes?
Fatal Fumes is a top-down racing game I developed as a hobby project in my teens. My brother helped me a bit with the physics, and a friend contributed the music. We also built the tracks together.
For me, Fatal Fumes was mostly a learning project, since it was my first full-scale game. Programming was very different back then because there were no ready-made libraries for sound or graphics, so you had to code everything from scratch. The biggest challenge was getting the game to run smoothly at 70 FPS. I also struggled a bit with implementing CPU opponents who could drive well enough.
Of course, we dreamed of big sales, but Fatal Fumes never became a commercial success. Still, I was very proud that the game’s demo was included on the cover disks of PC Gamer and PC Format magazines in the UK.
Fatal Fumes. Image: Mobygames.
My friends and I played Slicks ’n’ Slide a lot, and it was definitely an inspiration for our racing game. Fatal Fumes aimed to be something similar, but with larger tracks that spanned multiple screens. The charm of Slicks ’n’ Slide was always the multiplayer mode on a shared keyboard, but that didn’t work so well in Fatal Fumes, since I never managed to implement proper split-screen.
How did you end up making a new ski jumping simulator?
I had been experimenting with side-scrolling graphics that gave an effective 3D feel. It was originally meant for a platformer, but at some point, it reminded me of a ski jumping hill. I felt that other ski jumping games at the time had very simplistic physics and didn’t really capture the feeling of flight, so I decided to give it a go myself.
What were the biggest challenges you faced?
The biggest challenge was time. I only had three months off after high school before starting military service, and I finished the game just one day before I had to report in!
Technically, the hardest part was making the hills and environments look believable using my «fake» 3D graphics. The actual simulation part was mostly basic high school physics. I never took any programming courses in high school, so experience and code snippets from earlier projects were invaluable.
The most important factor in the game’s success was making the jumping feel fantastic—and I spent a lot of time on that. I think the biggest innovation was how the mouse controls were mapped to the jumper’s movements. It made players respond with their whole bodies, as if they were ski jumpers themselves.
Original Deluxe Ski Jump. Image: Mobygames.

data.title: LLM providers on the cusp of an 'extinction' phase as capex realities bite
data.author: abawany
data.article_summary: 文章指出，大型语言模型（LLM）提供商正面临资本支出压力，可能进入"灭绝"阶段。Gartner预测，到2025年，全球生成型AI支出将达6440亿美元，但LLM市场将经历类似云市场的整合，最终仅剩少数强者。当前，市场无法支持现有数量的模型提供商，企业更倾向于使用现成的商业解决方案而非自行开发。尽管AI市场将快速增长，但不会像 dotcom 时代那样迅速崩溃，而是一个逐步淘汰的过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕生成式AI技术的成本、盈利前景、技术选择以及市场策略的讨论。

不同观点：
• **成本透明性与实际价值**：[iteratethis] 认为，如果在线LLM能够显示实时功耗和实际美元成本，将有助于理解技术的补贴程度和实际的价值/成本比率。他引用了生成一张AI图片耗电相当于充满一部智能手机的例子，并质疑如果成本过高，当前的扩展是否可持续。

• **盈利能力与商业化策略**：[DebtDeflation] 提出，Google可能已经分析过训练大型Transformer模型的成本，并认为无法实现盈利，因此选择不急于商业化。

• **广告与市场竞争**：[ConSeannery] 预测广告将进入LLM的响应或侧边栏，并讨论谁会首先采用这种模式，以及谁会坚持不使用广告支持的LLM。

• **市场规模与泡沫**：[throwup238] 对全球生成式AI支出将在2025年达到6440亿美元的预测表示怀疑，并质疑这一数字与所谓的“灭绝阶段”是否相符。

• **硬件技术与发展趋势**：[Havoc] 认为GPU与TPU以及其他NPU技术的发展路径值得关注，并提到Sambanova、Cerebras、GROQ等公司。

• **运营成本与财务分析**：[meltyness] 指出讨论中提到的成本可能更多是运营成本（OPEX）而非贷款支付。

• **历史对比与投资周期**：[PeterStuer] 通过对比亚马逊的例子，指出可能需要多年才能实现盈利，即使在重大投资后仍可能出现亏损。

• **市场竞争与策略激进性**：[isoprophlex] 认为OpenAI采取了一种不关心安全和知识产权的态度，并引用Altman的言论，认为这是一种在市场泡沫破裂前的快速扩张策略。

• **AI性能与用户体验**：[DonHopkins] 提到不同LLM在不同时间段的表现差异，并幽默地建议创建一个监测AI愚蠢程度的网站。

• **技术 commoditization 与成本选择**：[siscia] 认为LLM技术已经 commoditization，选择模型时最重要的是成本，而非性能差异。

补充讨论：
• **价值与成本的平衡**：[seydor] 提出了一个开放性问题，即如果选择更便宜的模型，会失去多少价值。

争议焦点：
• **生成式AI技术的实际成本与盈利前景**：各方对生成式AI技术的成本、盈利能力和市场策略存在不同看法，部分人认为成本过高无法盈利，而另一些人则认为可以通过规模化或广告模式实现盈利。

• **技术选择的优先级**：部分评论者认为不同模型之间的性能差异不大，选择时应以成本为主要考虑因素，而其他人则关注硬件技术的发展和性能表现。

43543429.article_content:
AI + ML
27
LLM providers on the cusp of an 'extinction' phase as capex realities bite
27
Only the strong will survive, but analyst says cull will not be as rapid as during dotcom era
Lindsay Clark
Mon 31 Mar 2025
//
14:32 UTC
Gartner says the market for large language model (LLM) providers is on the cusp of an extinction phase as it grapples with the capital-intensive costs of building products in a competitive market.
Adoption right now is the most important thing: speed, adoption, being in the market – there is extinction coming. The market will not be able to support this number of model providers that we currently have
As the global tech research company forecasts worldwide generative AI (GenAI) spending will reach $644 billion in 2025, up around 76 percent from 2024, John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, said the market for model providers would see a similar consolidation to that of the cloud market, which is currently dominated by AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.
"Cloud was more transformational in one sense, [it] changed how we did and what we did and where we did it," Lovelock said. "But it was a replacement. I had to change from using my on-premises CRM system to move to a cloud-based system like Salesforce. GenAI comes in and adds to whatever it is you're running, and it will be part of every mobile phone, every PC, every laptop, every server, every piece of software, it will be in your car, your TV, and your watch."
Meanwhile, CIOs are set to opt for commercial-off-the-shelf solutions for more predictable implementation and business value, rather than building their own software around AI, he said.
"Despite model improvements, CIOs will reduce [proof of concept] and self-development efforts, focusing instead on GenAI features from existing software providers," said Lovelock.
As a result, LLM developers are currently chasing adoption among users, businesses, and software vendors as a higher priority than revenue or costs.
You know that generative AI browser assistant extension is probably beaming everything to the cloud, right?
AI agents swarm Microsoft Security Copilot
A closer look at Dynamo, Nvidia's 'operating system' for AI inference
Cloudflare builds an AI to lead AI scraper bots into a horrible maze of junk content
"Adoption right now is the most important thing: speed, adoption, being in the market – there is extinction coming. The market will not be able to support this number of model providers that we currently have. From the capital expenditure requirements through to revenue, the cloud market only bears three and you expect the same with GenAI model developers," he said.
However, the market was unlikely to see a rapid collapse along the lines of the dotcom crash, partly because that also came on the back of Y2K spending. "We're not going to wake up one morning and find 20 companies out of business. It will be a slower pruning."
AI services are set for the most rapid growth in the market, Gartner said, climbing from $10.6 billion in 2024 to $27.8 billion in 2025, a 163 percent increase. While devices and software-based GenAI were both set to nearly double, the server-based market for GenAI would see the slowest growth at 33.1 percent to reach $180 billion. ®

data.title: AI was enemy No. 1 during Hollywood strikes. Now it's in Oscar-winning films
data.author: jeffwass
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了好莱坞对人工智能（AI）技术的逐渐接纳及其引发的争议。两年前的罢工曾抗议AI对演员和编剧的威胁，但如今AI已悄然进入影视和游戏行业，甚至被用于奥斯卡获奖影片中，如修改声音和减龄演员。尽管AI技术受到批评，尤其是未经同意使用版权材料构建模型，但一些业内人士认为AI在好莱坞的应用是“不可避免的”，并强调艺术家应参与技术开发以保护自身利益。AI有望降低制作成本，可能催生新的天才导演，但也引发对工作岗位被取代的担忧。技术公司如OpenAI正大力投资AI工具，而好莱坞对此态度复杂，既好奇又谨慎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在影视行业中的应用及其对演员技能和行业标准的潜在影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：AI在影视中的应用会降低对演员专业技能的要求。aucisson_masque认为，如果AI能够精细调整口音、情感表达和语音语调，那么任何人都可以成为演员。这可能导致行业更加注重演员的外形而非演技，进一步削弱对专业表演能力的要求。

• 观点二：AI技术的使用可以提升影视作品的质量。例子包括《Emilia Perez》和《The Brutalist》等奥斯卡提名影片使用AI调整声音，以及Adrian Brody在《The Brutalist》中借助AI完善匈牙利口音并获得奥斯卡最佳男主角奖。这些例子显示AI技术能够辅助演员创造更真实的角色形象。

• 观点三：AI在演员外貌上的应用，比如让Tom Hanks和Harrison Ford等演员“减龄”，可能导致行业更加注重演员的外在形象。aucisson_masque担心这种趋势会使得外貌成为主要标准，而不是演技。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI技术的使用是否会削弱演员的专业性。一方面，AI可能使更多人凭借外形和技术辅助进入影视行业；另一方面，AI也能提升作品的艺术质量和真实性。
• AI在行业中的角色逐渐增强，可能改变传统的演员选拔和表演标准，这引发了对未来演员职业要求的讨论和担忧。

Image caption,
Countless signs during the historic Hollywood strikes decried using AI. It's now creeping further into the entertainment industry
Regan Morris
BBC News, Los Angeles
Published
31 March 2025
Inside a soundstage once used by silent film stars Charlie Chaplin and Mabel Normand, Hollywood executives, actors and filmmakers sipped cocktails as they marvelled at what some say is the biggest breakthrough since the talkies: AI-generated video.
But whether AI will be the future, or the end, of cinema is still up for debate.
It was only two years ago that actors and writers shut down Hollywood with strikes
demanding protections from AI
. Now the technology is controversially creeping into TV, movies and video games. Two films honoured at the Oscars even used the technology.
As a DJ played '90s hip hop, computer developers rubbed shoulders with actors and executives, in a sign of the changing power players in the industry.
AI in Hollywood is "inevitable", says Bryn Mooser, the party's host and the co-founder of Moonvalley, which created the AI generator tool Marey by paying for footage from filmmakers with their consent. Mooser says that while AI may still be a dirty word, their product is "clean" because it pays for its content.
Image source,
Courtesy of Joelle Grace Taylor for Asteria
Image caption,
Filmmakers, executives and actors rubbed shoulders at the new AI production company
"Artists should be at the table," he says, adding that it's better to build the tool for filmmakers rather than get "rolled over by big tech companies".
Artificial Intelligence has long been depicted as a villain in Hollywood. In The Terminator, AI used by the US military decides it must destroy everyone on earth.
But it's AI's creators, and not the technology itself, that has received the brunt of real-life criticism. Companies use publicly available data to build their AI models - which includes copyrighted material shared online - and creators say they're being ripped off.
OpenAI, Google and other tech companies are facing multiple lawsuits from writers, actors and news organisations, alleging their work was stolen to train AI without their consent. Studios like Paramount, Disney and Universal who own the copyright on movies and TV shows have been urged by writers to do the same, though none have taken legal action.
"We've all fought very hard for copyright laws, and nobody wants to see their work stolen to have somebody else profit from it," Mooser says.
Hollywood has begun toying with the new technology. The Oscar-nominated films Emilia Perez and The Brutalist used AI to alter voices. Adrian Brody won the Academy Award for best actor, even with the help of AI to fine tune his accent when he spoke Hungarian in his starring role in The Brutalist. AI has even been used to de-age actors like Tom Hanks and Harrison Ford.
Image source,
Getty Images
Image caption,
Generative AI was used to fine tune Adrian Brody's accent when he spoke Hungarian in The Brutalist
The technology is seemingly everywhere. OpenAI hosted an AI film festival in Los Angeles earlier this month. Marvel directors Joe and Anthony Russo told the Wall Street Journal they plan to invest $400 million to craft AI tools for filmmakers.
But the impacts on how it will alter the future of the entertainment industry remain unclear. Generative AI, for instance, allows computers to learn and solve problems in ways that can seem human â albeit much faster. And many worry about the technology replacing their jobs as AI is used to generate scripts, animation, locations, voices and human actors.
If you ask OpenAI's popular chatbot, ChatGPT, which Hollywood jobs are most easily replaced by AI, background actors are top of the list as "most vulnerable" with "A-List actors & directors" considered safest because "star power and brand recognition keep top talent irreplaceable".
At the Moonvalley party, everyone was talking about new AI technology though few wanted to speak with a reporter on record about it. But dozens of powerful people made the trek east to the hip Silver Lake neighbourhood from west Los Angeles, even though it was raining. In LA, that's remarkable.
"We're here to learn," said one executive who spent an hour in traffic getting to the party. "We're not signing anything or buying anything, but we're interested."
Mooser and his co-founder Naeem Talukdar speak passionately about how AI will transform Hollywood and allow filmmakers to create blockbuster style epics on much lower budgets. It could lead to many bad films - but it could also help discover the next Quentin Tarantino or Martin Scorsese, even if they don't have the backing of a big studio.
"This technology is utterly meaningless without the artist at the centre of it; the technology needs to ultimately be subservient to the artist," says Talukdar.
Image source,
Getty Images
Image caption,
Arnold Schwarzenneger played a murderous AI in the Terminator
Hollywood's foray into us
43543625.article_summary: 本文讨论了好莱坞对人工智能（AI）技术的逐渐接纳及其引发的争议。两年前的罢工曾抗议AI对演员和编剧的威胁，但如今AI已悄然进入影视和游戏行业，甚至被用于奥斯卡获奖影片中，如修改声音和减龄演员。尽管AI技术受到批评，尤其是未经同意使用版权材料构建模型，但一些业内人士认为AI在好莱坞的应用是“不可避免的”，并强调艺术家应参与技术开发以保护自身利益。AI有望降低制作成本，可能催生新的天才导演，但也引发对工作岗位被取代的担忧。技术公司如OpenAI正大力投资AI工具，而好莱坞对此态度复杂，既好奇又谨慎。

主要讨论点：Android应用权限、隐私问题及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• **关于Android权限漏洞的讨论**：
  - [captn3m0] 提到 Android 的 ACTION_MAIN 漏洞之前已经被写过，但 Google 拒绝修补。他质疑如果将此问题提交给Android的漏洞奖励计划（VDP），是否会被视为权限绕过。
  - [nindalf] 指出某些应用（如Tamil Calendar、Qibla Direction Finder等）通过特定应用判断用户种族和宗教，进行用户画像，质疑其必要性。
  - [graemep] 提到 HSBC 应用会检查手机上的其他应用，如果存在具有特定权限的应用（如替代启动器）或非Google应用商店的应用，则拒绝运行。

• **对原生App和WebApp的看法**：
  - [turblety] 认为大多数App都可以被网站或WebApp替代，原生App的优势仅在于能获取更多用户隐私信息，且App商店是Apple和Google为牟利而引入的不必要概念。
  - 相比之下，Web浏览器无需费用，且具备较好的沙盒机制，更具开放性。

• **技术解决方案和讨论**：
  - [Tmpod] 提出可以使用LSPosed模块（如XPrivacyLua）来阻止或伪造应用权限检查，并提到AppOps作为另一种选择。
  - [zx8080] 质疑浏览器为何需要枚举已安装应用，认为这种权限不合理。
  - [andsoitis] 指出Android存在隐私缺陷，而iPhone没有这种问题。

• **对特定应用和权限的批评**：
  - [hnburnsy] 批评Google允许某些应用（如银行应用、相机应用等）拥有QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES权限，认为这些权限过度。
  - [surmoi] 提到Exodus Privacy可以帮助识别应避免安装的Android应用，指出Swiggy在请求权限方面相对较少，而其他应用（如Weibo、Wechat等）请求更多权限且不值得信任。

补充讨论：
• **对社区和讨论平台的看法**：
  - [aucisson_masque] 认为Hacker News上的讨论质量较高，而Reddit的某些子版块（如r/android）则质量低下。

• **对Windows应用权限的讨论**：
  - [cheschire] 提出Windows应用是否可以枚举所有打开窗口的标题，并质疑这种技术在现实世界中的可行性。

争议焦点：
• **Android应用权限的合理性**：
  - 一部分用户认为某些应用请求的权限不合理且过度，尤其是涉及隐私信息的权限（如QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES）。
  - 另一部分用户则讨论了技术上的解决方案，如使用LSPosed和AppOps来阻止或伪造权限检查。

总结：
评论主要围绕Android应用权限、隐私问题展开，涉及漏洞、权限合理性、原生App与WebApp的比较、技术解决方案及社区讨论质量等多方面。争议的核心在于Android应用权限的合理性及隐私保护问题。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了申请遗失牙齿经济补偿的服务。如果牙齿因意外吞咽、被雪貂偷走或被小行星摧毁等原因无法被牙仙收取，可以通过该服务申请补偿。申请人可以直接开始申请，也可以打印并填写TF-230表格，然后放在枕头下提交。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个伪装成政府服务的牙齿仙女索赔网站的评论，用户们讨论了该网站的功能、使用体验、系统设计以及其与真实或虚构情境的关系。

不同观点：
• 一些用户如[matteason]和[NooneAtAll3]提到了网站的制作背景和设计意图，强调了其模仿英国政府网站风格的细节，并分享了实际使用效果，如成功骗过孩子。
• [silisili]分享了一个与牙齿丢失相关的童年糗事，借此表达对网站的兴趣，并提及自己对牙齿仙女虚构性质的早期察觉。
• [Lio]以幽默的方式表达了对可能因虚假申报而受到法律惩罚的担忧，暗示了网站的趣味性和用户对其虚构性质的认知。
• [amluto]对网站中牙齿类型标注的准确性提出了疑问，建议增加区分乳牙和恒牙的功能。
• [thih9]支持网站中允许申报智齿的设计，认为成年人也应有机会使用该网站。
• [pavel_lishin]分享了自己为了安抚孩子编造的“下水道美人鱼”故事，与网站的虚构性质形成呼应。

补充讨论：
• 技术性讨论：[ascorbic]关注了网站字体和设计系统的合规性，而[blatantly]则以调侃的方式指出了网站缺少政府服务常见的认证步骤。
• 功能建议：[gwern]建议在牙齿计数中增加序数以提高准确性，[benwerd]则以幽默的方式提到了一个虚构的社会问题——偷牙鼬。
• 语言问题：[Willingham]建议将"rubber"改为"eraser"以帮助更多英语儿童理解内容。

争议的焦点：
• 网站的真实性与虚构性质之间的界限，以及用户对网站法律效力的调侃式担忧。

data.title: Public secrets exposure leads to supply chain attack on GitHub CodeQL
data.author: cyberbender
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了GitHub CodeQL潜在供应链攻击的发现过程。攻击始于一个公开暴露的秘密，有效期仅1.022秒，但足以让攻击者在大多数使用CodeQL的仓库中执行代码。攻击可能导致：

1. 泄露私有仓库的源代码，损害知识产权。
2. 窃取GitHub Actions中的凭据，进一步发动供应链攻击。
3. 在运行CodeQL的内部基础设施上执行代码。
4. 危害使用CodeQL和GitHub Actions缓存的仓库中的工作流凭据。

研究人员通过自建的秘密扫描工具发现了这一问题，并确认了潜在的供应链攻击风险。尽管攻击手段类似于近期发生的tj-actions/changed-files攻击，但GitHub尚未发现其平台或系统受到危害的证据。CodeQL是GitHub的代码分析引擎，被数十万仓库信任使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub Actions的安全性、权限管理和性能问题

不同观点：
• Sytten认为，GitHub如果推出不可变 actions，可以解决目前 GitHub Actions (GHA) 上大部分的安全问题，尤其是攻击风险。他提到这一方案本可以防止很多当前出现的灾难性问题，并对 GitHub 尚未推出该功能表示失望。
  
• nyrikki 关注临时 token 的权限问题，质疑为什么这些 token 可以创建新部署和生成工件证明。虽然 GitHub 修复时禁用了调试日志，但 nyrikki 认为更重要的是修改临时 token 的权限以适应代码分析引擎的需求。

• ashishb 提出，CI（持续集成）和 CD（持续交付）应完全分离，以防止 CI 环境被攻破后导致 CD 相关的 token 泄露。这表明了对现有架构安全性的担忧。

• junto 对 GitHub 的响应速度表示赞赏，认为其快速反应值得肯定。

• helsinki 的评论更多是个人感慨，与技术讨论无直接关系，提到对域名所有权的个人兴趣。

Skip to content
Vulnerability Research
CodeQLEAKED – Public Secrets Exposure Leads to Supply Chain Attack on GitHub CodeQL
John Stawinski
March 26, 2025
A potential supply chain attack on GitHub CodeQL started simply: a publicly exposed secret, valid for 1.022 seconds at a time.
In that second, an attacker could take a series of steps that would allow them to execute code within a GitHub Actions workflow in most repositories using CodeQL, GitHub’s code analysis engine trusted by hundreds of thousands of repositories. The impact would reach both public GitHub (GitHub Cloud) and GitHub Enterprise.
If backdooring GitHub Actions sounds familiar, that’s because it’s exactly what threat actors did in the recent tj-actions/changed-files supply chain attack. Imagine that very same supply chain attack, but instead of backdooring actions in tj-actions, they backdoored actions in GitHub CodeQL.
An attacker could use this to:
Compromise intellectual property
by exfiltrating the source code of private repositories using CodeQL.
Steal credentials within GitHub Actions secrets
of workflow jobs using CodeQL and leverage those secrets to execute further supply chain attacks.
Execute code on internal infrastructure
running CodeQL workflows.
Compromise GitHub Actions secrets
of workflows using the GitHub Actions Cache within a repo that uses CodeQL.
This is the story of how we uncovered an exposed secret leading to a race condition, a potential supply chain attack, and CVE-2025-24362.
Note: Per
GitHub’s advisory
, they have found no evidence of compromise to its platform or systems.
How Did We Get Here?
In January 2025, I took a break from Praetorian’s
Red Team
and began three months of research. I aimed to push the limits of public GitHub Actions exploitation, building on presentations we’ve given at
Black Hat
,
DEF CON
,
Schmoocon
, and Black Hat Arsenal. Tools and takeaways from this research will be implemented in our
CI/CD Professional Services Engagements
, and into
Chariot
, our Continuous Threat Exposure Management platform.
I began my research rotation by scanning GitHub Actions workflow artifacts for secrets.
Secret Scanning
In August 2024, Palo Alto researcher Yaron Avital
published an article
about identifying secrets in workflow artifacts. I had a hunch that there were still secrets to be found, especially since there hadn’t been much public follow-up work since the article.
I built a simple Actions Artifacts Secret Scanner to get started. It downloads artifacts from GitHub Actions workflows, recursively extracts their contents, and scans their contents for secrets with
Nosey Parker
, Praetorian’s open-sourced secrets scanning tool.
The Actions Artifacts Secret Scanner has been integrated into Chariot and open-sourced as a
Gato
capability.
After running this scanner for one day, it found a secret that could lead to a supply chain attack on GitHub CodeQL.
But first, I needed to see if the key was usable.
Background
CI/CD vulnerabilities sound complicated until you understand the terminology. Let’s catch you up.
GitHub Actions is a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform that allows the execution of code specified within workflows as part of the CI/CD process. When you push code to a GitHub repository or create a pull request, GitHub Actions can automatically build, test, and deploy your code using workflows defined in YAML files.
For example, let’s say you are building a web application that is hosted in AWS. You can configure a GitHub Actions workflow so that whenever you push code to your repository, it is automatically tested and then deployed to AWS.
If you are new to GitHub Actions, we’d recommend reading through
some examples
.
Every workflow run generates a GITHUB_TOKEN
— a special, automatically generated GitHub App installation token that allows the workflow to interact with the repository. This token’s permissions can be configured in the workflow file, at the repository level, or at the org level, determining what actions it can perform within the repository.
Put simply:
GitHub workflows execute on GitHub runners (typically a VM or Docker containers).
GitHub runners need a way to authenticate to GitHub to do stuff the workflows tell them to do.
For that purpose, they use the GITHUB_TOKEN.
If the token has high privileges, then token compromise == bad.
What are Workflow Artifacts?
We found the publicly exposed secret in a
GitHub Actions workflow artifact
.
GitHub Actions workflows can upload workflow “artifacts” to GitHub Actions. Workflow artifacts can be any file and are saved by that workflow for later use. By default, artifacts are publicly accessible to anyone with read access to the repository and are stored for up to 90 days.
And Finally, What is CodeQL?
CodeQL
is GitHub’s Code Analysis Engine. The CodeQL actions perform static code analysis on GitHub repositories to try and identify vulnerabilities. They have found
several hundred CVEs
over it’s lifetime, protecting organi
43527044.article_summary:
本文介绍了GitHub CodeQL潜在供应链攻击的发现过程。攻击始于一个公开暴露的秘密，有效期仅1.022秒，但足以让攻击者在大多数使用CodeQL的仓库中执行代码。攻击可能导致：

1. 泄露私有仓库的源代码，损害知识产权。
2. 窃取GitHub Actions中的凭据，进一步发动供应链攻击。
3. 在运行CodeQL的内部基础设施上执行代码。
4. 危害使用CodeQL和GitHub Actions缓存的仓库中的工作流凭据。

研究人员通过自建的秘密扫描工具发现了这一问题，并确认了潜在的供应链攻击风险。尽管攻击手段类似于近期发生的tj-actions/changed-files攻击，但GitHub尚未发现其平台或系统受到危害的证据。CodeQL是GitHub的代码分析引擎，被数十万仓库信任使用。

data.title: Installing air filters in classrooms has surprisingly large educational benefits (2020)
data.author: tangjurine
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在教室安装空气过滤器对学生成绩的显著提升作用。洛杉矶学校在应对阿里索峡谷气体泄漏事件时意外发现，安装空气过滤器后，学生成绩大幅提高，尤其是数学和英语成绩，效果持续且显著。研究显示，花费约1000美元安装过滤器能提升成绩，效果相当于将班级规模缩小三分之一。空气污染对认知能力的负面影响已有广泛研究支持，因此，安装空气过滤器可能是成本效益最高的教育干预措施，尤其对低收入家庭的孩子受益更大。虽然仍需更多研究验证，但这一简单措施显示出巨大潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在教室中安装空气过滤器的效果及其对学生成绩和健康的影响

不同观点：
• **Aurornis**: 支持在教室安装空气过滤器，但认为研究结果过于极端，可能无法在进一步研究中成立。指出学生成绩每年变化大，可能受多种因素影响，如教师差异和学校政策。将空气过滤器的效果与过去关于鱼油补充剂的夸大健康声明相比较。
• **rayiner**: 质疑数据的准确性和研究方法，指出研究结果依赖于单一数据点和一个不符合理论背景的线性趋势。提到过去关于驱虫药物对第三世界国家儿童的巨大益处研究被撤回的例子，认为科学驱动的公共政策在实际操作中非常困难。
• **amluto**: 希望有更多关于空气中气体对人影响的数据。指出CO2水平对认知表现的影响尚不明确，可能存在其他影响认知表现的气体。认为需要更多研究来验证各种假设。
• **jwpapi**: 分享个人经验，安装空气质量监测器并提醒开窗，显著提高了工作效率。
• **tangjurine**: 解释研究中提高的0.22标准差意味着什么，指出这在实际中代表了从50百分位到55百分位的提升。
• **aetherspawn**: 质疑使用HEPA过滤器过滤天然气泄漏的有效性，并指出HEPA过滤器对CO2无效。对研究得出的结论持怀疑态度，考虑购买类似过滤器但犹豫不决。
• **craigdalton**: 认为该研究由于无法控制其他因素，属于低质量证据。指出在污染影响健康的研究中，混杂因素常常比污染物本身对健康结果影响更大。认为需要更好的研究设计来支持政策行动。
• **Balgair**: 分享个人经验，安装N-95空气过滤器和紫外线灯后，日托中心的儿童生病次数明显减少。
• **fifteenforty**: 指出防止孩子生病可以提高教育成果。
• **amai**: 指出许多空气过滤器产生噪音，可能反而造成分心，降低生产力。
• **theoreticalmal**: 更喜欢自然通风，认为开放窗户比空调环境更愉快。
• **yoshuaw**: 引用新研究指出空气传播疾病导致大量病假，认为推行清洁室内空气的标准和政策是必要的，可以显著减少集体病假天数。
• **culopatin**: 回忆过去教室中油漆气味重，质疑其对健康和认知的影响。

补充讨论：
• 对空气过滤器效果的科学证据和研究方法存在争议，特别是关于是否能显著提高学生成绩。
• 个人经验和 anecdotal evidence 显示空气过滤器和改善通风对健康和生产力的积极影响。
• 对空气过滤器的具体类型和技术细节有疑问，特别是其在不同环境中的有效性和适用性。
• 强调政策和标准在推广清洁室内空气方面的重要性，呼吁更统一和严格的监管措施。

43529257.article_content:
Future Perfect
Installing air filters in classrooms has surprisingly large educational benefits
$1,000 can raise a class’s test scores by as much as cutting class size by a third.
by
Matthew Yglesias
Jan 8, 2020, 6:30 PM UTC
Facebook
Link
Students at Lavrentyev Secondary School No 130 in Novosibirsk, Russia, on December 20, 2019.
Kirill Kukhmar\TASS via Getty Images
An emergency situation that turned out to be mostly a false alarm led a lot of schools in Los Angeles to install air filters, and something strange happened: Test scores went up. By a lot. And the gains were sustained in the subsequent year rather than fading away.
That’s what NYU’s Michael Gilraine finds in a new working paper titled “
Air Filters, Pollution, and Student Achievement
” that looks at the surprising consequences of the
Aliso Canyon gas leak
in 2015.
The impact of the air filters is strikingly large given what a simple change we’re talking about. The school district didn’t reengineer the school buildings or make dramatic education reforms; they just installed $700 commercially available filters that you could plug into any room in the country. But it’s consistent with a
growing literature on the cognitive impact of air pollution
, which finds that everyone from
chess players
to
baseball umpires
to
workers in a pear-packing factory
suffer deteriorations in performance when the air is more polluted.
If Gilraine’s result holds up to further scrutiny, he will have identified what’s probably the single most cost-effective education policy intervention — one that should have particularly large benefits for low-income children.
And while it’s too hasty to draw sweeping conclusions on the basis of one study, it would be incredibly cheap to have a few cities experiment with installing air filters in some of their schools to get more data and draw clearer conclusions about exactly how much of a difference this makes.
The Aliso Canyon gas leak, explained
Back on October 23, 2015, employees of the Southern California Gas Company discovered a massive leak in the Aliso Canyon natural gas storage facility near Porter Ranch in the San Fernando Valley. Significant for the larger purposes of the study, the Porter Ranch area is known for having “
some of the cleanest air in the Valley year-round
.”
The gas leak was a huge catastrophe from the standpoint of greenhouse gas emissions, but also naturally raised concerns in the local community about the immediate impact on public health.
Facing political pressure from concerned parents and teachers, Gilraine writes, “the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) and the owner of the gas well, the Southern California Gas Company, placed air filters in every classroom, office and common area in all schools within five miles of the gas leak at the end of January 2016.”
Strikingly, however, air testing conducted around the time of the installation of the filters shows that the schools didn’t actually have abnormally high levels of the kinds of pollution that are normally associated with natural gas. Methane is lighter than air, and by the time the filters were installed — nearly three months after the leak — the extra pollution caused was all the way up in the sky and not affecting school buildings.
Consequently, the installation of the filters served not to remove extra contamination caused by the leak, but simply to clean up the normal amount of background indoor air pollution present in the Valley. That lets Gilraine estimate the difference in student performance for schools just inside the boundary compared to those just outside.
He finds that math scores went up by 0.20 standard deviations and English scores by 0.18 standard deviations, and the results hold up even when you control for “detailed student demographics, including residential ZIP Code fixed effects that help control for a student’s exposure to pollution at home.”
For context, this is comparable in scale to some of the most optimistic studies on the potential benefits of smaller class sizes, with
Alan Krueger finding that cutting class size by a third
leads to a 0.22 standard deviation improvement in academic performance. Other studies find smaller or even negative effects (because adding teachers means bringing in less experienced or less effective ones), but even accepting the positive findings, it costs much more than $700 per classroom to achieve class size reductions of that scale.
This is a big, but not implausible, number
The effect Gilraine finds is strikingly large given that it’s a seemingly trivial intervention.
But Sefi Roth of the London School of Economics studied university students’ test performance relative to air pollution levels on the day of the test alone
.
He found that taking a test in a filtered rather than unfiltered room would raise test scores by 0.09 standard deviations. That’s about half the impact Gilraine found, just based on day-of-test air quality. In Gilraine’s natural experiment, students benefited from cl
43529257.article_summary: 文章讨论了在教室安装空气过滤器对学生成绩的显著提升作用。洛杉矶学校在应对阿里索峡谷气体泄漏事件时意外发现，安装空气过滤器后，学生成绩大幅提高，尤其是数学和英语成绩，效果持续且显著。研究显示，花费约1000美元安装过滤器能提升成绩，效果相当于将班级规模缩小三分之一。空气污染对认知能力的负面影响已有广泛研究支持，因此，安装空气过滤器可能是成本效益最高的教育干预措施，尤其对低收入家庭的孩子受益更大。虽然仍需更多研究验证，但这一简单措施显示出巨大潜力。
43529257.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在教室中安装空气过滤器的效果及其对学生成绩和健康的影响

不同观点：
• **Aurornis**: 支持在教室安装空气过滤器，但认为研究结果过于极端，可能无法在进一步研究中成立。指出学生成绩每年变化大，可能受多种因素影响，如教师差异和学校政策。将空气过滤器的效果与过去关于鱼油补充剂的夸大健康声明相比较。
• **rayiner**: 质疑数据的准确性和研究方法，指出研究结果依赖于单一数据点和一个不符合理论背景的线性趋势。提到过去关于驱虫药物对第三世界国家儿童的巨大益处研究被撤回的例子，认为科学驱动的公共政策在实际操作中非常困难。
• **amluto**: 希望有更多关于空气中气体对人影响的数据。指出CO2水平对认知表现的影响尚不明确，可能存在其他影响认知表现的气体。认为需要更多研究来验证各种假设。
• **jwpapi**: 分享个人经验，安装空气质量监测器并提醒开窗，显著提高了工作效率。
• **tangjurine**: 解释研究中提高的0.22标准差意味着什么，指出这在实际中代表了从50百分位到55百分位的提升。
• **aetherspawn**: 质疑使用HEPA过滤器过滤天然气泄漏的有效性，并指出HEPA过滤器对CO2无效。对研究得出的结论持怀疑态度，考虑购买类似过滤器但犹豫不决。
• **craigdalton**: 认为该研究由于无法控制其他因素，属于低质量证据。指出在污染影响健康的研究中，混杂因素常常比污染物本身对健康结果影响更大。认为需要更好的研究设计来支持政策行动。
• **Balgair**: 分享个人经验，安装N-95空气过滤器和紫外线灯后，日托中心的儿童生病次数明显减少。
• **fifteenforty**: 指出防止孩子生病可以提高教育成果。
• **amai**: 指出许多空气过滤器产生噪音，可能反而造成分心，降低生产力。
• **theoreticalmal**: 更喜欢自然通风，认为开放窗户比空调环境更愉快。
• **yoshuaw**: 引用新研究指出空气传播疾病导致大量病假，认为推行清洁室内空气的标准和政策是必要的，可以显著减少集体病假天数。
• **culopatin**: 回忆过去教室中油漆气味重，质疑其对健康和认知的影响。

补充讨论：
• 对空气过滤器效果的科学证据和研究方法存在争议，特别是关于是否能显著提高学生成绩。
• 个人经验和 anecdotal evidence 显示空气过滤器和改善通风对健康和生产力的积极影响。
• 对空气过滤器的具体类型和技术细节有疑问，特别是其在不同环境中的有效性和适用性。
• 强调政策和标准在推广清洁室内空气方面的重要性，呼吁更统一和严格的监管措施。

data.title: Ukrainian Soldiers Unearth Ancient Greek Burial
data.author: isaacfrond
data.article_summary: 乌克兰士兵在挖掘防御工事时，意外发现了一座位于南乌克兰的古希腊墓葬遗址。出土文物包括一个爱奥尼亚风格的小型双耳瓶和一个带有三个壶嘴的古希腊酒壶（oinochoe），以及公元前六或五世纪的人类遗骸。专家认为，这些完好无损的仪式用具来自希腊，表明埋葬者具有较高的社会地位。公元前一千年，古希腊人在现今乌克兰附近的黑海北部海岸建立了多个殖民地。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：乌克兰考古遗址的破坏情况及其影响

不同观点：
• tokai 认为，乌克兰的许多考古遗址正在被摧毁，尤其是古冢（kugans），因为它们在战争中提供了有利的战斗位置和打击目标。tokai 强调，虽然这不如人员死亡那么悲惨，但依然令人痛心。他还指出，目前破坏的真实规模尚不明确。

• dr_dshiv 则关注克里米亚周围的古希腊殖民地，并提到希腊人曾定居到如此内陆的地方。他提供了一个维基百科链接，介绍了希腊人在克里米亚的历史。

补充讨论：
• tokai 的评论引发了对战争中文化遗产破坏的关注，特别是那些具有战略价值的考古遗址。
• dr_dshiv 的回应将讨论引导至具体的考古发现，特别是希腊人在克里米亚及其周边地区的定居历史，这为讨论提供了一个具体的历史背景。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接的争议，但讨论中隐含了对文化遗产在战争中保护不力的惋惜，以及对不同考古遗址重要性的不同关注点。tokai 更关注整体破坏的程度，而 dr_dshiv 则关注特定历史遗迹。

Miniature amphora, Mykolaiv, Ukraine
MYKOLAIV, UKRAINE—According to a report by the
Ukrainska Pravda
, Ukrainian soldiers digging defensive fortifications stumbled upon an ancient Greek burial site in southern Ukraine. During excavation work, a machine operator from the 123rd Territorial Defense Brigade noticed a small amphora sticking out of a freshly dug trench, which he brought to the Mykolayiv Regional Museum of Local History. Museum experts determined that the vessel was of Ionian origin and was specially crafted for ritual purposes during funerary ceremonies. Further investigation at the site revealed an oinochoe—an ancient Greek jug with a single handle and three spouts—and human remains that experts believe were buried in a sixth- or fifth-century
b.c.
necropolis. “These are ritual objects made specifically for burials and brought from Greece,” said Oleksandr, a former archaeologist from Vasyl Sukhomlynskyi Mykolaiv National University who is now serving in the military. “The fact that the vessels are intact and undamaged suggests that the buried individuals held a high social status.” During the first millennium
b.c.
, ancient Greeks established several colonies along the northern coast of the Black Sea near present-day Ukraine. For more on Ukrainian archaeology, go to "
Ukraine's Lost Capital
."
