data.title: Excitable cells
data.author: johannes_ne
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲解了心脏折返性心律失常的形成和维持条件。心肌细胞（心肌细胞）激活时会去极化，引发连锁反应。正常情况下，心脏由窦房结控制，称为窦性心律。如果出现一个非响应区域（如心肌梗死后疤痕组织），去极化波可以绕行形成自我维持的回路，导致折返性心动过速，例如房室结折返性心动过速或室性心动过速。这些心律失常可能无害，也可能致命，如室性纤颤。要引发折返性心律，去极化波需绕过非响应区域，且不同路径的不应期长短不一。通过电击（除颤）或巧妙 timing 的异位搏动可恢复窦性心律。纤颤则是另一种复杂的心律失常，心肌细胞无序激活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：心脏健康、心电图（ECG）分析及其相关模拟

不同观点：
• [eknkc] 分享了自己频繁出现异位心跳的经历，虽然医生认为不会致命，但仍感到不适。他提供了Apple Watch的ECG记录，并建议有类似情况的人去看心脏科医生，因为频率和每天的数量值得关注。
• [johannes_ne] 表示想撰写一篇类似的文章，进行ECG模拟并解释如何使ECG看起来更真实。他提到模拟中的去极化需要相对复极化非常快速，这对基于细胞的模拟可能计算上困难。
• [pscanf] 也分享了自己突发心动过速的经历，心跳突然加速到230 bpm，但也能很快自行恢复。这种现象虽然有些吓人，但同时也让他感到非常有趣。
• [PaulHoule] 提到了一本让他感到震撼的心脏学书籍，书中讨论了心脏波的拓扑结构，特别是螺旋波现象。他解释了心脏兴奋的相位变量如何在单位圆上运作。
• [randerson] 分享了自己接受射频消融术的经历，以解决良性但频繁的心律不齐。手术后心律恢复正常，且体力有所提升。

补充讨论：
• [fraserphysics] 正在重新分析一个旧竞赛中的ECG数据，试图通过ECG识别阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。他对ECG的变异性有疑问，并寻求专家帮助。
• [mjamesaustin] 分享了自己患有房室结折返性心动过速（AVNRT）的经历，尽管经过两次消融手术和每日服药，心律失常问题仍未完全解决。
• [lofties] 对文章中的动画表示赞赏，但提到自己无法让循环动画正常运行。
• [the_arun] 对作者在医学和工程方面的知识背景表示好奇，并提到作者在电生理学、麻醉学和软件方面的能力。
• [samwho] 对文章表示高度赞赏。
• [Kalabasa] 对细胞自动机能否模拟其他类型的细胞/组织提出疑问。
• [agumonkey] 询问是否有关于血流/血液流变学的类似文章。
• [EncomLab] 提到自己因冠状动脉问题时刻面临心脏问题，看到这些视觉效果感到非常有趣。
• [dheera] 分享了自己三次从心室颤动中幸存的经历，并提到安装了植入式心律转复除颤器（ICD），一直担心设备会有失效的时候。
• [leereeves] 表示文章中的互动动画帮助他更好地理解了心脏生理学，尽管他已经了解文章中的知识。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对ECG模拟的复杂性有不同看法，[johannes_ne] 提到去极化速度的计算难度，而[fraserphysics] 则对ECG变异性的来源存在疑问。
• 对心律不齐治疗方式的个人体验不同，[randerson] 的射频消融术非常成功并提升了体力，而[mjamesaustin] 的两次手术后问题仍未完全解决。

这些讨论展示了心脏健康问题的复杂性，以及ECG分析和模拟中的挑战。

43504940.article_content:
I wrote this post to answer some of the questions, I had as a medical student, when I first learned about cardiac arrhythmias. Mainly, what are the conditions required to initiate and maintain a
reentrant arrhythmia
? That is, a state where the heart muscles are continuously activated by a self-sustaining loop, independent of the normal pace-making system. These arrhythmias can be benign, as with
AV-nodal reentry tachycardia (AVNRT)
; a common, and usually harmless, cause of palpitations in young people. Or they can be deadly, as with
ventricular fibrillation
.
Heart muscle cells (cardiomyocytes) have some interesting properties. When they are activated, they
depolarize
. Depolarization causes the cell to contract, but also activates neighboring cells, setting of a chain reaction.
For the following demonstrations, we use i highly simplified model of heart. Below is a grid of simulated cardiomyocytes, each ready to activate their neighboring cells. They all start in a
resting state
, ready to be
activated
.
Activated cells are black. After a short moment, they become inactive and
refractory
. Refractory cells cannot be activated. In the simulation, refractory cells go from dark gray to light gray, until they have regained their resting state, and are ready for a new activation.
👆️ Click/tap anywhere in the box below to activate a cell.
Notice, that the activation is not entirely symmetric and predictable. To give the simulation a more organic feel, I added a bit of randomness to the activation of cells. Each cell is activated with a higher probability the more of its four neighbors are active (33% chance if one neighbor is active, 100% chance when 3 or 4 neighbors are active).
Pacemaker cells
Sinus rhythm. From
ECGpedia
.
Another interesting property of cardiomyocytes is their
automaticity
; cardiomyocytes spontaneously activate if they are not stimulated by a neighboring cells for a period. Cells in the
sinoatrial node
(sinus node) in the right atrium have the fastest rate of spontaneous activation, and thus activate the remaining heart, making the sinus node the heart’s pacemaker.
In the following simulation, a cluster of cells in the top left corner act as pacemaker cells.
👆️ Move the slider below the simulation to change the rate of spontaneous depolarization (heart rate).
When the spontaneous depolarization of the sinus node determines the heart rate, the heart is said to be in
sinus rhythm
, which is the normal (physiological) activation path of the heart. If the sinus node paces the heart at a rate faster than 100 beats per minute, the rhythm is called
sinus tachycardia
. Sinus tachycardia (together with increased stroke volume) increases the flow of blood from the heart, and is the physiological response to exercise.
Reentry tachycardia
Ventricular tachycardia. From
Ecgpedia
.
In reentry tachycardia, the heart is not paced by the sinus node, but instead from a group of cells that have formed a circuit, where a wave of depolarization can loop around and stimulate itself over and over. This requires a non-responsive area among the cells (an area that cannot be activated), so a circuit can form around it.
In the simulation below, the red cells are non-responsive (dead). They could represent scar tissue after a
myocardial infarction
—
a common cause of ventricular tachycardia
. Or the simulation could illustrate
atrial flutter
, where a reentrant loop can form around the tricuspid valve.
👆️ To stop the reentrant tachycardia, shock the cardiac cells by pressing the “⚡️ Defibrillate!” button.
⚡️ Defibrillate!
After defibrillation, the system is in sinus rhythm. The pacemaker cells were always there, but were suppressed by the reentrant loop.
The simulation above illustrates how a reentrant loop can sustain itself around a dead area, but how does it start in the first place?
👆️ You can try to click/tap on the simulation above to set of an ectopic beat (a depolarization starting outside the sinus node), but you will not be able to initiate a reentrant loop again.
How does a reentrant loop start?
To initiate a reentrant loop, the wave of depolarization must be traveling only one way around the dead area. Otherwise the two waves traveling in opposite will just eliminate each other when they meet at the other side. However, if one pathway has cells with a
longer refractory period
, a wave of depolarization can arrive exactly when one pathway is ready to depolarize, while the other is still refractory.
In the simulation below, cells in the lower left corner have a longer refractory period.
👆️ Try initiating an ectopic beat (click/tap) next to the area with a longer refractory period, while the area is still refractory.
⚡️ Defibrillate!
👆️ You can get the system back in sinus rhythm either by ⚡️ defibrillation, or by cleverly timing a new ectopic beat to block the reentrant loop.
Fibrillation
Ventricular fibrillation. From
Ecgpedia
.
Another common cardiac arrythmia is fibrillation—atrial fibrillation or ventricu

• [Kalabasa] 对细胞自动机能否模拟其他类型的细胞/组织提出疑问。
• [agumonkey] 询问是否有关于血流/血液流变学的类似文章。

• 对心律不齐治疗方式的个人体验不同，[randerson] 的射频消融术非常成功并提升了体力，而[mjamesaustin] 的两次手术后问题仍未完全解决。

这些讨论展示了心脏健康问题的复杂性，以及ECG分析和模拟中的挑战。

data.author: goldenskye
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在大学第一份工作中进行的一个愚人节恶作剧。作者当时是一名数据库程序员，负责管理一台HP 9000 K250服务器和校园打印机系统。作者发现校园的HP LaserJet打印机可以通过指令改变其显示屏上的“READY”消息，于是计划在愚人节那天修改所有网络打印机的显示信息为“INSERT 5 CENTS”（投入5美分）。作者编写了一个简单脚本，在愚人节清晨提前到达工作岗位运行脚本，导致校园内所有网络打印机在打印前都显示需要投入5美分。这个恶作剧被认为是作者职业生涯中最成功的一次玩笑，甚至超过了其学生时代的一次著名恶作剧。文章以幽默的语气讲述了这个技术玩笑的实施过程。

43543743.article_content:
Everyone should pull one great practical joke in their lifetimes. This one was mine, and I think it's past the statute of limitations. The story is true. Only the names are redacted to protect the guilty.
My first job out of college was a database programmer, even though my undergraduate degree had nothing to do with computers and my current profession still mostly doesn't. The reason was that the University I worked for couldn't afford competitive wages, but they did offer various fringe benefits, and they were willing to train someone who at least had decent working knowledge. I, as a newly minted graduate of the august University of California system, had decent working knowledge at least of BSD/386 and SunOS, but more importantly also had the glowing recommendation of my predecessor who was being promoted into a new position. I was hired, which was their first mistake.
The system I was hired to work on was an HP 9000 K250, one of Hewlett-Packard's big PA-RISC servers. I wish I had a photograph of it, but all I have are a couple bad scans of some bad Polaroids of my office and none of the server room. The server room was downstairs from my office back in the days when server rooms were on-premises, complete with a swipe card lock and a halon system that would give you a few seconds of grace before it flooded everything. The K250 hulked in there where it had recently replaced what I think was an Encore mini of some sort (probably a Multimax, since it was a few years old and the 88K Encores would have been too new for the University), along with the AIX RS/6000s that provided student and faculty shell accounts and E-mail, the bonded T1 lines, some of the terminal servers, the massive Cabletron routers and a lot of the telco stuff. One of the tape reels from the Encore hangs on my wall today as a memento.
The K250 and the Encore it replaced (as well as the L-Class that later replaced the K250 when I was a consultant) ran an all-singing, all-dancing student information system called CARS. CARS is still around, renamed
Jenzabar
, though I suspect that many of its underpinnings remain if you look under the table. In those days CARS was a massive overlay that was loaded atop the operating system and database, which when I started were, respectively, HP/UX 10.20 and Informix. (I'm old.) It used Informix tables, screens and stored procedures plus its own text UI libraries to run code written variously as Perform screens, SQL, C-shell scripts and plain old C or ESQL/C. Everything was tracked in RCS using overgrown
Makefile
s. I had the admin side (resource management, financials, attendance trackers, etc.) and my office partner had the academic side (mostly grades and faculty tracking). My job was to write and maintain this code and shortly after to help the University create custom applications in CARS' brand-spanking new web module, which chose the new hotness in scripting languages, i.e., Perl. Fortuitously I had learned Perl in, appropriately enough, a computational linguistics course.
CARS also managed most of the printers on campus except for the few that the RS/6000s controlled directly. Most of the campus admin printers were HP LaserJet 4 units of some derivation equipped with JetDirect cards for networking. These are great warhorse printers, some of the best laser printers HP ever made. I suspect there were line printers other places, but those printers were largely what existed in the University's offices.
It turns out that the
READY
message these printers show on their VFD panels is changeable. I don't remember where I read this, probably idly paging through the manual over a lunch break, but initially the only fun things I could think of to do was to have the printer say hi to my boss when she sent jobs to it, stuff like that (whereupon she would tell me to get back to work). Then it dawned on me: because I had access to the printer spools on the K250, and the spool directories were conveniently named the same as their hostnames, I knew where each and every networked LaserJet on campus was. I was young, rash and motivated. This was a hack I just couldn't resist. It would be even better than what had been my favourite joke at my alma mater, where campus services, notable for posting various service suspension notices, posted one April Fools' Day that gravity itself would be suspended to various buildings. I felt sure this hack would eclipse that too.
The plan on April Fools' Day was to get into work at OMG early o'clock and iterate over every entry in the spool, sending it a sequence that would change the
READY
message to
INSERT 5 CENTS
. This would cause every networked LaserJet on campus to appear to ask for a nickel before you printed anything. The script was very simple (this is the actual script, I saved it):
#!/bin/csh -f
cd /opt/carsi/spool
foreach i (*)
echo '^[%-12345X@PJL RDYMSG DISPLAY="INSERT 5 CENTS"' | netto $i 9100
end
The
^[
was a literal ASCII 27 ESCape character, and
netto
was a simple

data.title: Experimental Tauri Verso Integration
data.author: stareatgoats
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Tauri框架与Verso浏览器的实验性整合。Verso是一个基于Rust的Servo引擎的浏览器，旨在简化Servo复杂API的使用。通过新的自定义运行时**tauri-runtime-verso**，开发者可以轻松切换运行时并继续使用Tauri的功能。虽然目前该整合尚未如Tauri的其他后端那样强大，但已支持基本窗口操作、React框架、Tauri命令行接口等功能。未来计划包括发布预构建的Verso可执行文件、支持更多窗口特性、以及改进初始化脚本处理方式。该整合旨在降低使用Servo的门槛，并增强Tauri的功能和灵活性。示例代码和演示可参见相关GitHub仓库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tauri框架的使用及其相关技术选择（如Servo、Verso、WebView等）的优缺点和应用场景

不同观点：
• shubhamjain：对在Tauri中集成Servo或Verso感到困惑，认为这可能违背了Tauri利用原生WebView创建轻量级应用的初衷。
• klabb3：解释Tauri的核心优势是利用系统WebView，从而实现比Electron更小的应用体积，通常只有几MB，而Electron则超过100MB。
• usrusr：虽然集成Servo或Verso看似违背了Tauri的独特卖点，但如果能作为应对不同平台WebView不确定性的备用方案，可能会促进Tauri的采用。将其类比为电动车中的续航焦虑问题。
• xrd：询问Tauri是否有移动端的支持，尤其是能否将Rust后端移植到Android或iOS，并提到利用系统WebView可能使移动端开发成为可能。
• Fraterkes：提到有人曾说Tauri可能最终会包含Chromium，因为不同操作系统中的原生WebView差异很大，使用原生WebView的可移植性优势可能并不明显。
• dcow：讨论了Tauri中运行时抽象边界的问题，提出如果要将不同的运行时进行替换，可能会遇到与原生UI组件（如菜单、系统托盘）相关的问题。建议将“Web渲染运行时”和“原生UI运行时”分开，或改进菜单系统的抽象。
• zachrip：询问Servo或Verso是否能提供原始帧缓冲（framebuffer），因为其项目目前使用CEF，但希望完全转向Rust。
• jonstewart：作为C++开发者，对Tauri作为跨平台应用框架感兴趣，但感到文档和各种选项（如前端框架、构建工具）选择太多，且缺乏足够的示例和指导，尤其是与Rust web服务框架的集成及状态管理方面。
• m00dy：对在Tauri中使用Verso代替Wry表示强烈兴趣，尤其是在高性能需求的AI驱动交易平台中，认为Rust驱动的渲染引擎可能带来更快的DOM更新、更好的安全性和更低的资源占用。同时询问了Verso的渲染速度和WebRTC支持情况。

补充讨论：
• synergy20：提到另一个不同的方案，提供了一个链接（https://webui.me/），暗示可能有其他技术方案可供选择。

争议焦点：
• Tauri集成Servo或Verso是否违背了其利用原生WebView创建轻量级应用的初衷，以及这种集成是否有实际意义和价值。
• 关于原生WebView的可移植性和一致性问题，以及是否需要引入如Chromium这样的浏览器来解决这些问题。

总结：讨论围绕Tauri框架的技术选择和应用场景展开，参与者对集成Servo或Verso的必要性、WebView的优缺点、移动端支持、运行时抽象边界及文档和示例的完善性等方面提出了不同的看法和建议。

Experimental Tauri Verso Integration
Mar 17, 2025
Tony
Tauri Development
What is Verso?
So first off, what is
Verso
?
Verso
is a browser based on
Servo
, a web browser rendering engine written in Rust
Why using Verso instead of Servo directly?
I believe there’re quite a lot of people having thought about using Servo but got intimidated by the complex APIs and just gave up, which frankly I was one of them, so the goal of building the Verso webview is to make it easy enough to understand and use so that people will actually start to experiment and use it
Servo itself is made to be relatively easy to embed compared to other browsers, but the APIs are still way too low level and it’s quite daunting to use, you can take a look at the minimal example for running Servo with Winit at (note this is not even a fully functional example):
https://github.com/servo/servo/blob/8d39d7706aee50971e848a5e31fc6bfd7ef552c1/components/servo/examples/winit_minimal.rs

It’s not to say Servo’s API is bad though, as they need to support a lot more use cases while we just need it for building applications with Tauri

43518462.article_summary: 本文介绍了Tauri框架与Verso浏览器的实验性整合。Verso是一个基于Rust的Servo引擎的浏览器，旨在简化Servo复杂API的使用。通过新的自定义运行时**tauri-runtime-verso**，开发者可以轻松切换运行时并继续使用Tauri的功能。虽然目前该整合尚未如Tauri的其他后端那样强大，但已支持基本窗口操作、React框架、Tauri命令行接口等功能。未来计划包括发布预构建的Verso可执行文件、支持更多窗口特性、以及改进初始化脚本处理方式。该整合旨在降低使用Servo的门槛，并增强Tauri的功能和灵活性。示例代码和演示可参见相关GitHub仓库。

不同观点：
• shubhamjain：对在Tauri中集成Servo或Verso感到困惑，认为这可能违背了Tauri利用原生WebView创建轻量级应用的初衷。
• klabb3：解释Tauri的核心优势是利用系统WebView，从而实现比Electron更小的应用体积，通常只有几MB，而Electron则超过100MB。
• usrusr：虽然集成Servo或Verso看似违背了Tauri的独特卖点，但如果能作为应对不同平台WebView不确定性的备用方案，可能会促进Tauri的采用。将其类比为电动车中的续航焦虑问题。
• xrd：询问Tauri是否有移动端的支持，尤其是能否将Rust后端移植到Android或iOS，并提到利用系统WebView可能使移动端开发成为可能。
• Fraterkes：提到有人曾说Tauri可能最终会包含Chromium，因为不同操作系统中的原生WebView差异很大，使用原生WebView的可移植性优势可能并不明显。
• dcow：讨论了Tauri中运行时抽象边界的问题，提出如果要将不同的运行时进行替换，可能会遇到与原生UI组件（如菜单、系统托盘）相关的问题。建议将“Web渲染运行时”和“原生UI运行时”分开，或改进菜单系统的抽象。
• zachrip：询问Servo或Verso是否能提供原始帧缓冲（framebuffer），因为其项目目前使用CEF，但希望完全转向Rust。

• m00dy：对在Tauri中使用Verso代替Wry表示强烈兴趣，尤其是在高性能需求的AI驱动交易平台中，认为Rust驱动的渲染引擎可能带来更快的DOM更新、更好的安全性和更低的资源占用。同时询问了Verso的渲染速度和WebRTC支持情况。

补充讨论：
• synergy20：提到另一个不同的方案，提供了一个链接（https://webui.me/），暗示可能有其他技术方案可供选择。

争议焦点：
• Tauri集成Servo或Verso是否违背了其利用原生WebView创建轻量级应用的初衷，以及这种集成是否有实际意义和价值。
• 关于原生WebView的可移植性和一致性问题，以及是否需要引入如Chromium这样的浏览器来解决这些问题。

总结：讨论围绕Tauri框架的技术选择和应用场景展开，参与者对集成Servo或Verso的必要性、WebView的优缺点、移动端支持、运行时抽象边界及文档和示例的完善性等方面提出了不同的看法和建议。

data.article_summary: 美国海军陆战队将获得由Regent Craft开发的高速、雷达隐身的电动掠海飞行器（seagliders），名为Viceroy，用于救援任务。该飞行器最高时速可达180英里，航程约180英里。其独特之处在于能够水上起降，无需传统跑道，适合争议海域行动。电动推进系统使其具有低雷达和声呐特征，并可从岸上或舰上充电，确保能源供应。该项目始于与海军陆战队作战实验室的合同，现已进入第二阶段，将深入评估其技术能力，以满足不断变化的国防需求。这种飞行器具有高效、低成本的特点，适用于后勤和救援任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Regent的"Viceroy"地效飞行器及其潜在应用，特别是其在军事和救援行动中的作用。

不同观点：
• icegreentea2认为该飞行器主要用于支持美军在第一岛链内的军事行动，特别是后勤和物资运输，而非救援行动。他引用了2022年的一篇文章，讨论了地效飞行器在海上运输中的潜力，并指出该技术仍在测试和开发中，尚未确定是否能实际应用。
• JR1427将该飞行器与前苏联的Ekranoplans（地效飞行器）进行比较，暗示这种技术并非全新，历史上已有类似应用。
• acc_297指出Regent的飞行器尚未建造和试飞全尺寸原型，仅在2022年成功展示了一个四分之一比例模型，并对飞行器的"雷达隐形"特性提出质疑，认为其低空飞行特性自然使其难以被雷达探测。
• nsiemsen提到Regent是Y Combinator的一个公司，暗示其有创业背景和商业潜力。
• Rygian质疑为何标题强调"救援行动"，因为该技术似乎并不限于此用途，并指出文章中提到的"与特定防御行动相关的演示"范围更广。
• fidotron认为地效飞行器可能在无人机物流方面有重要作用，尤其是在湖区，但对仅将其用于救援表示失望。
• bluesounddirect询问该飞行器是否为地效机器，显示出对技术细节的兴趣。
• lttlrck对飞行器的475万美元原型成本表示赞赏，并表示希望在飞行模拟器中使用该模型。
• ein0p担心飞行器是否能躲避无人机，认为如果不能，可能会浪费纳税人的钱，因为廉价无人机可能威胁到昂贵的军事设备。
• zombiwoof的评论"Hello Greenland"似乎是无关的或幽默的插曲，未直接参与技术讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该飞行器的实际应用和潜在军事价值，特别是其在运输和防御行动中的可行性。
• 有人关注该技术的研发状态和原型测试进展，特别是其全尺寸原型的开发和测试结果。
• 对飞行器的雷达隐形特性和反无人机能力存在质疑，显示出对其在现代战场上的生存能力的关注。
• 讨论还涉及该技术的商业应用潜力，特别是在物流和运输领域的可能用途。

Viceroy seaglider
Regent Craft
Regent Craft, a developer specializing in all-electric seagliders based in Rhode Island, has completed its initial contract with the U.S. Marine Corps Warfighting Lab (MCWL).
In a significant progression, the company has secured a follow-up agreement, estimated at $10 million, which offers opportunities for further extensions.
The initial phase of Regent’s partnership with MCWL, valued at $4.75 million, encompassed twelve key deliverables that validated the technical feasibility of seagliders.
This phase began with testing a quarter-scale prototype and culminated in the recently successful sea trials of the full-scale Viceroy prototype.
High-speed, radar-proof electric seagliders
The second phase of the agreement aims to deepen the evaluation of the Viceroy’s technical capabilities.
This will involve demonstrations relevant to specific defense operations, a crucial aspect as military needs evolve.
Tom Huntley, Vice President of Government Relations and Defense at Regent, expressed pride in continuing collaboration with the Marine Corps.
He highlighted the role of Regent’s seagliders in meeting national security requirements, specifically in logistics operations that face challenges in contested maritime environments.
The advantages of seagliders are particularly noteworthy for defense operations, where speed and efficiency can determine the success of missions.
The Viceroy seaglider can soar up to 180 mph over approximately 180 miles.
One of the standout features of sea gliders is their ability to take off and land on water.
This capability eliminates reliance on traditional runways, which can be vulnerable in conflict situations.
Furthermore, these electric-powered vessels can be recharged from shore and ship resources, ensuring a dependable energy
source
during operations.
Another significant benefit is their low radar and sonar signatures. By flying close to the water’s surface, seagliders avoid radar detection while minimizing heat and infrared visibility due to their electric propulsion systems.
For rescue ops
Their design simplicity and fewer components translate into lower operational and maintenance costs when compared to traditional aviation and maritime vehicles.

data.title: Self-Hosting like it's 2025
data.author: finnlab
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自托管（self-hosting）的技术选择、安全性、便捷性以及备份问题

不同观点：
• 自托管的乐趣与控制感：[ltr_] 认为自托管像回到了2000年代，带来掌控感和远离大科技公司控制的自由，享受与朋友一起创建项目的过程，并表达对大科技公司的不满。
• 安全性担忧与技术门槛：[0xEF] 对自托管感兴趣，但担心安全问题，特别是如何保护家庭网络和设备免受攻击，表达了对自托管安全的焦虑，并寻求学习资源。
• 对自托管趋势的担忧：[TrayKnots] 担心自托管的普及会导致监管和隐私问题，比如矩阵实例被要求设置后门，以及对自托管项目的潜在影响。
• 自托管的工具选择和复杂性：
  - [bauerd] 认为在家中使用Kubernetes过于复杂，不必要。
  - [Youden] 分享了自己的经验，从Docker、Quadlet到Kubernetes，最终选择了Hashicorp Nomad和Consul，并解释了各工具的优缺点。
  - [cullumsmith] 偏好使用FreeBSD jails和shell脚本，认为这些工具稳定且避免了技术更新过快的烦恼。
  - [notpushkin] 推广自己的项目Lunni，作为Portainer的替代方案，目前仅支持Docker Swarm。
  - [terminalbraid] 支持使用dokku来托管web应用。
  - [zephyreon] 推荐Unraid作为简化的自托管解决方案。
• 备份问题的讨论：[FloatArtifact] 指出自托管社区对备份问题重视不够，呼吁更便捷的容器备份方案。
• 自托管的技术实现与简化：[vbezhenar] 分享了自己的VPS配置方法，使用RHEL 9和Podman，并解释了选择这些工具的原因和设置过程。
• 自托管的安全与便捷配置：[Helmut10001] 认为Docker Compose比Portainer更易用，并分享了设置rootless Docker的资源和自动更新的方法。
• 外包安全与简化配置的需求：[aborsy] 认为自托管应用的安全性需要外包给公司，因为个人难以跟踪所有漏洞，并提到Cloudflare Tunnels作为部分解决方案。
• 简单自托管方案：[martin_a] 和 [kuon] 都提倡使用简单的工具和方法，如"rsync"和静态站点生成器，避免使用容器和复杂工具，以减少依赖和维护成本。

补充讨论：
- 自托管的技术选择和复杂性是主要讨论焦点，不同用户根据自己的需求和经验选择了不同的工具和方法。
- 安全性是自托管的一个重要关注点，尤其是对于技术不够熟练的用户，如何简化安全配置和保护自托管项目是一个挑战。
- 备份问题也被提及，社区需要更简单和可靠的备份解决方案。

• 对自托管趋势的担忧：[TrayKnots] 担心自托管的普及会导致监管和隐私问题，比如矩阵实例被要求设置后门，以及对自托管项目的潜在影响。
• 自托管的工具选择和复杂性：
  - [bauerd] 认为在家中使用Kubernetes过于复杂，不必要。
  - [Youden] 分享了自己的经验，从Docker、Quadlet到Kubernetes，最终选择了Hashicorp Nomad和Consul，并解释了各工具的优缺点。
  - [cullumsmith] 偏好使用FreeBSD jails和shell脚本，认为这些工具稳定且避免了技术更新过快的烦恼。
  - [notpushkin] 推广自己的项目Lunni，作为Portainer的替代方案，目前仅支持Docker Swarm。
  - [terminalbraid] 支持使用dokku来托管web应用。
  - [zephyreon] 推荐Unraid作为简化的自托管解决方案。
• 备份问题的讨论：[FloatArtifact] 指出自托管社区对备份问题重视不够，呼吁更便捷的容器备份方案。
• 自托管的技术实现与简化：[vbezhenar] 分享了自己的VPS配置方法，使用RHEL 9和Podman，并解释了选择这些工具的原因和设置过程。
• 自托管的安全与便捷配置：[Helmut10001] 认为Docker Compose比Portainer更易用，并分享了设置rootless Docker的资源和自动更新的方法。
• 外包安全与简化配置的需求：[aborsy] 认为自托管应用的安全性需要外包给公司，因为个人难以跟踪所有漏洞，并提到Cloudflare Tunnels作为部分解决方案。
• 简单自托管方案：[martin_a] 和 [kuon] 都提倡使用简单的工具和方法，如"rsync"和静态站点生成器，避免使用容器和复杂工具，以减少依赖和维护成本。

补充讨论：
- 自托管的技术选择和复杂性是主要讨论焦点，不同用户根据自己的需求和经验选择了不同的工具和方法。
- 安全性是自托管的一个重要关注点，尤其是对于技术不够熟练的用户，如何简化安全配置和保护自托管项目是一个挑战。
- 备份问题也被提及，社区需要更简单和可靠的备份解决方案。

data.title: An e-bike that charges off USB-C
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: Ampler推出了两款新型电动自行车Nova和Nova Pro，它们可以通过USB-C接口充电，使用常见的USB-C PD 3.1充电器，仅需三小时即可充满电。该系列电动车电池为48V 336Wh，支持双向USB-C接口，不仅能充电，还能为其他设备提供15W电力。Nova售价€2,990，Pro售价€3,490，配备250W电机，最高时速25公里，Pro型号拥有更好的传动系统和轮组。两款车型将于6月在英国、欧盟和瑞士发售，并提供两年保修和14天退货政策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：USB接口在电动自行车上的适用性及其实际功能性

不同观点：
• **citrin_ru的观点**：担心USB接口在电动自行车上的耐用性，尤其是在恶劣环境下（如沙尘、潮湿）的可靠性。他认为，自行车在 dirty 和未干的道路上行驶时，接口很容易受到影响，因此更倾向于使用更加坚固耐用的接口。

• **netsharc的观点**：对USB-C接口的普及表示质疑，认为虽然USB-C实现了接口统一，但不同设备的功能差异导致使用时产生混乱。例如，用户需要考虑接口是否支持充电、是否支持显示输出、是否支持电力传输（PD）等，这反而增加了不确定性和复杂性。

• **Tepix的观点**：从电力需求的角度出发，认为USB PD（电力传输）能提供超过140W的电力，这对于电动自行车来说很有意义，尤其是像Bosch 6A快速充电器可以达到216W的功率。他进一步提出240W的电力传输可能性，暗示USB接口在供电能力上还有提升空间。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：USB接口在电动自行车上的实际应用面临两个主要问题：一是耐用性，特别是在复杂环境下的表现（citrin_ru的观点）；二是功能一致性和电力传输能力的混乱和不确定性（netsharc的观点）。同时，有用户（Tepix）对USB PD的供电能力表示期待，认为其有潜力满足电动自行车的高电力需求。

• **论据和例子**：
  - citrin_ru以自行车在脏乱道路上行驶为例，说明接口需要具备更好的抗环境能力。
  - netsharc以USB-C接口的功能多样性和设备间差异为例，说明统一接口并未完全解决使用中的困惑。
  - Tepix通过Bosch 6A快速充电器的例子，说明电动自行车对高功率电力传输的需求，并提出USB PD的潜力。

总体来看，讨论围绕USB接口在电动自行车上的实用性和可行性展开，涉及耐用性、功能一致性和电力传输能力等多个方面。

43545378.article_content:
News
Finally, an e-bike that charges off USB-C
A fast three hours means the Ampler Nova is no April fool.
A fast three hours means the Ampler Nova is no April fool.
by
Thomas Ricker
Apr 1, 2025, 6:00 AM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Up to 140W off a USB-C PD 3.1 laptop charger you might already own.
Image: Ampler
Thomas Ricker
is a deputy editor and Verge co-founder with a passion for human-centric cities, e-bikes, and life as a digital nomad. He’s been a tech journalist for almost 20 years.
Ampler made one of the
first modern e-bikes I ever tested
, and now it’s selling the first commercial electric bikes — the Nova and Nova Pro — I’m aware of that can be charged over a USB-C port integrated right into the frame. Hell, that same jack will even charge your gadgets in a pinch, but not in the US because this e-bike is for Europe only.
Estonia-based
Ampler
is best known for making reliable direct-to-consumer e-bikes from its home in Tallinn using decent, mostly off-the-shelf parts that can be serviced at any local bike shop. Adding USB-C charging from a
laptop charger you might already own
makes a ton of sense as
Europe standardizes on the port
to eliminate redundancy and reduce waste. It also makes it easier to find a compatible bike charger if you leave yours at home.
You can charge the relatively small 48V 336Wh integrated batteries (removable for service only) on the Nova series e-bikes from zero to full in as little as three hours from a USB-C PD 3.1 charger operating at up to 140W. That’s very respectable. Some e-bikes fitted with a battery this same size can take
five hours
or longer to refill from chargers with proprietary connectors, and others fitted with larger batteries and 300-plus-watt charging bricks can bring that down to around two hours. Fortunately,
240W USB-C chargers
are now starting to ship, so USB-C is well in position to compete.
Previous
Next
1
/
10
Ampler has also tested its bikes to work with less capable Ikea and MacBook chargers that support the older USB-C PD 3.0 spec. If you don’t already have such a charger, Ampler will sell you its own 140W USB-C PD 3.1 charger for €80 (about $87). And while the USB-C port is bidirectional on the Nova series, it’s only capable of charging your USB-C gadgets at a modest 15W.
Both the €2,990 (about $3,230) Nova and €3,490 (about $3,770) Nova Pro are available in step-through and step-over frames in three sizes to accommodate most riders, with EU standard 250W motors maxing out at a basic 25km/h. They’re essentially improved
Stout and Stella
models designed to be more compatible with accessories like U-locks, third-party saddles, and child carriers. The base Nova model is fitted with wide 27.5-inch tires and depends on an oily chain and derailleur for its nine-speed transmission. The Nova Pro, however, is the bike I’d opt for, with its slightly larger 28-inch wheels, Gates Carbon belt drive, and a 10-speed Shimano Deore drivetrain baked into the hub.
Both the Nova and Nova Pro are available to preorder starting today in the UK, EU, and Switzerland, with shipping set to begin in June. Ampler is backed by official service centers in Germany and a network of “
Ampler Friendly
” workshops scattered around Europe. Each bike comes with a two-year warranty and a 14-day return policy.

data.title: AWS S3 sync does not sync all the files
data.author: pera
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AWS S3同步工具的一个问题：某些文件在一年前被修改后，没有正确同步到目标位置，尽管这些文件的时间戳不同，且S3上保存的是更新的文件。用户使用的同步命令是`aws s3 s3://source /local-folder --delete`，并提到所有未同步的文件具有相同的时间戳，但分布在不同文件夹中。用户询问是否存在可以更改时间戳的S3 touch命令，以促使这些文件重新同步。该问题被标记为需要核心团队审核的标准优先级功能请求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS CLI 中的 sync 命令是否适合用于文件同步任务

不同观点：
• kbumsik 认为 AWS CLI 并非专门用于文件同步的工具。他指出，AWS CLI 本质上是一个用于单个API调用的封装工具，因此其提供的 sync 命令在一开始就显得不太合适。kbumsik 建议使用像 rclone 这样专门为同步任务设计的工具，因为这些工具能够更好地完成此类任务。

补充讨论：
• kbumsik 强调了工具的专业性，主张使用那些为特定任务优化的工具，而不是依赖多功能但可能不专精的工具。
• 争议的焦点在于 AWS CLI 的 sync 命令是否足够好用于文件同步任务，以及是否有必要使用专门工具如 rclone 来替代。
• 例子：kbumsik 提到了 rclone 作为一个例子，说明了有其他工具可能更适合文件同步任务。

We have several hundred thousand files and S3 reliably syncs files. However, we have noticed that there were several files which were changed about a year ago and those are different but do not sync or update.

All the files that do not sync have the same date but are spread across multiple different folders.
Is there an S3 touch command to change the timestamp and possibly get the files to sync again?

data.article_summary: 2025年3月31日，白宫宣布完成对《大西洋》杂志编辑杰弗里·戈德堡意外被加入一个讨论也门袭击计划的高层官员Signal群聊的审查。白宫新闻秘书卡罗琳·利维特表示，此案已结案，并采取了措施防止类似事件再次发生，但未提供具体细节。审查由国家安全委员会、白宫法律顾问办公室及特朗普顾问埃隆·马斯克参与。尽管群聊创建者、特朗普的国安顾问迈克·沃尔兹仍将继续担任重要职务，但参议院武装部队委员会的两党领袖已要求五角大楼代理监察长展开调查，非营利组织美国监督也提起诉讼以确保记录保存符合《联邦记录法》。

data.title: You Can Still Read NASA's Deleted "First Woman" Graphic Novels
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文报道了NASA删除的“First Woman”系列漫画小说虽被从官网移除，但仍可获取。这些漫画于2021年和2023年发布，旨在激励年轻女性加入“阿尔忒弥斯世代”。尽管2025年3月这些出版物被从NASA的互联网平台删除，但通过某些方式仍可下载。这些漫画通过虚拟现实和增强现实技术提供互动体验，讲述了第一位探索月球的女性Callie Rodriguez的故事，展示了NASA的月球探索技术。然而，相关视频和图片在文章发布后数小时内被撤下，引发对多样性和女性主题内容被清理的讨论。

Keith’s 23 March update:
within a few hours after this was posted (over a weekend) A NASA YouTube video and an official NASA photo of two female astronauts were pulled offline. Both things had been online for several years. This is not the first time this has happened. Apparently NASA DEI Sanitation Squad is using my postings to help them delete things. Details below
.
Keith’s 22 March note:
in 2021 NASA
issued
the first of two interactive comic books/graphic novels (
“First Woman: Dream to Reality”
) depicting young women dreaming of – and then training for – a future that would comprise the so-called “Artemis Generation.” NASA
issued a second novel
(
“First Woman: Expanding Our Universe”
) in November 2023. Yet, as of March 2025 NASA has moved all evidence of these two publications from their various internet platforms as part of the ongoing Federal Government purge of anything related to diversity or women etc. (see
“
NASA’s Ever-Changing Artemis Crew Tagline
‘)
. But these two publications are not totally gone. I found them – rather easily.
Here they are:
You can download
volume 1
(pdf) and
volume 2
(pdf) or click on the images below.
According to the second novel’s
press release
:
“This second issue of the graphic novel series features a diverse crew of astronauts on the Moon’s surface who learn and grow as a team, navigate the unexpected, and conduct experiments and technology demonstrations for the benefit of humanity.”
According to the first novel’s
press release
“NASA released its first digital, interactive graphic novel on Saturday in celebration of National Comic Book Day. “First Woman: NASA’s Promise for Humanity” imagines the story of Callie Rodriguez, the first woman to explore the Moon
.
The story of Callie captures how passion, dedication, and perseverance allow us to turn our dreams into reality,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Pam Melroy. “Callie, much like myself, grew her skills, seized learning opportunities, and overcame challenges to become a NASA astronaut. Her diversity is reflected in our own astronaut corps today – it’s important we can see ourselves as the explorers among the stars.”
“The 40-page comic book highlights NASA technologies for traveling to, landing on, and exploring the Moon. The digital format comes to life, letting readers engage and interact through augmented reality elements using the First Woman website or their mobile devices.”
Both graphic novels were give VR tags and (when NASA still had  things hooked up) provided some rather cool Augmented reality imagery that you could see on any cellphone or tablet. The
Android
and
iOS
Apps are still available but they point to links for these two graphic novels at NASA.gov which are now dead. You can listen to the audio version of the first novel
at SoundCloud
.
And this image below was
posted

showing two astronauts in space holding up a copy of the first novel which they read from.
“In this image from Jan. 12, 2024, NASA astronauts Jasmin Moghbeli (left) and Loral O’Hara pose with a copy of “First Woman”, NASA’s first graphic novel, inside the International Space Station’s cupola. Through Callie’s journey, “First Woman” features real-life technologies developed by NASA to enable future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. data.title: James Webb Space Telescope reveals that most galaxies rotate clockwise
data.author: instagraham
data.article_summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has observed that about two-thirds of 263 studied galaxies rotate clockwise, contrary to the expectation that galaxies should be evenly split in rotation direction. Lior Shamir's study in *Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society* highlights this asymmetry, noting it is evident in JWST's Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) images. One explanation could be that the universe itself is rotating, supporting black hole cosmology, where our universe exists within a black hole. Another possibility is that the Milky Way's rotation affects observations, with galaxies moving opposite to it appearing brighter due to the Doppler shift. This discovery may require recalibration of cosmic distance measurements and could impact understanding of the universe's expansion and galaxy formation. Further research is needed to confirm these findings.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于星系旋转方向的观测结果及其可能的解释，以及某研究者声称的宇宙各向异性问题。

不同观点：
• [nabla9] 认为该计算机科学家的多项研究基于不同数据集得出了相互矛盾的结论，且这些结论在后续被天文学家发现存在分析错误和统计测试不严谨的问题。独立研究并未发现显著的各向异性证据。此外，指出该研究者未对自己相互矛盾的结果进行反思，且研究样本量过小，未考虑相关因素如邻近星系的旋转相关性。
• [keyle] 提出一个假设性问题，即如果我们观察到的大多数星系朝某个方向旋转，是否意味着我们处于可观测宇宙的两个极之一。
• [over_bridge] 指出自然界中存在多种不平衡现象（如物质-反物质比例、左手性和右手性分子、星系旋转方向），暗示这些可能有更深层次的关联。
• [vincnetas] 强调星系的旋转方向是相对的，取决于观察者的位置，因此观察到的大多数星系朝某个方向旋转可能只是因为我们所处的位置所致。
• [misja111] 认为更可能的解释是我们对自己星系旋转的假设有误，这可以解释宇宙学中其他未解问题，如宇宙膨胀速率的差异。

补充讨论：
• [worldsayshi] 和 [like_any_other] 讨论了星系旋转方向的相对性以及多普勒效应是否会影响星系的亮度，并提出方向性或上下方向的问题。
• [mapt] 和 [_kst_] 质疑研究样本量过小，并指出应该有更多可见星系可以用于分析。此外，[mapt] 提到不同望远镜（如哈勃和JWST）观测结果的对比。
• [zurfer] 和 [alenrozac] 提出关于我们是否生活在黑洞内的假设性问题，并将宇宙膨胀与黑洞视界扩展相联系。

争议焦点：
• 某计算机科学家的研究结果及其相互矛盾的结论，研究方法的严谨性以及编辑评审过程的质量控制问题。
• 星系旋转方向的观察是否具有宇宙学上的深远意义，或者只是观察位置和样本量导致的统计现象。

这些讨论揭示了对星系旋转方向及其潜在宇宙学意义的多种视角和质疑。

43533306.article_content:
Spiral galaxies imaged by JWST that rotate in the same direction relative to the Milky Way (red) and in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way (blue). The number of galaxies rotating in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way as observed from Earth is far higher.
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
NASA’s
James Webb Space Telescope
(JWST) launched into orbit around the sun in December 2021. Since then, it has been studying the history of our universe. Now, images of deep space from JWST’s Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) have revealed something puzzling: most galaxies rotate in the same direction.
About two-thirds of the 263 galaxies studied in a
paper
published February 17 in the
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
rotate clockwise, while the other one-third rotate counterclockwise.
“The analysis of the galaxies was done by quantitative analysis of their shapes, but the difference is so obvious that any person looking at the image can see it,"
Lior Shamir
, a computer scientist from Kansas State University and sole author of the study, says in a
statement
. "There is no need for special skills or knowledge to see that the numbers are different. With the power of the James Webb Space Telescope, anyone can see it.”
The galaxies identified as rotating in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way.
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
The problem is that astronomers have long posited that galaxies should be evenly split between rotating in one direction or the other, astronomer
Dan Weisz
from the University of California, Berkeley, who was not involved with the study, wrote for
Astronomy
back in 2017. “This stems from the idea that we live in an ‘isotropic’ universe, which means that the universe looks roughly the same in every direction. By extension, galaxies shouldn’t have a preferred direction of spin from our perspective,” he added. According to Shamir, there are two strong potential explanations for this discrepancy.
One explanation is that the universe came into existence while in rotation. This theory would support what’s known as black hole cosmology: the hypothesis that our universe exists within a black hole that exists within another parent universe. In other words, black holes create universes within themselves, meaning that the black holes in our own universe also lead to other baby universes.
"A preferred axis in our universe, inherited by the axis of rotation of its parent black hole, might have influenced the rotation dynamics of galaxies, creating the observed clockwise-counterclockwise asymmetry,”
Nikodem Poplawski
, a theoretical physicist at the University of New Haven who was not involved in the study, tells
Space.com
’s Robert Lea. "The discovery by the JWST that galaxies rotate in a preferred direction would support the theory of black holes creating new universes, and I would be extremely excited if these findings are confirmed.”
The galaxies identified as rotating in the same direction relative to the Milky Way (counterclockwise).
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
Another possible explanation involves the Milky Way’s rotation. Due to an effect called the
Doppler shift
, astronomers expect galaxies rotating opposite to the Milky Way’s motion to appear brighter, which could explain their overrepresentation in telescopic surveys.
“If that is indeed the case, we will need to re-calibrate our distance measurements for the deep universe,” Shamir explains in the statement. "The re-calibration of distance measurements can also explain several other unsolved questions in cosmology such as the differences in the
expansion rates of the universe
and the
large galaxies
that according to the existing distance measurements are expected to be older than the universe itself.”
It remains to be seen whether further research will confirm black hole cosmology or that astronomers have been measuring the universe’s expansion incorrectly—or perhaps something else entirely.

data.title: 'Please leave feedback': how constant online reviews are changing our brains
data.author: sandebert
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了在线评分文化对人们心理和生活的影响。在现代社会中，我们不断被要求为各种服务和产品打分，从购买的商品到乘坐的出租车。虽然这些评分看似提供了有用的信息，但它们也引发了相互 surveillance（监视）的现象，改变了人们的互动方式。一些人因低评分而感到焦虑，甚至改变自己的行为以求获得更高评价。文章提到，这种文化可能导致人们变得更加自我意识，影响日常决策和人际关系。例如，Uber乘客Helen Plyconic因低评分而感到压力，每次乘车都担心被司机评判。心理专家Vic Paterson也指出，这种持续的评分文化可能对人们的心理健康产生负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对在线评价体系的信任与质疑

不同观点：
• FinnLobsien认为在线评价体系（如Airbnb、Google Maps）不再值得信任。他指出，由于系统内的各方都有动机提高评分，导致评分膨胀（Goodhart法则）。此外，他认为评价不具可替代性，即陌生人的评价不一定符合个人的偏好。他举例说明一些高质量的店铺因为特定政策（如不允许使用笔记本电脑或没有英文菜单）而得到低评分，而这些因素恰恰是某些顾客喜欢这些店铺的原因。FinnLobsien总结说，在线评分没有意义，他更倾向于通过本地新闻或Reddit获取推荐。

• RamblingCTO对FinnLobsien的观点表达了不满，特别是对“评价影响信任”的表述。RamblingCTO认为，所有我们接触和消费的信息都会改变我们的大脑，这种改变本身是中性的。他似乎在暗示，评价体系的影响是不可避免的，但并不一定是不好的。

补充讨论：
• FinnLobsien强调了评价体系中的激励机制如何导致评分膨胀，并举例说明了某些特定情况下的评价偏差。
• RamblingCTO则关注评价体系对消费者认知的影响，认为信息消费本身就是一个不断改变大脑的过程，而不一定是负面或不可信的。
• 争议的焦点在于在线评价体系的可信度及其对消费者决策的影响。FinnLobsien持怀疑态度，而RamblingCTO则认为这种影响是中性的和不可避免的。

‘If I don’t rate them, will they rate me badly?’
Composite: Guardian Design; posed by model; Maskot/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
‘If I don’t rate them, will they rate me badly?’
Composite: Guardian Design; posed by model; Maskot/Getty Images
Retail industry
‘Please leave feedback’: how constant online reviews are changing our brains – and our lives
We live under mutual surveillance, asked to leave public ratings for every purchase, meal, taxi ride or hair appointment. What is it doing to us?
Chloë Hamilton
Tue 1 Apr 2025 05.00 EDT
Last modified on Tue 1 Apr 2025 05.37 EDT
Share
‘A
lexlilly1999* has left you feedback!” pings the Vinted notification. My stomach flips as the app loads and I open my review: “Quite good.” A gut punch. I sit in shock, scrutinising the words in front of me. “Good” is a bit uninspired but “quite” feels both passive-aggressive and viciously spiteful:
quite
good. Alexlilly1999 has also given me just four stars. It’s a lukewarm write-up considering the dress I sold them was good quality, a brilliant price and shipped quickly. I glare at the review. And then another notification pops up: do I want to leave feedback for the buyer? Well, yes, actually, I do.
It’s likely we’ve all, at some stage, been asked to leave feedback online. Called your electricity provider with a query? Please answer a few quick questions about the service you received. Had something delivered by a courier? Please rate your experience. Often, the promise of prizes – from £200 worth of high street vouchers, to spa trips and luxury hampers – is dangled in exchange for our appraisals. We’re asked to judge the people who serve us coffee; drive us in taxis; cut our hair; extract our teeth. A friend of a friend was recently asked to leave feedback for an interview process just moments after the company had rejected them for the role.
The odd thing is, lots of us do leave feedback. Perhaps it has become normalised to mark, out of five, the toilet plunger we bought at 2am – or perhaps we’ve been influenced by “influencer culture”, in which everyone can (and does) have an opinion. Lots of us also, of course, like getting feedback, with positive ratings on platforms like Uber,
Airbnb
and Vinted becoming badges of honour.
View image in fullscreen
Does your new purchase cut the mustard?
Photograph: Posed by model; filadendron/Getty Images
According to a study by
Power Reviews
, 98% of consumers see reviews as an essential part of the decision-making process and 45% of users won’t buy a product if there aren’t any reviews. Ratings, it seems, have become so ubiquitous that an absence of them is an automatic red flag.
But while, on the face of it, authentic, real-world information about goods and services may seem helpful – necessary, even – one can’t help but wonder what this culture of mutual surveillance is doing to our brains – and our lives. If every decision is judged, often publicly, how long before it starts to change the way we interact?
For Helen Plyconic, it already has. The 45-year-old has a 4.12 (out of 5) rating on Uber – a ranking so low it can, reportedly, mean some Uber drivers refuse to pick you up (although the company itself says destination and fare are more likely to drive a driver’s decision to turn down a booking). The Walthamstow resident, who says she has never been rude or drunk in an Uber, believes her rating is low because she once missed a taxi when her phone ran out of battery after booking, and she jumped in a friend’s cab instead. While she concedes this was her fault, she has, since then, received consistently low ratings for reasons, she thinks, such as needing help with her bags (she had three children with her) and a driver having to change a pickup point due to closed roads. As a result, she has begun to alter her behaviour, tipping extra-generously and even explaining her predicament to drivers, all to no avail.
The Vinted phenomenon: how one woman sold her clothes – and created a billion-dollar company
Read more
A self-confessed people pleaser, Plyconic now feels anxious each time she takes an Uber. “Do I chat to show I’m friendly or be silent so as not to upset them?” she says. She describes, too, how drivers even tell her how lucky she is they picked her up, given her poor rating. “I then question why they did, and wonder if they are dodgy themselves.” (Riders, incidentally, can check their drivers’ ratings, meaning Plyconic could, if she wanted, refuse a driver if she deemed their rating too low. She would, however, incur a £5 cancellation fee.)
Anxiety specialist Vic Paterson – who, when we speak, is considering how best to review her dog walker – says she has noticed her clients struggling with this constant feedback culture. “While specific research on ubiquitous rating systems is still developing, therapists and psychologists – including me – are noticing recurring patterns,” she says. “Many clients [experience] increased self-consciousness during everyday interactions tha
43545057.article_summary: 文章探讨了在线评分文化对人们心理和生活的影响。在现代社会中，我们不断被要求为各种服务和产品打分，从购买的商品到乘坐的出租车。虽然这些评分看似提供了有用的信息，但它们也引发了相互 surveillance（监视）的现象，改变了人们的互动方式。一些人因低评分而感到焦虑，甚至改变自己的行为以求获得更高评价。文章提到，这种文化可能导致人们变得更加自我意识，影响日常决策和人际关系。例如，Uber乘客Helen Plyconic因低评分而感到压力，每次乘车都担心被司机评判。心理专家Vic Paterson也指出，这种持续的评分文化可能对人们的心理健康产生负面影响。

data.title: In the 1980s we downloaded games from the radio
data.author: spzb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在Facebook上看到一张1980年代家用电脑和卡带的照片，勾起了他对于1980年代通过广播下载视频游戏的回忆。当时，人们可以将广播中的音频录制到卡带中，然后在电脑上加载游戏。然而，评论中有人否认这种做法曾经存在。作者因此回顾了1980年代早期英国的背景，包括经济衰退、科技发展以及BBC的计算机扫盲项目。该项目通过电视和广播节目教育公众，其中广播节目《The Chip Shop》播放专门为多种家用电脑设计的BASICODE程序，听众可以录制并在自己的电脑上运行，尽管这些程序多为文本基础，而非图形游戏。这篇文章反映了科技发展的历史以及人们对过去事实的遗忘和质疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过无线电等传统方式传输软件的历史实践及其现代对比

不同观点：
• Coreyh14444和HarHarVeryFunny分享了在20世纪80年代通过杂志中的BASIC代码手动输入程序的经历，强调了这种方法的繁琐和易错性，但当时这是常见的软件分享方式。
• Joeboy认为这种通过无线电传输软件的方式在当时并不普遍，甚至可以说是“不存在的”，并将这种现象类比为现代的NFT纹身，认为其影响有限。然而，他在后续补充中承认对NFT纹身的了解不足。
• Ochrist提供了荷兰和丹麦之间通过BASICODE 2标准进行程序传输的实例，展示了当时不同计算机品牌之间实现软件兼容的具体方法。
• Danieldk提到了英国通过电视传输软件的例子，并指出BBS（电子公告板系统）在互联网前时代的作用，强调了多种软件分享途径的存在。
• Nunnez反驳否认这种无线电传输实践的观点，指出现代Wi-Fi和蜂窝网络的原理与当时无线传输并无本质区别。
• Bluedino分享了20世纪90年代在美国通过电视卡接收数据广播的经历，提到使用Intercast技术，但对其具体效果记忆模糊。

• Flohofwoe提供了Prof Dr Horst Völz关于东德无线电计算机节目的记录，强调了东西德计算机爱好者之间的合作。
• Buildsjets提到现代通过WAV文件从网站下载软件到Apple ][的实例，展示了这种传统方法的现代延续。
• CakeEngine和Lemonad分享了通过电视传输计算机程序的实例，分别提到了瑞典的公共广播电台和将光敏电阻（LDR）连接到电视屏幕的方法。
• Uneventual幽默地指出无线电传输软件在20世纪80年代短暂流行，随后被有线互联网取代，而现在大部分软件又通过无线方式下载。
• Theginger提到电视节目中的“数据突发”传输方式，通过VCR录制和回放静止帧中的计算机代码。
• Caseyy提到了CD Projekt Red创始人可能通过无线电传输将西方游戏走私到铁幕国家的传闻，尽管他认为这可能是都市传说。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到通过无线电、电视等传统媒介传输软件在20世纪80年代和90年代的实践，并通过具体实例和个人经历加以佐证。
• 争议的焦点在于这种传输方式的普遍性和实际影响，部分评论者认为其影响有限，而其他人则提供了具体的实例证明其可行性和实践性。
• 现代与历史的对比也是一个讨论重点，特别是在无线传输技术重新成为主流的今天，如何看待过去这些实践的价值和意义。

43510393.article_content:
So there I was, minding my own business, doom-scrolling my way through Facebook posts when I happened upon one that hit me straight in the nostalgia. A photo of a 1980s home computer, a cassette player and some tapes. The text underneath proclaimed "In the 1980s, people could download video games from radio broadcasts by recording the audio onto cassette tapes. These tapes could then be played on computers to load the games". I nodded sagely to myself as I remembered doing just that.
Then I started to read the comments underneath and people were flat-out denying that this had ever happened. The reply guys broadly fell into two camps: the "I have never heard of this, therefore it never happened" and the over confident "expert" saying things like "this would be technically impossible due to some fancy sounding words I've heard like 'hertz', 'compression' and 'frequency shift keying', therefore it never happened".
Just to make sure I was in a spluttering rage the page itself was titled "Unbelievable facts" as if my own childhood had become unbelievable. Although now I think about it it was an unbelievably long time ago, so maybe they have a point.
My youth is now an unbelievable fact, apparently
Anyway, come back with me to the UK in the early 1980s. Recession, strikes, unemployment and the first female Prime Minister, Margaret Thatcher, dominated the news. The home video cassette recorder was only just becoming common, the compact disc wouldn't be launched until the middle of the decade and mobile phone networks didn't even exist. Dexy's Midnight Runners, Irene Cara and Culture Club soundtracked the era and, across the land, the home computer boom was booming.
Computers were new, barely making their way even into the workplace. Most people in office jobs were using typewriters, carbon papers and the postal system. But the microprocessor revolution promised to make computer skills essential to the economy and so the British Broadcasting Corporation began a public education exercise :
The BBC Computer Literacy Project
.
The BBC's project is best remembered for the TV programmes fronted by
Ian McNaught Davis
and
Chris Serle
and, of course, the eponymous
BBC Micro
specially developed by Acorn to accompany the programmes. Less well known was a Radio 4 series called
The Chip Shop
. According to the ever reliable internet, it was presented by Barry Norman (much better known as a film critic than a technology expert) although I have no recollection of that.
Home computers at the time were a marvel of cost efficient engineering. Usually consisting of a chunky wedge-shaped keyboard with all the gadgetry inside, it used your normal home TV as a display and a normal portable cassette recorded as a data storage device. Software (which for most of us meant games) would be supplied on an audio cassette on which a series of piercing screeching noises were recorded. You'd hook up the cassette player to your computer, play the screeching noises into your computer through a cable of some description and after a few minutes your game would be loaded up and ready to play. Or, more often, you'd hear several minutes of screeching before the process died with a cryptic message like "R Tape Error" and you'd have to start again.
There were many different companies making these computers all competing for the nascent home market. And, with a few
notable exceptions
, they were all incompatible with each other and the screeching noises on cassette for, say, your ZX Spectrum would be of no use to the kid next door who had a Commodore 64. This presented a problem for Barry and his Chip Shop. The BBC wanted to broadcast software as part of the radio programme but they'd have to play a different set of screeching noises for each type of computer and their regular listeners would be subjected to twenty minutes of screeching noises at a time.
The solution lay over the water in The Netherlands. The Dutch public broadcaster NOS had encountered the same problem and had developed a system called
BASICODE
. Often described as a kind of "Computer Esperanto", it allowed the same software to run on different types of computer. You would order a cassette that had BASICODE interpreters for different machines, load up the one that matched your device and then that interpreter would load up the BASICODE program you'd recorded off your radio.
The BBC extended this system as BASICODE 2 (and later 2+) to include more functionality and support more brands of computer. And so was born The Chip Shop Takeaway. Late at night when anyone with any sense was asleep and not listening to their radio, the BBC would broadcast BASICODE programs for home computer enthusiasts to record and use on their machines. To call these "video games" would be a bit of a stretch as BASICODE didn't really support any kind of graphics but I certainly remember some very basic text-based games amongst a load of academic software which meant absolutely nothing to me as an eight year old bo

data.title: George Orwell and me: Richard Blair on life with his extraordinary father
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了乔治·奥威尔（George Orwell）的儿子理查德·布莱尔（Richard Blair）对父亲的回忆。理查德在出生三周后被奥威尔夫妇收养，九个月后，他的养母艾琳去世。尽管奥威尔因健康问题无法生育，但他一直渴望成为父亲，并亲自照顾理查德。理查德回忆起与父亲在苏格兰乡村的日子，称奥威尔是个全心全意投入的父亲。尽管奥威尔以反极权主义著作如《1984》和《动物农场》闻名，但他个人生活充满矛盾：他是个讲究茶道的人，但私生活较为放荡。理查德与奥威尔性格迥异，但他深深敬仰父亲，视自己为父亲精神的守护者。奥威尔去世时理查德年幼，但他一直感受到父亲的深厚爱意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于茶文化的具体做法以及对乔治·奥威尔作品的评价与理解

不同观点：
• 关于泡茶的方法，_joel引用了某种传统的英式泡茶方式，强调使用印度或锡兰（斯里兰卡）的茶叶，而不是中国茶叶。他还详细描述了泡茶的步骤，包括茶壶的使用、茶叶的用量、是否加牛奶和糖等细节。这种观点强调了泡茶的仪式感和特定步骤，体现了一种对传统英式茶文化的坚持。

• 另一种观点来自ilamont，虽然主要评论的是对乔治·奥威尔作品的理解，但也通过提及与家人的互动（与 teenager 一起观看电影《1984》）展现了对文化传承的不同视角。ilamont更关注奥威尔作品的文化影响，尤其是通过家庭视角（如与青少年一起看电影）来理解奥威尔的深刻意义。这种观点强调了文化体验的个人化和代际传承。

• ilamont的评论中提到了对奥威尔作品的不同形式（书籍与电影）的欣赏，特别是与年轻一代的分享，这表明了对经典文学作品跨代际吸引力的认可。

• 茶文化中的传统与创新的冲突，特别是关于特定步骤和材料的坚持（如不用中国茶，不加糖）与其他可能更为包容和多元的茶文化观点之间的对立。

George Orwell holding his son, Richard, in late 1946.
Photograph: Vernon Richards
View image in fullscreen
George Orwell holding his son, Richard, in late 1946.
Photograph: Vernon Richards
George Orwell
Interview
George Orwell and me: Richard Blair on life with his extraordinary father
Simon Hattenstone
The literary giant’s only child reflects on his father’s devotion in their days together in rural Scotland, his early death, his genius as a writer – and his reputation as a womaniser
Wed 19 Mar 2025 01.00 EDT
Last modified on Wed 19 Mar 2025 05.54 EDT
Share
R
ichard Blair didn’t have the easiest start in life. At three weeks old, he was adopted. Nine months later, his adoptive mother, Eileen, died at 39, after an allergic reaction to the anaesthetic she was given for a hysterectomy. Family and friends expected Blair’s father, Eric, to un-adopt him. Fortunately, Eric, better known as
George Orwell
, was an unusually hands-on dad for the 1940s.
Orwell and Eileen had wanted children for years, but he was sterile and it is likely that she was infertile as a result of uterine cancer. Having finally agreed to adopt after their struggle, Orwell was not going to give up on his son. “The thing he wanted most in life was to have children,” says Blair. “And now I was his family.”
We are in the kitchen of Blair’s home and he is making me a cuppa. On the kitchen wall is a framed poster of his father’s famous instructions for making tea. “Use tea from India or Ceylon (Sri Lanka), not China,” it starts. “Use a teapot, preferably ceramic. Warm the pot over direct heat. Tea should be strong, six spoons of leaves per litre. Let the leaves move around the pot. No bags or strainers. Take the pot to the boiling kettle. Stir or shake the pot. Drink out of a tall, mug-shaped teacup. Don’t add creamy milk. Add milk to the tea, not vice versa. No sugar!”
Orwell, perhaps the most influential writer of the 20th century, railed against totalitarianism in his dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four; chronicled it in his memoir about fighting in the Spanish civil war, Homage to Catalonia; and satirised it in his wonderful fable Animal Farm. Yet it has to be said his tea-making rules verge on the autocratic. Perhaps we shouldn’t be surprised. Orwell, who died at 46 in 1950, was a cauldron of contradictions – a single‑minded rebel so concerned about embarrassing his parents when writing about homelessness that he adopted a pen name; an Old Etonian man of the people; an introverted party animal; an egalitarian socialist and bigot; a man who railed against the “incorrigible dirtiness and untidiness” and the “terrible, devouring sexuality” of women, but who lived in filth and devoured as many women as possible.
View image in fullscreen
Richard Blair with a maquette of George Orwell
Photograph: Fabio De Paola/The Guardian
Blair apologises. No teapot, no leaves; he is making do with a teabag. “It is from Harrods, though!” He is 80 years old, just like Animal Farm. Blair hands me the tea in an orange-and-white mug designed like an old-fashioned Penguin book cover of Nineteen Eighty-Four. “Biscuits?” He gets out the chocolate digestives. On the table is a copy of today’s Daily Telegraph.
You couldn’t imagine two more different men. Orwell was a puritan radical; Blair is a “leftwing Conservative” who says he could never vote for Labour because he can’t bear the thought of singing The Red Flag. Orwell detested the privilege into which he was born and spent much of his life living in squalor; Blair lives a cosy, suburban life in a pretty, middle-class village near Leamington Spa in Warwickshire. Orwell was a police officer in Burma, now Myanmar; ran around with revolutionaries in Spain, where he got shot in the throat; lived on the streets in London; hung out in brothels in Paris; and retreated to the remote island of Jura towards the end of his life to write Nineteen Eighty-Four. Blair, meanwhile, started out as a farmer before training people to sell tractors, finally ending up as a landlord for holiday cottages in Craignish on the west coast of Scotland.
Yet Orwell has shaped his life. “My father was devoted to me,” he says. “Absolutely devoted.” And Blair is equally devoted to him. He regards himself as the keeper of the sacred flame for his father.
Blair, a broad man with caterpillar eyebrows and an establishment air, looks out over his large garden and says if he had been sensible he would have bought the plot of land next to their house; it would be worth a fortune now. On a shelf in the hallway, we pass a maquette of the Orwell sculpture that stands outside Broadcasting House in London. He is instantly recognisable – thin as a pipe cleaner, gangly (he was 6ft 2in, or 1.88 metres, tall), pencil moustache, waves of dark hair, fag in hand.
View image in fullscreen
‘My father was devoted to me’ … Blair with Orwell.
Photograph: Vernon Richards
Opposite is a mounted plaque featuring a slab of slate and an illustration of a white stone house. Underne
43498861.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了乔治·奥威尔（George Orwell）的儿子理查德·布莱尔（Richard Blair）对父亲的回忆。理查德在出生三周后被奥威尔夫妇收养，九个月后，他的养母艾琳去世。尽管奥威尔因健康问题无法生育，但他一直渴望成为父亲，并亲自照顾理查德。理查德回忆起与父亲在苏格兰乡村的日子，称奥威尔是个全心全意投入的父亲。尽管奥威尔以反极权主义著作如《1984》和《动物农场》闻名，但他个人生活充满矛盾：他是个讲究茶道的人，但私生活较为放荡。理查德与奥威尔性格迥异，但他深深敬仰父亲，视自己为父亲精神的守护者。奥威尔去世时理查德年幼，但他一直感受到父亲的深厚爱意。

data.title: Lapham's Quarterly Announces New Stewardship
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 《Lapham’s Quarterly》将由巴德学院及其Hannah Arendt人文中心接管，于2025年重新发布。该期刊由已故的Lewis H. Lapham于2007年创立，以其历史和文学思想而闻名。在巴德学院的指导下，期刊将与长期贡献者及文学界合作恢复出版。Lapham去世后，这一转变旨在延续其遗志和愿景。Hannah Arendt中心将管理期刊资产，并通过巴德监狱计划将期刊提供给在押读者。哥伦比亚大学也收购了Lapham的私人档案，Hawthornden基金会则将在其办公室设立永久纪念。此次合作确保期刊的持续发展，并扩展其思想和文学的可及性。

43530863.article_content:
Donate Now
L
apham’s Quarterly
, the celebrated journal of history and ideas founded by the late editor and journalist Lewis H. Lapham, will relaunch under the stewardship of Bard College and its Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities in 2025. With Bard College’s guidance, the
Quarterly
will resume publication with an editorial team that works closely with longtime contributors, supporters, and the broader literary community. Further details regarding the magazine’s relaunch, programming, and initiatives will be announced in the coming months.
The transition comes at a pivotal moment in the publication’s history, as staff, subscribers, and supporters mourn the loss of Lapham, who passed away in July 2024. This new chapter ensures that his vision and legacy will endure for generations to come.
Founded in 2007 by Lapham, the longtime editor of
Harper’s Magazine
,
Lapham’s Quarterly
has remained a beacon of historical and literary thought, drawing on the great writers of the past and vital voices of the present to illuminate our times. After a yearlong hiatus and restructuring, this partnership with Bard College marks a rare second chance for a literary journal—one that secures its future and reaffirms its place in the intellectual landscape.
T
he Hannah Arendt Center for Politics and Humanities, renowned for its interdisciplinary exploration of politics, culture, and the human condition, will adopt the
Quarterly’s
assets, including its archives, back issue inventory, media, and intellectual property. The Center plans to build upon Lewis H. Lapham’s legacy by integrating the journal into Bard’s broader mission of fostering critical inquiry and dialogue.
This transition not only ensures that
Lapham’s Quarterly
will continue to thrive but also represents a broader commitment to preserving intellectual legacies in an era when historical reflection is more important than ever.
“Lewis Lapham was a singular figure in American letters, and the
Quarterly
was a testament to his unyielding belief in the power of history to inform the present,” said Paul W. Morris, Publisher of
Lapham’s Quarterly
. “With its reputation for academic excellence and dedication to critical thinking, Bard College and the Hannah Arendt Center are the ideal custodians of this legacy. This collaboration is not only a lifeline but also a transformative opportunity to reimagine the
Quarterly’s
future while staying true to Lewis Lapham’s original vision.”
Before his passing last summer, Lewis endorsed the promise of this partnership and saw its obvious potential. Bard College will help realize Lapham’s longtime dream of distributing free copies of the
Quarterly
to incarcerated readers. Through the Bard Prison Initiative, one of the country’s most respected college-in-prison programs,
Lapham’s Quarterly
will be made available to incarcerated students in the program as a resource for intellectual engagement, historical education, and critical thinking. This initiative underscores the shared mission of both Bard College and the
Quarterly
to expand access to ideas and literature for all.
“Lewis’ monthly column first at
Harper’s
and then at
Lapham’s Quarterly
was at the center of my intellectual universe for nearly two decades,” said Roger Berkowitz, Founder and Academic Director of the Hannah Arendt Center. “His intellectual curiosity, his belief that history and the humanities illuminate and inform the present fully aligns with the mission at the Arendt Center and Bard College, to be an institutional space for bold and provocative humanities thinking about the public world. We are honored to continue his extraordinary work and look forward to shaping the future of
Lapham’s Quarterly
while remaining faithful to its founding ideals.”
I
n addition to Bard College’s new stewardship of
Lapham’s Quarterly
, Columbia University has acquired Lewis H. Lapham’s private archives for its Rare Book & Manuscript Library, further cementing his legacy among the great intellectuals, writers, and editors of his time. The acquisition includes his correspondence, annotated books, editorial notes, and unpublished writings, offering scholars a reservoir of insight into his life’s work.
Meanwhile, Hawthornden Foundation, a longtime champion of literary preservation, has also committed to honoring Lapham’s legacy with a permanent tribute at the
Quarterly’s
Union Square West office. This space will feature a full set of
Lapham’s Quarterly
journals, a commemorative plaque, and a display of Lapham’s typewriter and personal desk—artifacts imbued with his lifelong devotion to letters. Hawthornden’s archivist will catalog the
Quarterly’s
extensive library, creating specially designed bookplates that mark each volume as part of the journal’s institutional collection.
To learn more about how to support this partnership with a tax-deductible financial gift, please visit
this online donation page
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟如何通过反强制工具（ACI）应对经济胁迫，尤其是针对科技巨头如Meta、Google、Microsoft等公司，以及可能产生的经济和贸易后果。

不同观点：
• [theGeatZhopa] 认为欧盟的反强制工具（ACI）可能会被激活，尤其是在Meta等公司面临被禁的风险时。他指出，Facebook不重要，Instagram和WhatsApp虽然有一定重要性，但爱国情绪可能使得放弃这些应用变得容易。他认为，对于Google和Microsoft这样的公司，情况则不同。他还提到，欧盟可能采取更严格的措施，如对美国科技公司征收25%的税收，并禁止数据传输到美国，这可能会反过来影响美国公司。

• [theGeatZhopa] 进一步提到，美国对进口产品实施的25%关税也可能被视为胁迫行为，从而触发欧盟的反强制工具（ACI）。他认为，这可能会对NASDAQ和S&P500产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• [impish9208] 提供了一个链接，指向《华尔街日报》关于Meta在欧盟裁决的文章，这可能与讨论相关，提供了更多背景信息和细节。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于欧盟反强制工具（ACI）的适用范围和可能的后果，尤其是对大型科技公司的影响。一方面认为这些公司可以被轻易替代，另一方面则认为这些公司对经济和贸易的重要性不可忽视。

• 另一个争议点是美国和欧盟之间的关税和数据传输问题，这可能导致双方的经济摩擦和报复性措施。

data.author: mailyk
data.article_summary: 《诺贝尔对决》讲述了科学家安德鲁·沙利（Andrew Schally）和罗杰·吉耶曼（Roger Guillemin）之间激烈的竞争，以及他们发现下丘脑肽类激素的过程，最终两人共享了1977年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。文章指出，诺贝尔奖作为科学界最高荣誉，激发了科学家们的强烈竞争，甚至可能改变科学发现的历史进程。下丘脑通过释放激素调控垂体，进而影响生长、代谢、繁殖和应激反应等重要生理过程。吉耶曼和沙利在研究下丘脑与垂体的沟通机制时展开了长达数十年的对决，反映了科学界在荣誉和压力下的激烈竞争。文章提醒人们关注科研中竞争压力对科学进程的复杂影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：诺贝尔奖得主Schally和Guillemin之间的学术竞争及其避免的可能性

不同观点：
• Metacelsus认为Schally和Guillemin之间的竞争并非不可避免。他认为，尽管当时科学环境中的竞争氛围是导致对抗的必要条件，但真正驱动竞争的是两人的人格特质和沟通方式。如果他们在早期能通过坦诚对话达成合作或划分研究领域，竞争本可以避免。

• 另一种隐含的观点是，科学界普遍存在竞争，但并非所有科学家都会产生激烈争端。Metacelsus指出，其他内分泌学家并没有发生大规模争执，暗示了人际互动和个性在竞争激化中的重要作用。

补充讨论：
• Metacelsus以自身经历为例，说明他花费近三年时间撰写相关评论，期间深入研究了包括1960年代肽纯化方法在内的多个科学细节，显示了该历史事件的复杂性。

• 评论中还提到现代科学竞争中的沟通问题，建议在感知到不公或未被认同时，主动沟通以防止矛盾升级，而不是通过负面信件或电子邮件相互攻击。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于学术竞争是否不可避免。Metacelsus认为通过有效沟通和合作可以避免竞争激化，但现实中科学家能否放下个人成见进行合作仍是一个开放性问题。

What would you give for a Nobel Prize?
For more than a century, the Nobel has been science’s highest honor. The prize is awarded to only a few researchers per year for achievements in physics, chemistry, and “physiology or medicine.”
1
Nobel laureates hold immense prestige and wield influence not only within their fields but also within the broader public sphere. Nearly every scientist, at some point in their career, dreams of winning a Nobel, even if just as an overconfident undergraduate student. But for some, the prize is more than merely a dream: it’s an obsession.
Published in 1981, Nicholas Wade’s
The Nobel Duel
recounts how endocrinologists
Andrew Schally
and
Roger Guillemin
discovered peptide hormones produced by the hypothalamus, earning each of them a 1/4 share of the
1977 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
.
2
But more than this, Wade’s book details an intensely bitter rivalry, shaped not only by the personalities of the characters involved but by the incentives of the system in which they worked. More than forty years later,
The Nobel Duel
remains a valuable cautionary tale about the competitive pressures that shape scientific discoveries.
Hypothetical Hormones
Before diving into Schally and Guillemin, it’s helpful to learn a bit about the hypothalamus, the subject of their scientific struggles. The hypothalamus is a small lump of brain tissue, about the size of a hazelnut, that sits about seven centimeters behind the nose.
3
Despite its small size, the hypothalamus serves an important role as a regulatory center for hormonal signaling. It controls the pituitary gland, for example, another small tissue nodule located directly underneath it. The hypothalamus responds to nerve signals from the brain and stimulates the pituitary to release hormones that act on the rest of the body. This pathway controls a wide variety of critical processes, including
growth
,
metabolism
,
reproduction
, and
stress response
. The hypothalamus
plays an integral role in reproductive biology
, too, controlling everything from the production of sex hormones to ovulation and the menstrual cycle.
The hypothalamus sits deep in the brain, right next to the pituitary glands. Credit:
OpenStax
In rabbits, where ovulation is triggered by sexual intercourse, the hypothalamus converts the neural signal (female orgasm) into a hormonal signal (luteinizing hormone release by the pituitary) causing the ovaries to release eggs. This was discovered in a set of groundbreaking experiments in the 1930s,
4
but the mechanism remained unclear for decades. How, exactly, does the hypothalamus communicate between the brain and the pituitary?
An obvious hypothesis would be that the hypothalamus controls the pituitary via nerve signals. However, although the hypothalamus sits immediately adjacent to the pituitary, anatomists were unable to identify any nerves that could plausibly be responsible.
5
In the 1940s and 50s, the English physiologist Geoffrey Harris
conducted a set of experiments to test an alternative hypothesis
: namely, that a small molecule, rather than a physical neural connection, might be responsible.
Working in rats, Harris carefully severed a set of tiny blood vessels connecting the hypothalamus and pituitary and showed that the rats stopped reproducing. Harris proposed that the hypothalamus sends its own hormones through these blood vessels, triggering the pituitary to release its own set of hormones. But until such hormones could be directly identified, many scientists met this idea with skepticism. In order to explain the regulation of all the different hormones of the anterior pituitary, Harris had to hypothesize not just one hypothalamic hormone, but
a whole set of them
. And after all, Occam’s Razor states that “
entities are not to be multiplied without necessity
.” Even for Harris, this hypothesis was a leap into the unknown.

Subscribe
Stress and Strife
Roger Guillemin and Andrew Schally were no strangers to stress, even early in their lives. And in an ironic coincidence, it was stress itself that sparked their acrimonious race to discover the hormones of the hypothalamus.
Guillemin, born in 1924, grew up in the French town of Dijon. The Nazi occupation interrupted his medical studies, but after the war, he found a position in Montreal, where he completed his PhD under professor
Hans Sel

data.title: Systems Correctness Practices at AWS: Leveraging Formal and Semi-Formal Methods
data.author: yarapavan
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了AWS如何利用形式化及半形式化方法确保系统正确性，以提供高可靠性服务。AWS主要使用TLA+语言进行形式化验证，帮助在开发早期发现并修复潜在错误，同时支持性能优化。然而，由于TLA+学习曲线陡峭，AWS引入了更易用的P编程语言，用于建模和验证分布式系统。P语言已在多个AWS核心产品中应用，如S3存储服务的强一致性迁移。此外，AWS开发了PObserve工具，用于在测试和生产环境中验证分布式系统的正确性。这种系统化的正确性实践显著提升了开发效率，并确保服务的高可靠性和成本效益。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS的正式验证和结构化文档系统的实用性及其实际应用

不同观点：
• **jlcases的观点**：认为AWS的方法与技术文档的需求相似，强调复杂系统不仅需要正式验证，还需遵循MECE原则的结构化文档。他分享了实施层次化文档系统的经验，指出这种方法能提高AI助手生成代码的准确性，并提出正式验证工具与结构化文档互为补充。

• **gqgs的观点**：关注正式验证系统的准确性确认问题，认为验证工具本身的可靠性是一个潜在的无法解决的问题，这可能导致系统中仍然存在错误。虽然这不使正式验证不切实际，但需要注意常被忽略的 caveats。

• **pera的观点**：对TLA+和PlusCal的学习难度提出疑问，希望有经验的人能提供一个在TLA+中难以表达而在P中更容易表达的例子，以比较两者的易用性。

• **csbartus的观点**：分享了使用形式化方法创建软件的经验，包括使用ologs、FSMs和XState等工具，并提到实现“图即是代码”愿景的可能性。

• **neuroelectron的观点**：认为csbartus的评论是一个愚人节玩笑，暗示其不真实或夸张。

• **OhMeadhbh的观点**：质疑正式证明在AWS的实际应用，认为AWS的招聘实践更注重算法和数据结构的掌握，而非正式证明。虽然承认正式证明的研究价值，但怀疑其对AWS系统或流程的影响。

• **nullorempty的观点**：质疑哪些团队实际使用这些方法，要求具体说明。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于正式验证系统的实用性和准确性，特别是验证工具本身的可靠性。
• 对TLA+和P的易用性存在疑问，希望通过具体例子进行比较。
• 对AWS中正式证明的实际应用持怀疑态度，认为其可能仅限于研究的范畴，而非广泛应用于实际系统中。
• 对使用形式化方法创建软件的实际案例和愿景的讨论。

Past Issues
Topics
February 4, 2025
Volume 22, issue 6
PDF
Systems Correctness Practices at AWS
Leveraging Formal and Semi-formal Methods
Marc Brooker and Ankush Desai
AWS (Amazon Web Services) strives to deliver reliable services that customers can trust completely. This demands maintaining the highest standards of security, durability, integrity, and availability—with systems correctness serving as the cornerstone for achieving these priorities. An April 2015 paper published in
Communications of the ACM
, titled "How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods," highlighted the approach for ensuring the correctness of critical services that have since become among the most widely used by AWS customers.
21
Central to this approach was TLA+,
14
a formal specification language developed by Leslie Lamport. Our experience at AWS with TLA+ revealed two significant advantages of applying formal methods in practice. First, we could identify and eliminate subtle bugs early in development—bugs that would have eluded traditional approaches like testing. Second, we gained the deep understanding and confidence needed to implement aggressive performance optimizations while maintaining systems correctness.
Moreover, 15 years ago, AWS's software testing practice relied primarily on build-time unit testing, often against mocks, and limited deployment-time integration testing. Since then, we have significantly evolved our correctness practices, integrating both formal and semi-formal approaches into the development process. As AWS has grown, formal methods have become increasingly valuable—not only for ensuring correctness but also for performance improvements, particularly in verifying the correctness of both low- and high-level optimizations. This systematic approach toward systems correctness has become a force multiplier at AWS's scale, enabling faster development cycles through improved developer velocity while delivering more cost-effective services to customers.
This article surveys the portfolio of formal methods used across AWS to deliver complex services with high confidence in its correctness. We consider an umbrella definition of formal methods that encompasses these rigorous techniques—from traditional formal approaches such as theorem proving,
7,10
deductive verification,
18
and model checking
8,14
to more lightweight semi-formal approaches such as property-based testing,
6,19
fuzzing,
9
and runtime monitoring.
11
The P Programming Language
As the use of formal methods was expanded beyond the initial teams at AWS in the early 2010s, we discovered that many engineers struggled to learn and become productive with TLA+. This difficulty seemed to stem from TLA+'s defining feature: It is a high-level, abstract language that more closely resembles mathematics than the imperative programming languages most developers are familiar with. While this mathematical nature is a significant strength of TLA+, and we continue to agree with Lamport's views on the benefits of mathematical thinking,
15
we also sought a language that would allow us to model check (and later prove) key aspects of systems designs while being more approachable to programmers.
We found this balance in the P programming language.
8
P is a state-machine-based language for modeling and analysis of distributed systems. Using P, developers model their system designs as communicating state machines, a mental model familiar to Amazon's developer population, most of whom develop systems based on microservices and SOAs (service-oriented architectures). P has been developed at AWS since 2019 and is maintained as a strategic open-source project.
22
Teams across AWS that build some of its flagship products—from storage (e.g., Amazon S3, EBS), to databases (e.g., Amazon DynamoDB, MemoryDB, Aurora), to compute (e.g., EC2, IoT)—have been using P to reason about the correctness of their system designs.
For example, P was used in migrating S3 (Simple Storage Service) from eventual to strong read-after-write consistency.
1
A key component of S3 is its index subsystem, an object metadata store that enables fast data lookups. To achieve strong consistency, the S3 team had to make several nontrivial changes to the S3 index protocol stack.
25
Because these changes were difficult to get right at S3 scale, and the team wanted to deliver strong consistency with high confidence in correctness, they used P to formally model and validate the protocol design. P helped eliminate several design-level bugs early in the development process and allowed the team to deliver risky optimizations with confidence, as they could be validated using model checking.
In 2023, the P team at AWS built PObserve, which provides a new tool for validating the correctness of distributed systems both during testing and in production. With PObserve, we take structured logs from the execution of distributed systems and validate post-hoc that they match behaviors allowed by the formal P specific

data.title: Globe Gores
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了地理与地图部门收藏的各类印刷地球仪瓣（globe gores），这些瓣状地图从16世纪到20世纪不等，用于制作地球或天球的模型。地球仪瓣是预制的构建模块，可以快速用于组装地球仪，节省绘制地图的时间。文章追溯了地球仪制作的历史，提到公元前3世纪希腊人的地球知识，以及150 B.C.希腊学者Cratus of Mallus制作的已知最早地球仪。15世纪德国学者Martin Behaim制作了现存最古老的地球仪，而Martin Waldseemüller在1507年制作了首批印刷地球仪瓣，这一年美国首次出现在地图上。16世纪的德国学者Johann Schöner首次将印刷的天球和地球仪瓣配对使用。16世纪的佛兰德地图学家Gerard Mercator改进了木刻技术，使用铜版雕刻制作更精细的地球仪瓣，并添加了赤道坐标和黄道线。其后，Jodocus Hondius继承了Mercator的工作。17世纪的威尼斯地图学家Vincenzo Maria Coronelli为法国国王制作了当时最大的地球仪，并以缩小版形式复制。

43546607.article_content:
The Geography and Map Division holds a variety of printed globe gores in a variety of sizes and configurations ranging from some of the earliest examples in the 16
th
century to more modern examples in the 20
th
century.  Globe gores are strips of paper containing printed maps in the sizes and shapes needed for globe construction. The maps can be either terrestrial (showing the earth) or celestial (showing the heavens) and the gores are typically football shaped.  The gores can be thought of as pre-assembled building blocks for a globe of a particular size which a globe-maker can quickly utilize to construct a globe without having to spend the time constructing the maps.  The printed gores would be cut out of the printed sheet(s) and pasted onto a sphere of appropriate size to construct a globe.
As far back as the third century B.C. written records about globe construction by the ancient Greeks show knowledge of a round earth.  Greek grammarian and stoic philosopher Cratus of Mallus (ancient city in current day Türkiye) is known for constructing the earliest known globe of the earth around 150 B.C.  The 1492
Erdapfel
by 15
th
century German polymath Martin Behaim is the oldest surviving terrestrial globe, which was manually constructed from painted on globe gores and later inscribed with over 2,000 place names by a team of artists and scribes.  Another German cartographer by the name of Martin Waldseemüller created what are thought to be the first set of printed globe gores in 1507.  Coincidentally, this globe gore map along with his
wall map
also created in 1507 were also where the name
America
first appears on a map.  Below is an 1879 facsimile of the Waldseemüller globe gores
.
Section from:
Waldseemüller, Martin, Erster gedruckter Globus, Martin Hylacomylus (Waltzemüller)
, 1879, Geography and Map Division.
The cleric and printer Johann Schöner was another German who played an important role in the history of globe gores.  He was the first to bring printed terrestrial and celestial globes together as a matched pair starting in 1515.   Below is an
example of celestial globe gores
by Schöner from 1517.
Schöner, Johann, [Celestial globe gores]
, 1517, Geography and Map Division.
The 16
th
century Flemish cartographer Gerard Mercator’s terrestrial and celestial globe gores created between 1541-1551 improved upon Johann Schöner’s and Martin Waldseemüller woodcut engraving technique with copper engraved plates for his gores and also added equatorial coordinates and an ecliptic (path of the sun in its apparent orbit around the Earth) line that are now common features of modern terrestrial globe gores.  The copper engraving technique allowed for greater detail than woodcut and the metal plates could be updated with new geographic information. A new edition of globe gores made from a woodcut would need to be entirely re-sculpted from scratch.  The technical additions of features like the ecliptic line made the finished terrestrial globe more useful, especially with its celestial pair which also included this line.
Another Flemish cartographer and engraver by the name of Jodocus Hondius was a contemporary of Mercator.  He purchased Mercator’s
Atlas
map plates in 1604 and republished and sold a prolific number of updated copies.
Hondius, Jodocus, [Terrestrial globe gores],
1615, Geography and Map Division.
Hondius’ terrestrial 1615 globe gores shown above depict the Mercator-influenced features such as the ecliptic line and equatorial coordinates.  The prime meridian on this map appears to be Ferro (Canary Islands), which was common for this time period.
My favorite globe gore maker is 17
th

43546607.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了地理与地图部门收藏的各类印刷地球仪瓣（globe gores），这些瓣状地图从16世纪到20世纪不等，用于制作地球或天球的模型。地球仪瓣是预制的构建模块，可以快速用于组装地球仪，节省绘制地图的时间。文章追溯了地球仪制作的历史，提到公元前3世纪希腊人的地球知识，以及150 B.C.希腊学者Cratus of Mallus制作的已知最早地球仪。15世纪德国学者Martin Behaim制作了现存最古老的地球仪，而Martin Waldseemüller在1507年制作了首批印刷地球仪瓣，这一年美国首次出现在地图上。16世纪的德国学者Johann Schöner首次将印刷的天球和地球仪瓣配对使用。16世纪的佛兰德地图学家Gerard Mercator改进了木刻技术，使用铜版雕刻制作更精细的地球仪瓣，并添加了赤道坐标和黄道线。其后，Jodocus Hondius继承了Mercator的工作。17世纪的威尼斯地图学家Vincenzo Maria Coronelli为法国国王制作了当时最大的地球仪，并以缩小版形式复制。

Bletchley code breaker Betty Webb dies aged 101
3 hours ago

Share
